Zero-order convergence and a one-sided gradient estimate then produce uniform strict concavity after a transient period; this concavity supplies the damping needed for derivative decay. The same damping mechanism extends to the full ultraparabolic perturbation equation, allowing us to close the nonlinear stability estimates.

papers.title: The Maximum Commute Time of Regular Graphs
papers.abstract: For a connected simple regular graph $G$, let $τ(G)$ be the maximum commute time for simple random walk, and let $t_n$ be the maximum of $τ(G)$ over all such graphs of order $n$. Aldous and Fill conjectured that $t_n\sim3n^2/2$. We determine $t_n$ exactly and classify all maximizers for every even $n\geq10$ and every odd $n\geq15$; both thresholds are best possible. The maximizers are cubic block chains joined by bridges at even orders and quartic block chains joined at cut vertices at odd orders. The exact formulas specify the linear corrections according to the order modulo four and five, respectively, and imply $ t_n\sim \begin{cases} \dfrac32 n^2, & n\text{ even},\\[1mm] n^2, & n\text{ odd}, \end{cases} \qquad n\to\infty. $ Thus the conjectured asymptotic formula holds along even orders but fails along odd orders. The proof combines unit-current potential orderings, cut-current inequalities, and sharp block resistance bounds, supplemented by finite computations in exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Orders in the Euclidean Court
papers.abstract: Following Johnson, Queen, and Sevilla, we call an order $\mathcal{O}$ in a number field $K$ \textsf{generalized Euclidean} if for all $α,β\in \mathcal{O}$ with $β\ne 0$ for which $α\mathcal{O}+β\mathcal{O}$ is a principal ideal of $\mathcal{O}$, there are $γ, ρ\in \mathcal{O}$ with $α=βγ+ ρ$ and $|N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(ρ)| < |N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(β)|$. We prove that only finitely many quadratic orders are generalized Euclidean. Additionally, assuming GRH, we show that for each fixed $d > 1$ there are only finitely many integers $m$ for which $T^d-m$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{Z}[m^{1/d}] = \mathbb{Z}[T]/(T^d-m)$ is generalized Euclidean. When $d$ is even, we can remove the assumption of GRH.

papers.title: Perturbation theory for quantum information quantities of Gaussian states
papers.abstract: Many quantum-information tasks can benefit from Gaussian quantum resources, while their fundamental performance limits are characterized by quantum information quantities. However, a unified perturbation theory for these quantities directly within the Gaussian-state formalism has been lacking. We develop such a theory for the von Neumann entropy, quantum relative entropy, quantum Chernoff quantity, and quantum fidelity, using perturbations of the moments of a reference Gaussian state. Using general Fréchet-derivative identities, we derive compact second-order expressions for reference-state covariance matrices whose symplectic eigenvalues are all greater than $1/2$. We also show that the perturbative quantum Chernoff quantity is maximized at its symmetric point, yielding the quantum Chernoff exponent (QCE). We further show that symplectic eigenvalues equal to 1/2 can lead to slower asymptotic vanishing, potentially improving the corresponding fundamental performance limits. For reference-state covariance matrices containing symplectic eigenvalues both equal to and greater than 1/2, we identify sufficient conditions under which the former determine the leading covariance-matrix contributions, allowing the remaining modes to be traced out without changing the leading-order asymptotic scaling or the coefficient. Applying the framework to quantum illumination and incoherent-light sub-Rayleigh object discrimination, we recover known asymptotic QCEs directly within the Gaussian-state formalism. In the latter problem, the slower asymptotic vanishing explains the known quadratic scaling of the QCE with the source separation.

papers.title: Asymptotic low slopes of toric exponential sums
papers.abstract: Let $Δ$ be an integral Newton polytope containing the origin. We prove that the generic Newton slopes corresponding to Hodge slopes strictly smaller than one differ from their Hodge values by $O_Δ(p^{-1})$. No hypothesis is imposed on the semigroup generated by the lattice points of $Δ$. The proof combines an auxiliary prime and the Cartier operator to show that a coefficient of each required Dwork principal minor is nonzero. When the origin is interior to $Δ$, duality gives the same estimate for the corresponding high slopes and, in dimension two, for all slopes.

papers.title: Computation of Free Boundary Minimal Tori via Extremal Steklov Eigenvalues
papers.abstract: Fraser and Schoen showed that the first Steklov eigenfunctions of a metric maximizing the length-normalized first eigenvalue of a surface with boundary define a free boundary minimal immersion into a Euclidean ball. We develop a method for this extremal problem on surfaces of genus one with $b$ boundary components and use it to compute free boundary minimal tori for $b \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8\}$. By uniformization, the problem is a nonsmooth maximization over the modulus of a flat torus, the centers and radii of $b$ removed disks, and a boundary weight. The eigenvalues are computed with doubly periodic layer potentials, all derivatives follow from a single formula for the underlying pencil of boundary integral operators, and the coalescence of eigenvalues at a maximizer is handled by a two-stage nonsmooth method. The Lagrange multiplier matrix that certifies first-order stationarity rescales the eigenfunctions into the free boundary minimal immersion. For $b=1$, the supremum is the Fraser--Schoen bound $4π$, attained by branched double covers of the disk; the embedded torus with connected boundary of Carlotto, Franz, and Schulz is a saddle point, which answers their question whether it maximizes the eigenvalue in the negative. For $b \geq 2$ the largest values correspond to free boundary minimal tori in \mathbb{B}^5 and \mathbb{B}^6; the surfaces of Folha, Pacard, and Zolotareva, two disks joined by a central neck and $b$ equatorial necks, are maximizers within their symmetry class but saddle points of the full problem, with values increasing toward $4π$ as $b \to \infty$.

papers.title: Self-Similar Solutions of the 2D Incompressible Euler Equations via a Lagrangian Construction
papers.abstract: We give a Lagrangian construction of forward self-similar solutions of the $2$D incompressible Euler equation. For every $1<α<2$ and every real $h\in L^{2/α}(\mathbb{S}^1)$, the construction produces a flow with initial vorticity $|x|^{-α}h(\arg x)$, without smallness or sign assumptions. The argument is based on a fixed-point formulation of backward particle transport from time $t=1$ to $t=0$. Mollifying the Biot--Savart velocity in self-similar variables preserves exact vorticity transport, while symmetrization yields the unforced Euler equation in velocity form even when the ordinary vorticity flux is not locally integrable. The limiting solution admits an almost-everywhere invertible, measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flow from time zero, with strong local continuity and preservation of signed value distributions and absolutely integrable Casimirs.

papers.title: Convergence of alternating score-system iterations for regularized Landau particle dynamics
papers.abstract: We analyze an alternating iteration for score-based particle approximations of the homogeneous Landau equation. Each step computes a regularized score along the previous trajectory and recomputes the trajectory with that score frozen. First, at fixed positive regularization, we prove existence, uniqueness, and $W_1$-Lipschitz stability of a Tikhonov score minimizer in a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space embedded in $C_b^2$. For bounded Lipschitz collision matrices, this yields factorial convergence to the coupled regularized dynamics on every finite interval, with constants independent of particle number. Global objective gaps and system residuals control inexact solves, and structural kernel assumptions ensure momentum and energy conservation. The mean-field and alternating-iteration limits commute at fixed regularization in this regime. Second, score-difference cancellation extends the theory to far-field-truncated Landau kernels with $γ\geq -2$ and the uncut case $γ=-2$. For the uncut three-dimensional Coulomb kernel, a separate continuum construction gives local factorial convergence from bounded, compactly supported densities. Third, we characterize the obstruction to removing regularization at fixed particle number and establish a separate conditional density-level convergence criterion under uniform regularity and approximation assumptions, using relative entropy. A heat-equation counterexample shows that an unregularized density-level Picard iteration can diverge. Atomic Coulomb and simultaneous particle-zero-regularization limits remain open.

papers.title: Free abelian group actions on projective fibered varieties
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional normal projective variety of Kodaira dimension $κ$ and $G$ an abelian subgroup of automorphisms such that all elements of $G\backslash \{\mathrm{id}\}$ are of positive entropy. Dinh and Sibony showed that $G$ is actually free abelian of rank $\le n-κ-1$. In this paper, we show that after replacing $G$ by a finite-index subgroup, there exists a G-Equivariant Minimal Model Program for the pair $(X, G)$ when $\mathrm{rank}(G)=n-κ-1$ and $κ>0$, and the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a $Q$-abelian variety provided that the termination of flips holds in this setting.

papers.title: A Fourier expansion principle for coherent cohomology of powers of Tate curves
papers.abstract: In the case of the totally degenerate split degenerations given by fibered powers of Tate curves over $\mathbf{Z}[[q^{1/w}]]$, this article proves a Fourier expansion principle that applies to higher coherent (equivariant) cohomology classes of rigidified line bundles on the $\mathbf{Z}((q^{1/w}))$-fiber. We do not require any ampleness hypotheses. This generalizes a previous Fourier expansion principle due to Faltings--Chai that applies only to sections of ample line bundles; that version was used as a key step in their proof of their classification of polarized degenerations and thus in the construction of toroidal compactifications of moduli spaces of polarized abelian varieties. This article can be considered as a theory of Fourier expansions for algebraic theta cocycles associated to possibly indefinite quadratic forms, and has application to arithmetic: in joint work with Venkatesh, we have used it to produce an algebraic theory of Kudla--Millson indefinite modular theta functions.

papers.title: Lusztig's asymptotic algebra and a cell factorisation for the second lowest two-sided cell in type $\tilde{B}_n$
papers.abstract: We determine Lusztig's asymptotic algebra for the second lowest two-sided cell~$Δ_1$ in the equal parameter extended affine Weyl group $\tilde{\mathsf{B}}_n$ for all $n\geq 2$, realising it as a full matrix algebra over the representation ring of $\mathsf{Sp}_{2n-2}(\CC)\times C_2$ with $C_2$ the group of order~$2$. Our result is an explicit isomorphism of based rings, determining the image of each basis element $\mathsf{t}_w$ of the asymptotic algebra. As a consequence we verify that Lusztig's original conjecture from 1989 on the structure of the asymptotic algebra holds for this cell. A key ingredient in our proof is a refinement of Shi's description of~$Δ_1$, giving an explicit parametrisation of the elements of this cell (a \textit{cell factorisation}). This cell factorisation simultaneously describes all intersections of left and right cells, with uniqueness and length-additivity of expressions. Applications include a classification of the involutions in $Δ_1$, and a calculation of the length generating functions for $Δ_1$ and the right cells in~$Δ_1$.

papers.title: Jumps and Iterated Jumps of Perfect Subtrees of Positive Trees
papers.abstract: An infinite (binary) tree is \emph{positive} iff its set of paths is non-null. As an elementary observation, positives trees always have positive perfect subtrees. Given a positive tree of certain complexity, here we present several theorems concerning the distribution of the Turing jumps or iterated Turing jumps of (positive) perfect subtrees of the given tree in the universe of Turing degrees.

papers.title: Hadamard Transforms for Dimension Reduction
papers.abstract: Using the Hadamard matrix for dimension reduction can accelerate the computation due to the fast Hadamard transform. However, the previous target dimension bounds in terms of the Gaussian width depend on the ambient dimension. In this paper, we obtain the following ambient dimension free bound using three Hadamard-diagonal blocks. Let $H\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be the normalized Walsh-Hadamard matrix, and let $D_1,D_2,D_3\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be independent Rademacher diagonal matrices. We prove that for any symmetric set $T\subset \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, \[ \mathbb P\left\{\sup_{\boldsymbol t\in T}\big|\frac dm\|P_ΩHD_3HD_2HD_1\boldsymbol t\|_2^2-1\big|\le\varepsilon\right\} \ge1-δ\] whenever \[ m\gtrsim\varepsilon^{-2}w(T)^2\log^2\frac eδ\,\log^4\!\left(e+\frac{w(T)}\varepsilon\log\frac eδ\right). \] Here $w(T)$ is the Gaussian width of $T$, and $Ω$ is a set of $m$ distinct coordinates chosen uniformly. This is the first ambient dimension free bound on the target dimension using Hadamard transforms, for an arbitrary symmetric set in terms of its Gaussian width. We also prove that it is impossible to obtain an ambient dimension free bound for an arbitrary set in terms of its Gaussian width using two Hadamard-diagonal blocks.

papers.title: Noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for convolution operators under $L_1$-Hörmander conditions
papers.abstract: We prove weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for families of scalar convolution operators acting on operator-valued function spaces. A joint $L_1$-Hörmander condition, together with a maximal strong type estimate at one exponent $1<r\leq\infty$, suffices. The kernels may be complex-valued and need not have uniformly bounded $L_1$ norms. Under a size condition, the result also yields a weak endpoint estimate for all sharp truncation radii of singular kernels. This resolves, for convolution kernels, the problem mentioned in \cite[Remark~5.5]{parcet09pseudo} and recalled in Parcet's recent survey \cite[Remark~1.3]{Parcet2026ICM}. The proof involves not only a simultaneous dyadic representation of the operators but also a noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates of the resulting dyadic operators. This approach seems entirely new even in the commutative setting. Numerous applications are provided. On the one hand, it yields various maximal inequalities and pointwise convergence results for integrable kernels and dyadic approximations of the identity, monotone $L\log L$ majorants, and Poisson integrals on nilpotent groups and symmetric spaces. On the other hand, via various transference techniques, it implies maximal inequalities for Fourier multipliers, Schur multipliers and double operator integrals, together with bilateral almost uniform convergence of dyadic Fourier summation methods on $L_1$ of group von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: A Benders decomposition approach for hierarchical k-medoids
papers.abstract: We study a hierarchical clustering problem formulated as a sum of k-medoids objectives. This problem is related to the multi-period p-median problem, but instead of having nested facilities, we consider a hierarchy of nested assignments. We present two Benders formulations from the p-median literature and show how the obtained nested p-median solutions can be converted into hierarchical k-medoids solutions. We validate our methods on various instances. First, we show on small-scale instances that a standard Benders decomposition approach achieves speedups of up to three orders of magnitude over an existing branch-and-price method, while producing hierarchical k-medoids solutions that are at most 5% away from optimality. Second, we present an aggregated Benders heuristic that can handle instances with more than 13,000 observations.

papers.title: On one-dimensional pressureless Euler--Poisson systems: existence for non-semiconvex interaction potentials
papers.abstract: One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are repulsive at short range and attractive at long range are useful simplified models that describe biological aggregation. In the current work we employ new techniques to treat compactly supported solutions in the case where the potential is $C^1$ and satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions although it is not necessarily semiconvex, as required in previous work. Central to this approach are uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system, which requires the potential be only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. In the semiconvex case, these bounds also yield convergence of time-shifted trajectories to an eternal solution. The tradeoff, just as in the case of repulsive Euler-Poisson, is that we cannot claim that the emerging solutions for non-semiconvex potentials are sticky.

papers.title: On the Hausdorff dimension of oscillatory motions in three-body problems
papers.abstract: We show that for the Sitnikov example and for the restricted planar circular 3-body problem the set of oscillatory motions often has maximal Hausdorff dimension. Also, we construct Newhouse domains for both problems.

papers.title: Berry--Esseen Bounds for High-Temperature Ising Models
papers.abstract: We consider the nearest-neighbour Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and establish sharp results for the normal approximation of the magnetisation throughout the high-temperature regime. In particular, we establish optimal Berry--Esseen bounds between the magnetisation in an arbitrary finite region and a Gaussian with the corresponding finite-volume variance. These results hold for finite-volume Gibbs measures with arbitrary boundary conditions, as well as for the infinite-volume Gibbs measure. We also determine sharp rates of convergence of the magnetisation in a finite box to a Gaussian with variance given by the infinite-volume susceptibility. For this fixed Gaussian target, we show that, in dimensions $d\ge 3$, periodic boundary conditions yield strictly faster convergence than free boundary conditions. Our approach uses Stein's method to quantify the normal approximation error by analysing the semigroup of the continuous-time Ising heat-bath dynamics.

papers.title: Combinatorial Calabi flows on infinitely triangulated surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the combinatorial Calabi flow associated with vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces with piecewise Euclidean and piecewise hyperbolic metrics. Under the assumptions of uniformly bounded vertex degree and an $ε$-uniformly nondegenerate initial metric, we establish short-time existence of smooth solutions and prove uniqueness among solutions that are continuous in the $L^\infty$ norm.

papers.title: Free boundary regularity for the porous medium equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we resolve the local cone conjecture proposed by Kienzler, Koch, and Vázquez concerning the free-boundary regularity of the porous medium equation. We prove that the local cone condition guarantees the smoothness of the free boundary lying outside the initial support. The proof relies on new gradient estimates obtained through maximum principle arguments and comparison principles. As an application, we establish the global-in-time smoothness of the free boundary for solutions with convex initial support under standard assumptions on the initial data.

papers.title: Linear Group Actions with Exactly One Regular Orbit
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $G$ a finite $p$-group, and $V$ a finite faithful irreducible $G$-module. We show that if $G$ has exactly one regular orbit on $V$, then $p=2^{n}-1$ is a Mersenne prime and $(G,V)$ embeds into $(P_m,V_m)$ for some $m\ge 1$, where $P_m$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of the monomial group ${\rm GL}_1(2^{n})\wr S_{p^{m-1}}$ and $V_m$ is its natural module, regarded over ${\Bbb F}_2$. We determine the largest orbit size $p^{x_m}$ of $P_m$ on $V_m$ and the number of orbits of this size, and we construct subgroups of $P_m$ of order $p^{x_m}$ whose unique regular orbit is a largest orbit of $P_m$; for $p=3$ such subgroups exist for every $m$, whereas for Mersenne primes $p\ge 7$ we prove that they exist only for $m\ge 3$. Finally, we classify the subgroups of $P_m$ of order $p^{x_m}$ with exactly one regular orbit for $m=2$ and, with the help of a computer, for $p=3$ and $m=3$, where there are $13$ such pairs up to isomorphism; for $p=3$ and $m=4$ we show that there are exactly $4914$ conjugacy classes of such subgroups in $P_4$. In particular, such a subgroup is in general not determined by its regular orbit.

papers.title: Characteristic cycles and non-acyclicity classes for constructible étale sheaves
papers.abstract: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism between smooth schemes over a perfect field $k$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible sheaf on $X$ and $Z$ a closed subscheme of $X$ such that $f$ is $SS(\mathcal F)$-transversal outside $Z$. We construct a class supported on the non-transversal locus $Z$ by using the characteristic cycle $CC(\mathcal F)$ defined by T. Saito. This class is a geometric counterpart of the non-acyclicity class introduced by the third author and Zhao in [Invent. Math. 240 (2025), 123-191]. Under certain conditions, the formation of this class is compatible with base change and proper pushforward. It also satisfies the Milnor formula and a conductor formula. We conjecture that the image of this geometric class under the cycle class map is the non-acyclicity class. This conjecture can be viewed as a (relative version of) Milnor-type formula for non-isolated singularities. We prove this conjecture when $k$ is algebraically closed, $X$ is quasi-affine and $Y=\mathbb A^1_k$.

papers.title: Measuring the Quantum Phase of Multiphoton Systems
papers.abstract: The quantum phase of a multiparticle system has remained a long-standing mystery in quantum physics. The absence of a phase operator that faithfully represents this physical quantity has prevented the formulation of a meaningful uncertainty relation with particle number. Here, we resolve this problem by measuring, for the first time, the quantum phase of multiparticle systems containing up to fifteen particles. We achieve this through a new quantum state tomography scheme that combines homodyne interferometry with photon-number-resolving detection. This approach enables us to reconstruct complementary photon-number and phase representations and establish the corresponding number-phase uncertainty relation. Our measurements further provide access to the mutually unbiased basis of a multiparticle system, a fundamental resource for multiparticle quantum information processing. Furthermore, we report the spatially resolved characterization of the quantum phase. These results provide an operational framework for measuring quantum phase in multiparticle systems, with implications for fundamental quantum physics and scalable multiparticle quantum technologies.

papers.title: Iterative Truncated SVD for Inverse Scattering Problems
papers.abstract: We propose an iterative truncated SVD (iTSVD) algorithm based on a nonlinear least squares formulation for Newton's method for inverse scattering problems. The key idea is to estimate the effective rank of the corresponding linearized operator (or the Jacobian matrix after discretization), which defines the dimension of the signal space of the associated forward operator. Once the effective rank is estimated, truncated SVD (TSVD) reconstruction in the signal space can be computed efficiently based on fast random SVD (RSVD) -- only requiring matrix-vector multiplication which can be implemented in a matrix-free formulation by solving multiple forward and adjoint problems of the same type. Our analysis and numerical experiments show that iTSVD can markedly improve computational efficiency by reducing the number of iterations and enhance stability by physics/information based inversion. Moreover, the effective rank estimate is naturally model- and data-based. Extensive experiments, including far- or near-field, limited aperture, and random measurement data without or with noise, are presented.

papers.title: Frobenius Profiles of Polynomial-Multiple MRD Codes
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius intersection profiles of maximum rank distance (MRD) codes arising from ordinary polynomial multiples over finite fields. We prove that every numerically admissible profile is realized within this family over every sufficiently large extension, using a root-exponent pattern independent of the extension degree. A factor-orbit gap formula provides the underlying structural description, while effective extension-degree bounds guarantee realization. We also establish a lower bound valid for all polynomial generators and show that the upper and lower bounds differ by only $O_q(\log n)$ along an infinite family of parameters. Finally, we characterize the generalized Gabidulin members and obtain non-generalized-Gabidulin realizations of every profile with initial loss at least two over infinitely many extensions.

papers.title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics
papers.abstract: The block generalized-power method pairs threshold-based support selection with inexpensive Stiefel updates, but the standard block formulation conflates two nonequivalent objectives and leaves inactive components, threshold ties, and post-selection refitting ill-specified. We rebuild the model from the primal. Eliminating each loading column from the normalized loading-ball problem gives a sum of soft-thresholded Euclidean norms (A-SUM); the squared-threshold objective in common use arises from a quadratic lift (A-SQ). We prove both identities, exhibit a two-component instance whose maximizers disagree, and specify explicit conventions for zero-response columns, ties, rank deficiency, and mask-before-refit. For A-SQ we separate the historical full-polar iteration from a safeguarded Riemannian ascent and prove, for the latter, whole-sequence convergence via a sufficient-ascent lemma, a relative-error lemma, and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property, which applies because the soft-threshold objective and the Stiefel constraint are semi-algebraic. A strict threshold margin then forces finite identification of the support and sign pattern. The post-identification map is ordinary power iteration on the active covariance for a rank-one hard threshold, and the Frechet derivative of a coupled polar map for component-specific supports; a radius-based safe-screening rule follows from the same local analysis. Planted-spike experiments match the predicted identification time and local rates. On modern-AI panels (GPT-2 residual stream, ViT CLS stream, Pitprops) the thresholded block-sparse components match dense PCA on reconstruction and improve on it in monosemanticity and class specialisation. On three native-label scRNA datasets (Zheng17 FACS-sorted PBMCs, 68k donor-A with FACS-correlated labels, Tabula Muris) A-SQ beats dense PCA on cluster-recovery AMI by +0.023 to +0.044 at matched sparsity.

papers.title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $\D$ be either $F$ or a quaternion division algebra over $F$. We prove that every irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_{p+q}(\D)$ has at most one linear period transforming under any prescribed character of $\GL_p(\D)\times\GL_q(\D)$.

papers.title: The Eighth-Order Evolution Model for Closed Planar Curves
papers.abstract: We consider the $L^2(ds)$ gradient flow of $\frac12\int k_{ss}^2\,ds$ for smooth closed immersed planar curves. The stationary curves are precisely the multiply covered circles. We give an explicit sufficient condition under which the elastic energy is non-increasing and for each nonzero turning number, explicit small initial scale-invariant energy yields a global smooth solution with bounded positive length and exponential convergence to a fixed multiply covered circle, after reparametrisation. We note that that the qualitative rigidity and convergence results are already contained in the generalised ideal flow theory of McCoy and Wheeler. The present paper gives quantitative measure of small initial data, corrected evolution identities, and a complete argument in the case of the curvature energy $\frac12\int k_{ss}^2\,ds$.

papers.title: Big Ramsey degrees and structures in relational languages
papers.abstract: We establish a precompact transfer theorem for big Ramsey structures and a uniform envelope theorem for valuation hypergraphs. These yield big Ramsey structures for generic injective relational structures in languages with finitely many symbols of each positive arity, answering the existence part of Problem~6.3.2 of Balko et al.\ [M.~Balko et al., J.~Eur.~Math.~Soc.\ 28, 2101--2150 (2026)], and refute Conjecture~4.7 of Braunfeld et al.\ [S.~Braunfeld et al., Adv.~Comb., Paper No.~4 (2024)]. We also construct a finitely constrained free amalgamation class in a finite language of maximum arity three whose Fraïssé limit has infinite singleton big Ramsey degree, giving a negative answer to the existence question in Problem~6.3.3 of Balko et al.

papers.title: Rational Points on Drinfeld Modular Curves of Prime Level
papers.abstract: Let $q \ge 3$ be a prime power and let $\mathfrak{p} \subset \mathbf{F}_q[T]$ be a nonzero prime ideal of degree $d$. We prove that $Y_0(\mathfrak{p})(\mathbf{F}_q(T))=\emptyset$ if $d \ge 4$ is even or $d>q$, and that $Y_1(\mathfrak{p})(\mathbf{F}_q(T)) = \emptyset $ for every $d \ge 3$.

papers.title: Distributed Phase Tags: A Locality-Preserving Realification Compiler for Misty-State Quantum Programs
papers.abstract: Complex amplitudes can be simulated over real Hilbert spaces by adjoining a two-dimensional real/imaginary degree of freedom. In a multipartite program, however, one globally shared phase tag is not a locality-preserving program transformation: every party would have to act on the same auxiliary system. We recast the distributed real simulation of multipartite quantum mechanics as a syntax-directed compiler into a real misty-state intermediate language. For $n$ parties we give explicit phase-reference codewords $|0\rangle_{P_n}$ and $|1\rangle_{P_n}$ on $n$ local tags and prove that the same real operator $J=XZ$ on any single tag realizes the logical action of multiplication by $i$. If a complex party-local gate is $A=A_R+iA_I$, its real translation is \[ \widehat A_j=A_R\otimes I+A_I\otimes J_j, \] which acts only on party $j$'s data and local phase tag. We prove an intertwining theorem for arbitrary finite party-local pure-state circuits, exact preservation of computational-basis measurement probabilities, preservation of the run-time interaction graph, and one-rebit-per-party overhead. For the canonical three-party GHZ program, the translation lies entirely inside the ordinary black-and-white misty gate fragment: controlled-$J$ replaces the complex phase operation, while the invariant $J_jJ_k|0\rangle_P=-|0\rangle_P$ transfers the required branch sign. This yields a short correctness proof for all four promised GHZ inputs and explains the earlier 64-path cancellation calculation at a single logical phase-code boundary. We distinguish this program realification problem from the weaker task of finding any real strategy with the same correlations, and state precisely which parts are known real-Hilbert-space simulation and which parts belong to the misty-language compilation layer developed here.

papers.title: Sharp Holder regularity for autonomous Beltrami equations
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb C$ be a domain and let $\mathcal H:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be Lipschitz with constant $0<k<1$. We prove that every weak $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ solution of the autonomous Beltrami equation $f_{\bar z}=\mathcal H(f_z)$ belongs to $C^{1,γ}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, where $γ=3/(2K+1)$ and $K=(1+k)/(1-k)$. The exponent is optimal, resolving the conjecture of Astala, Clop, Faraco, Jääskeläinen and Koski.

papers.title: Geometric and measure-theoretic characterizations of the measure-determining property of balls in metric spaces
papers.abstract: The question of what structural properties drive the collection of open or closed balls to uniquely determine Borel probability measures on a metric space, the ball property, has a long history in measure theory. While various sufficient conditions have been known since the 1970s, and it was shown by Preiss and Tišer (1991) that it holds for all separable Banach spaces, Davies (1971) constructed a famous counterexample that shows it can fail on compact metric spaces. It was only recently established in van Delft (2026) that metric spaces admitting an isometric Hilbertian embedding must possess the ball property. This article provides a comprehensive structural and measure-theoretic characterization of the ball property. First, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the ball property to fail: the collection of balls must possess sufficient combinatorial capacity, which we define as charged dyadic shattering. Second, by characterizing the ball property via $λ$-systems, we place classical vector space results within a unified context. Building on this to understand spaces that have the topological capacity but lack linear or geometric rigidity required to force ball-annihilating measures to zero, we relate the metric outer measure to the cylinder outer measure on countable products of Polish spaces, deriving necessary and sufficient measure-theoretic conditions for the ball property to hold. This allows us to derive a structural taxonomy on the decoupling of the metric outer measure from the cylinder outer measure. This is subsequently used to deconstruct Davies' counterexample. Finally, we introduce a minimal combinatorial generalization of the ball property, the $n$th order ball property, and show that such classes can fully recover measure determination in highly pathological constructions like Davies' counterexample.

papers.title: Global hydrodynamic limit of the incompressible Navier-Stokes/Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system with large data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we aim to investigate the global-in-time hydrodynamic limit of the incompressible Navier-Stokes/Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system for light particles. With a modified micro-macro decomposition yielding uniform a priori estimates with respect to the Deborah number $\varepsilon$, we prove that the solution of the original system tends to that of the target system, i.e., the incompressible Navier-Stokes/Kramers-Smoluchowski system, as Deborah number goes to zero, and that quantitative convergence rates are obtained in the $L_{x,v,t}^\infty$ norm. Compared with the existing results that the convergence is from ``weak solution" to ``strong solution", the convergence results in the present work are further developed globally in time from ``strong solution" to ``strong solution" with vacuum (i.e., the macroscopic particle density may vanish at far field or at any point) and large initial data for both the original system and the target system. In addition, the ill-prepared initial data for the microscopic component of the kinetic quantity are allowed.

papers.title: On the effects of rotation on stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the half spaces in scale-critical spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier--Stokes equations with the Coriolis force in the half space with the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We show the existence of a unique small solution in the scale-critical Besov spaces. In particular, for any boundary data with only the normal component assumed to be sufficiently small, and for any external forces, we establish the well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary value problem when the speed of rotation is sufficiently large. In the proof, to exploit the stabilizing effect of the Coriolis term, we employ two explicit formulas depending on the relation between the horizontal frequency and the magnitude of the rotation speed.

papers.title: A Unifying View of Distributionally Robust Optimization for Probability Smoothing via Maximum Entropy
papers.abstract: The probability smoothing problem seeks estimators that assign positive probability to all categories, including those unobserved in a finite sample. In our previous work, we established that the estimator derived from distributionally robust optimization (DRO) with a $q$-norm ambiguity set ($q$-DRO) satisfies the axioms of Positivity, Symmetry, and Order Preservation, while relaxing the rigid Ratio Preservation axiom characterizing Laplace smoothing. In this paper, we observe that Symmetry itself imposes a strong constraint: it forces all unobserved categories to receive identical probability regardless of their relation to observed categories. Motivated by this observation, we study DRO with an optimal transport ambiguity set (OT-DRO), which incorporates inter-category dissimilarities through a cost matrix and thereby enables structure-respecting smoothing. We derive a tractable dual reformulation of OT-DRO as an empirical cross-entropy minimization with a Lipschitz-type penalty on the log-probability vector, and we identify an explicit threshold on the robustness radius at which the optimal estimator reduces to the uniform distribution, paralleling the threshold established for $q$-DRO. We then show, through Sion's minimax theorem, that DRO for probability smoothing over any compact convex ambiguity set that contains a strictly positive distribution is equivalent to entropy maximization over that set. This unifying perspective explains the parallel threshold structure in $q$-DRO and OT-DRO.

papers.title: On the arithmetic rank and cohomological dimension of some residual intersections
papers.abstract: We determine the arithmetic rank and cohomological dimension of each generic residual intersection of the ideal of submaximal Pfaffians of an alternating matrix of variables. This ideal fails to be a set-theoretic complete intersection. Our methods yield several structural results: in characteristic zero, we compute the $D$-module length of the top local cohomology module supported at this ideal and show that over the integers, it admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space structure. In particular, the top local cohomology module has no integer torsion. We also establish the $F$-regularity of the generic residual intersection rings considered here. Further, for each admissible height $s$, we construct $s$-residual intersections of complete intersection ideals and height three Gorenstein ideals that are set-theoretic complete intersections in any characteristic. Finally, we pose a general question of independent interest concerning the behaviour of arithmetic rank.

papers.title: On The Manin Constant
papers.abstract: We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.

papers.title: Fully First-Order Optimization for Implicit Multilevel Compositions via Recursive Perturbations
papers.abstract: We study optimization over a finite composition of implicit response maps generated by smooth potentials with strongly monotone signed gradients. This class includes chains mixing strongly convex minimization and strongly convex--strongly concave saddle responses. We propose a fully first-order method based on recursively perturbed response solves. The central issue is stability under inexact response solves: a downstream adjoint error changes the perturbation vector of the next upstream perturbed problem. We establish coupled bounds for the forward response errors and backward errors in the scaled response differences whose coefficients remain bounded as the perturbation parameter $δ$ decreases. A triangular Lyapunov construction combines these bounds with the $O(δ)$ bias of the exact perturbation estimator. For the warm-started method with finitely many inner iterations, this gives $\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nablaΦ(x^k)\|^2 \leq O(K^{-1})+O(δ^2).$ Thus, for fixed problem data and finite depth, $δ=O(ε)$ yields an $O(ε^{-2})$ outer-iteration dependence. For strongly convex minimization chains, we also derive condition-number-dependent first-order oracle complexity bounds.

papers.title: Blow-up of damped semilinear wave equation with short range potential and critical power nonlinearity
papers.abstract: The present paper is devoted to the study of a semilinear wave equation with spatially dependent scattering damping and a short-range potential, with particular focus on determining the critical exponent for the power-type nonlinearity. By employing the test function method, we establish wave-type blow-up results and derive lifespan estimates at the critical level. The main contribution of this work lies in providing a uniform asymptotic analysis for a family of test functions, which is achieved through a detailed investigation of a parametric second-order elliptic equation. As a further novelty, we relax the radial symmetry condition conventionally imposed on the coefficients $D$ and $V$ by resorting to the comparison principle in conjunction with a monotone exhaustion argument.

papers.title: The factorial separation conjecture
papers.abstract: We propose the Factorial Separation Conjecture (FSC), a strict strengthening of earlier factorial gap conjectures: \[ |n!-m^k|>n \] for all integers $n\ge8$ and $m,k\ge2$. The inequality excludes every displacement up to and including the factorial index. We prove the conjecture unconditionally for exponents divisible by three, for even exponents at least four, and for every exponent at least two when the largest prime divisor of the base is at most $n+2$. For exponents divisible by five, we prove the finite interval $8\le n\le1100$ and all sufficiently large indices, with an effective but uncomputed threshold. The conclusion for every $n\ge8$ and every exponent divisible by five is proved under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for a specified family of Dedekind zeta functions. Here GRH asserts that their nontrivial zeros have real part $1/2$. The arguments combine valuations, cyclotomic factorizations, cubic reciprocity, character estimates and explicit formulas. All finite comparisons are justified in the text. The general conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Quantum State Search with Classical Interactive Advice
papers.abstract: We study whether a quantum verifier can find a hidden quantum state by exchanging classical messages with an unbounded prover who knows the state. The verifier has access to a reflection oracle about the target. For a Haar-random $n$-qubit target, we prove that achieving constant average fidelity with the target requires $(q+1)^2(B+1)=Ω(2^n)$, where $q$ is the number of verifier queries and $B$ is the total prover-to-verifier communication. The bound allows arbitrary classical interaction and unrestricted computation between queries. Our proof extends the lower bound of Aaronson and Kuperberg from a single classical proof to an arbitrary classical interaction. As a result, we obtain a quantum-oracle separation of UniqueQMA from QCIP with polynomially many classical messages. In particular, we give a unitary oracle $\mathcal{U}$ such that there exists a language $L\in\mathrm{UniqueQMA}^{\mathcal{U}}$ but $L\notin\mathrm{QCIP}^{\mathcal{U}}$. We further give an oracle construction for a notion known as QMA-QCIP[2] gap problem. This gives average case hardness for a QMA language under classical access to a QCIP[2] decision oracle and is used in establishing negative results on witness encryption and quantum indistinguishability obfuscation.

papers.title: The classification of taut surface singularities via representations from logarithmic vector fields
papers.abstract: We study logarithmic vector fields on exceptional cycles through finite-dimensional representations and recover Laufer's classification of taut normal complex surface singularities. For graphs with two nodes, restriction maps define representations of a fixed quiver, with dimensions bounded independently of the number of components and their self-intersections. We identify restriction cohomology with an extension group and use interval decomposition to reduce its vanishing to interpolation on a rational chain. These calculations determine the classification conditions, and vanishing on every analytic realization proves sufficiency, including the nonrational cases. The obstruction cycles also give a uniform criterion: a graph is taut if and only if $H^1(5E,S_X|_{5E})=0$ for every analytic realization, where $S_X$ is the ambient logarithmic tangent bundle. We prove that five is the smallest positive integer for which this criterion holds for all graphs.

papers.title: Phase diagram and fluctuations in the cubic mean field Ising model
papers.abstract: We study the cubic mean field Ising model with three body and two body interactions and an external field. Our main result is a complete classification of the global maximizers of the variational pressure in the full three-parameter region $(K,J,h)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$. We identify a coexistence surface with two nondegenerate global maximizers and a critical curve with a unique quartically degenerate maximizer; elsewhere the maximizer is unique and nondegenerate. This extends the phase diagrams previously obtained on two-parameter subfamilies \cite{CMO24,O24}. As applications of the general results in \cite{CR}, we give explicit magnetization fluctuation theorems and asymptotic distributions for one-parameter maximum likelihood estimators in the resulting regimes.

papers.title: Cohomology and Representation Theory for Lie Superalgebras
papers.abstract: In this paper the authors describe two general frameworks for studying algebraic supergroup and Lie superalgebra representations. These encompass the well-known rational representations for a reductive algebraic group and the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}$ for semisimple Lie algebras. Many of the important developments will be surveyed and a blueprint for these new approaches will be provided. The existence of odd elements simply add an additional layer of difficulty. The authors prove that the calculation of the sheaf cohomology in the super setting for the rational category is equivalent to understanding the Lie superalgebra cohomology. This generalizes the well-known fact that the classical Bott-Borel-Weil theorem is equivalent to Kostant's theorem. Furthermore, for the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}^{\mathfrak p}$ where ${\mathfrak p}$ is a principal parabolic, the authors show that the characters of simple modules can be obtained by looking at natural generalizations of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials given by extensions between simple modules and costandard modules arising from the underlying costandardly stratified category.

papers.title: Quantum symmetric spaces at roots of 1
papers.abstract: We study the integral form of quantized coordinate algebras of symmetric spaces and its specializations at roots of unity. Our main tool is an integral localization, whose classical specialization recovers the open Borel orbit in the symmetric space. At a suitable odd root of unity, we prove that the quantum symmetric space is a finite projective module over its Frobenius center, which is canonically isomorphic to the classical coordinate algebra of the symmetric space. We show that the fibre algebras are isomorphic along each double Bruhat cell of the symmetric space. We determine the PI degree and propose a conjectural dimension formula for irreducible modules. In the simply connected case, we introduce a framed Kac-Moody data, which leads to a description of fibre algebras of quantum symmetric spaces via those of quantum Schubert cells.

papers.title: Which Immersions into Euclidean Space are Boundary Immersions?
papers.abstract: Here we study the problem of whether a given codimension one immersion $f$ of a closed and connected manifold into Euclidean space can be extended to an equidimensional immersion $F$ of some compact manifold $M$ whose restriction to the boundary parameterizes the image $S$ of $f$. Such an extension $F$ exists if and only if (i) simple conditions on orientations and wrapping numbers are satisfied and (ii) a distinguished finite subset of the first cohomology of $S$ with coefficients in a certain sheaf of finite groups contains the preferred point.

papers.title: Non-existence of negative weight derivations on Jacobian algebras
papers.abstract: Let $S=\mathbb K[x_1,\cdots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables with positive integer weights over a field $\mathbb K$ of characteristic zero. Let $f\in S$ be a weighted homogeneous polynomial such that the Jacobian algebra $$A=\left.S \middle/ \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1},\cdots,\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_n}\right)\right.$$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb K$-vector space. We prove that $A$ has no nonzero negative weight derivation, which confirms a conjecture of the third author. An immediate consequence of this conjecture is the micro-local characterization of quasi-homogeneous singularities.

papers.title: Structural stability of cylindrical transonic shocks to the three-dimensional Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring combustion equations
papers.abstract: We address the structural stability of transonic shock solutions to the Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring (ZND) combustion equations in a cylindrical domain under three-dimensional perturbations of the incoming supersonic flow and exit pressure. The perturbed transonic shock is completely free and its strength and position are uniquely determined by the incoming flow and the exit pressure. The solution shares the same regularity for the velocity, the pressure, the entropy and the fraction of unburned gas. The main difficulties are that the shock front is a free boundary to be determined simultaneously with the subsonic flow and the equations for all states are coupled with each other due to the combustion process. One of the key ingredients of the analysis is to reformulate the three-dimensional ZND combustion equations into a deformation-curl system and four transport equations in terms of the deformation tensor and vorticity. Another one is an elaborate decomposition of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions so that the shock front is uniquely determined by an algebraic equation and an unusual second order differential boundary condition is obtained on the shock front for the first order nonlocal deformation-curl system, from which an oblique boundary condition can be derived after homogenizing the curl system and introducing the potential function.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Inference in Linear Models with Clustered Outcomes: Exact Multivariate Tests and Cluster-Robust Confidence Sequences
papers.abstract: We extend anytime-valid inference for linear models from independent scalar outcomes to units that contribute a vector of dependent outcomes. We develop a parametric and a nonparametric treatment. For the Gaussian multivariate linear model with an unstructured error covariance, we derive a closed-form Bayes factor under the right-Haar prior and a matrix-normal mixture alternative and prove that it is an exact e-value at every sample size and a test martingale in the invariant filtration. To our knowledge, this Bayes factor is new in the generality considered here: a d x q coefficient matrix, nuisance regressors and an arbitrary fixed positive-definite prior precision under the right-Haar nuisance prior. It yields sequential Hotelling and MANOVA tests with exact confidence sequences. Under a common within-cluster design, the cluster-robust Wald statistic of a pooled regression is equal to Hotelling's T^2 statistic computed from the per-cluster least-squares summaries, giving an exact Gaussian benchmark with G-1 degrees of freedom. For general clustered population least-squares projections, the corresponding sandwich statistic is an asymptotic e-process, without Gaussian, common-design or linearity assumptions. Each treatment includes growth and first-order expected stopping-time results; under stronger regularity, direct comparisons of expected log evidence identify a fixed mixture precision that maximizes expected log growth through constant order within a specified family, for a specified frequentist alternative. Applied to randomized experiments with several outcomes, the robust procedure gives asymptotically anytime-valid joint tests, confidence ellipsoids and simultaneous confidence sequences for the vector of average treatment effects from ordinary least-squares estimates and cluster-robust standard errors.

papers.title: Convex-cyclic and super convex-cyclic weighted shifts
papers.abstract: Convex-cyclic operators are considered by H. Rezaei \cite{R1}. However, there is a general lack of theoretical understanding of super convex-cyclic operators. In this paper, we analyze super convex-cyclic operators. In particular, Super Convex-cyclicity Criterion is described. Additionally, we characterize convex-cyclicity of (invertible) bilateral weighted shifts in terms of their weight sequences, which in turn correct \cite[H. Rezaei (2013) Theorem 4.2 ]{R1}. Meanwhile, we give super convex-cyclicity of (invertible) weighted shifts in the bilateral case.

papers.title: Polynomial Spectral Gap Estimates for Finitely Differentiable Quasi-Periodic Schrödinger Operators
papers.abstract: We prove polynomial upper bounds on spectral gaps of quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators with small $C^{k}$ potentials and Diophantine frequencies. For sufficiently large $k$, the decay exponent is $k-34τ$, where $τ$ is the Diophantine exponent. We construct examples with lower bounds along infinitely many gap labels, showing that the leading coefficient $1$ of $k$ is asymptotically optimal. The proof uses quantitative reducibility and the Moser-Pöschel argument.

papers.title: Tensorial pinching by deforming curvature cones in higher codimension mean curvature flow
papers.abstract: We develop a pinching method for mean curvature flow in higher codimension. Motivated by pinching constructions for Ricci flow, the method uses a nonlinear deformation of the second fundamental form. We introduce two tensorial curvature conditions for closed immersions in Euclidean space which extend beyond the scope of classical scalar pinching results. In dimensions at least ten, we apply the method to prove convergence to a round point under the first condition and a canonical neighborhood theorem under the second.

papers.title: Negative Values of Wahl's Second Chern Number for Normal Surface Singularities
papers.abstract: We disprove Wahl's 1993 vanishing conjecture, open for more than thirty years, which asserts that $c_2^w(X)=0$ for every nonquotient normal surface singularity. Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve with a nontrivial involution having $r>0$ fixed points, and put $d=2g(C)-2$. If $d>r$, the union of the diagonal and the graph of the involution in $C\times C$ has negative definite intersection matrix and can be analytically contracted to a normal surface singularity $(X,o)$. A direct relative Chern-class computation and Wahl's residue formula give $c_2^w(X)=-r(d+r)/(d-r)$. An explicit curve of genus four gives $c_2^w(X)=-4$. Branched double covers of a fixed curve of genus two yield examples with $c_2^w(X_m)=-2m(m+1)$, so these values are unbounded below. We give the construction and intersection calculations in detail, as well as a line-bundle filtration realizing the negative value.

papers.title: On solutions to tropical Monge-Ampère equations
papers.abstract: This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Ampère equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and Kähler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Ampère equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, θ)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical Kähler form $θ$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Ampère equations on Berkovich spaces.

papers.title: Mixed Unfitted finite element approximation of band structures in photonic crystals
papers.abstract: Photonic crystals are periodic dielectric structures whose optical properties are characterized by Maxwell eigenvalue problems with discontinuous material coefficients. For arbitrarily shaped inclusions, their numerical solution remains challenging due to costly mesh generation and remeshing as the geometry changes. In this paper, we address this challenge by developing a mixed unfitted finite element method based on the Floquet-Bloch transform. Our method uses a uniform background mesh independent of the inclusion geometry, thereby avoiding interface-fitted meshing and allowing us to impose the periodic boundary condition through a direct identification of degrees of freedom. A key feature of our construction is that the resulting finite element pairs preserve the de Rham commuting relation for the shifted operator. This structure enables us to establish an inf-sup condition uniformly with respect to the cut position and, in particular, to rule out spurious modes. We further establish optimal convergence of the eigenvalues and eigenspaces, with constants independent of both the mesh size and the position of the interface. Finally, we present extensive numerical experiments in two and three dimensions to validate our theoretical results and demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
papers.abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation à la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

papers.title: A liquid-crystal analogue of the skyrmion Hall effect
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03379-0Magnetic skyrmions are known to exhibit a Hall effect in the presence of an electric current. Now it is shown that liquid-crystal solitons also exhibit a Hall-like drift under shear flow.

papers.title: Evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03454-6The mechanism for superconductivity in cuprates is still not known. Now, the observation of a relationship between the critical temperature and strength of coupling between electrons and spin fluctuations suggests the latter as a prime candidate.

papers.title: Upper bounds on the number of images produced by point-mass lenses at different distances
papers.abstract: If a light source is sequentially lensed by $n$ intervening point-mass lenses at distinct distances, the number of isolated images for a generic source position cannot be greater than $2\cdot 3^{n-1}$. If lensing shear is present in each lens plane, the image counts could be as large as $4^n$, however. For a general multi-plane point-mass lens system, we also devise the recurrence for the BKK bound on the image counts, which is strictly less than Perry's bound due to the resultant degree for $n\ge 2$. None the less, this bound is still quadratic in the number of lenses on each plane, so is likely to overestimate the true sharp bound, which is expected to grow linearly with the number of lenses.

papers.title: Biquandle Image Quivers
papers.abstract: We introduce a new family of weighted quiver-valued invariants of oriented classical and virtual knots and link, surface-knots and surface-links, and immersed surface-knots and surface-links associated to finite biquandles. We derive several polynomial invariants from these quivers via decategorification. We provide examples to illustrate the computation of the invariant as well as toy examples showing tables of invariant values for small biquandles.

papers.title: Minimal immersions by first eigenfunctions of Riemann surfaces with large conformal automorphism groups. The Klein quartic
papers.abstract: Minimal immersions of closed surfaces into spheres by first eigenfunctions play an important role in both the theory of minimal surfaces and spectral geometry. In this paper, we establish the existence of equivariant conformal minimal immersions of this type for Hurwitz surfaces and other families of %Riemann surfaces with large automorphism group. Finally, we explicitly construct a conformal minimal equivariant immersion of the Klein quartic into the unit sphere $S^{7}$ by first eigenfunctions. Ths immersion is a natural candidate for maximizing the normalized $λ_1$ among closed genus-3 surfaces.

papers.title: Equivariant deformation theory and deformations of homogeneous varieties
papers.abstract: We show that, in characteristic $p$, almost all projective homogeneous varieties under a reductive group and with non-reduced stabilizer do not lift to characteristic $p^2$. To this end, first we develop a general framework for equivariant deformation theory, leading to practical criteria ensuring that the deformations of a scheme come with deformations of a group scheme action. Second, we establish a formula to compute the cohomology of equivariant vector bundles over projective homogeneous varieties with non-reduced stabilizer, enabling us to determine the $G$-module structure of the first cohomology groups of their tangent bundles.

papers.title: Two Generalizations of the G_0 Dichotomy
papers.abstract: We give classical proofs of the generalizations of the $\mathbb{G}_0$ dichotomy to $κ$-Souslin digraphs and uniformly analytic sequences of digraphs indexed by $κ^{\mathbb{N}}$.

papers.title: Infinitesimally polar Killing foliations via geometric resolutions
papers.abstract: We establish the strong Molino conjecture for complete infinitesimally polar singular Riemannian foliations and identify their Molino sheaves with those of their geometric resolutions. The resolution preserves basic and equivariant basic cohomology and transverse curvature bounds. These comparisons yield orbifold models and approximations of leaf-closure spaces, Euler localization, closed-leaf existence and Euler positivity under positive curvature, and transverse sphere theorems. Maximal defect gives a closed-ball leaf-closure space. Further applications include fundamental-group growth bounds and closedness under nonpositive transverse Ricci curvature that is negative definite at one regular point.

papers.title: A 2X2 Matrix Approach to Hopf Fibrations:: Quaternionic Reduction of Octonionic Bi-unitary Matrices and an RLLR/LRRL Bracketing Rule
papers.abstract: We develop a common two-by-two matrix framework for the four classical Hopf fibrations associated with the real, complex, quaternionic and octonionic numbers. In all four cases the Hopf map is the image of the north pole of a sphere of trace-free Hermitian matrices under conjugation by a bi-unitary matrix, and it depends only on the first column of that matrix, without any bracketing convention, even for the non-associative octonions. Our main results concern general octonionic bi-unitary matrices, beyond the compatible matrices, with entries in a single complex subalgebra, on which earlier work on octonionic Lorentz transformations relies. We prove that every octonionic bi-unitary matrix is in fact quaternionic: its entries lie in a quaternion subalgebra depending on the matrix. We show that requiring Hermitian output leaves exactly four inequivalent ways of bracketing the octonionic triple products, among them an interlaced rule called RLLR/LRRL, and that each of them splits into an ordinary five-dimensional rotation and a four-dimensional scaling governed by a non-commutative determinant. This determines exactly when the evaluation preserves the geometry of the sphere, shows that it may contract or even collapse four dimensions, and explains why it cannot be compatible with matrix multiplication. We also recover in compact form, through the Clifford map, the known fact that suitable compatible matrices, which we interpret as transvections of the eight-sphere, generate the spin group Spin(9) by nested evaluations. Non-associativity thus does not prevent a two-by-two octonionic description of the full Spin(9) symmetry; it prevents that description from being realised through unrestricted multiplication of octonionic matrices.

papers.title: Integrable distortion I: Weil--Petersson circle homeomorphisms and the Schoen conjecture
papers.abstract: A circle homeomorphism $β:\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}$ is Weil--Petersson if it has a quasiconformal disk extension whose Beltrami coefficient is square integrable for hyperbolic area. We minimise the hyperbolic anti-holomorphic energy \[ E_2(h)=\int_\mathbb{D}η(h)|h_{\bar w}|^2,dA, \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \int_\mathbb{D}\frac{|μ_f|^2}{1-|μ_f|^2},dA_η,\quad f=h^{-1}, \] over all monotone Sobolev maps with boundary values $β$. For Weil--Petersson data, the unique minimiser is a real analytic hyperbolic harmonic diffeomorphism, globally quasiconformal and asymptotically conformal, with an explicit dilatation bound in terms of any admissible barrier's energy. We prove that a circle homeomorphism is Weil--Petersson if and only if it admits a finite-distortion homeomorphic extension satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}(\mathbb{K}_F-1),dA_η<\infty. \] For every $p>1$, the boundary values of a finite-distortion homeomorphism satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}|μ_F|^p(1-|μ_F|^2)^{-p_*/2},dA_η<\infty \] lie in Guo's $p$-integrable Teichm"uller space $T^p$. A capacity estimate for boundary moduli for the quasisymmetric ratio yields a derivative-free characterisation of $T^p$, essentially Bishop's theorem when $p=2$. The minimum defines a M"obius-invariant boundary energy, quantitatively comparable to the weighted square norm of the minimiser's Hopf differential. For arbitrary quasisymmetric data, we prove Markovi'c's theorem (the Schoen conjecture) by approximation with our smooth quadratic minimisers. Mori's theorem and the mean-value property of a logarithm verify the averaged-distance hypothesis in Riestenberg--Smillie's interior comparison, giving explicit displacement, energy-density and dilatation bounds in terms of the quasisymmetry constant. The nonquadratic ($p\neq2$) theory is developed in Part~II.

papers.title: Elliptic closed geodesics on non-negatively curved Finsler manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that if a compact simply-connected manifold $(M,F)$ with a bumpy irreversible Finsler metric $F$ whose flag curvature $K$ satisfies $K\ge 0$ and $H^*(M;\Q)\cong T_{d,n+1}(x)$ for some $d\in2\N$ and $n\in\N$ carries exactly $\frac{dn(n+1)}{2}$ (the number of closed geodesics in Katok's example) closed geodesics, then there are at least $2$ irrationally elliptic closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

papers.title: Goldbach and Alexandroff Shake Hands
papers.abstract: We introduce a relational Alexandroff topology associated with the strong Goldbach conjecture on the set of even integers greater than or equal to six. The construction is induced by a multivalued map encoding Goldbach representations and leads naturally to a notion of relational reachability. For arbitrary binary relations, we show that singleton closures coincide with reachable sets and that the common intersection of all singleton closures consists exactly of the globally reachable points. In the Goldbach setting, this yields a topological characterization of the conjecture in terms of the distinguished point \(6\). In particular, the strong Goldbach conjecture is equivalent to the associated relational space being non-\(wR_0\) and connected. We also obtain compactness and supercompactness criteria in terms of the set of possible Goldbach exceptions.

papers.title: On Huppert's $ρ$-$σ$ conjecture for primes in the orders of elements
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $ρ(G)$ denote the number of distinct prime divisors of $|G|$, and let $σ(G)$ be the maximal number of distinct prime divisors of the order of an element of $G$. Let $ρ(n)=\max\{ρ(G) \mid G \text{ solvable}, σ(G)=n\}$. We prove that $ρ(n)\le 4n-1+π(2n)$ for all $n$, and, with the help of a computer, that $ρ(n)\le 9n/2$ for all $n\le 16$. In particular, $ρ(n)\le\lfloor 9n/2\rfloor+2$ and $ρ(n)\le (101/22)n$ for all $n$, and $ρ(n)\le 9n/2$ for all $n\ge 58$. This improves the bound $ρ(n)\le (17/3)n$ due to Yang, and it shows that the bound $ρ(n)\le 5n$ stated by Bellotti, Keller and Trudgian holds, although its original proof contains a gap. Moreover, we show that $ρ(n)\ge 3n$ for all $n\ge 4$, which proves one half of a conjecture of the second author stating that $ρ(n)=3n$ for $n\ge 4$. We also derive a consequence for character codegrees and, conditionally, for arbitrary finite groups. The proofs of the main results do not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.

papers.title: A Reduced-Order Model for the High-Field Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System Based on a Micro-Macro Decomposition
papers.abstract: We develop a projection-based reduced-order model for the high-field Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system. Based on a micro-macro decomposition, the proposed Micro-ROM applies proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-Galerkin reduction only to the microscopic fluctuation while retaining the macroscopic density on the full spatial grid. The field-dependent Maxwellian and collision operator introduce additional computational costs that cannot be eliminated by Galerkin projection alone. To remove the dependence on the velocity-grid resolution during online simulations, we approximate the projected Maxwellian terms using precomputed Chebyshev expansions of functions of the local electric field and exploit a separable discretization of the collision operator to assemble the reduced collision matrix exactly from precomputed blocks. A first-order implicit-explicit scheme is employed to evolve the reduced coefficients and the density. The resulting method conserves discrete mass and formally recovers a discretization of the limiting high-field model as $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$. Its online computational cost per time step is independent of the velocity-grid resolution. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across a range of parameters, including the high-field regime.

papers.title: Superschemes and supermanifolds with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action
papers.abstract: We prove that given an analytic supermanifold $X$ over a complete field on which the additive supergroup $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ of super-dimension $0|n$ acts freely (in an appropriate sense), the quotient $X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ exists as an analytic supermanifold, and the canonical morphism $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is an $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. A stronger version of this result is proven for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds, whereby $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is a trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. Previously, Polishchuk [18] established an algebro-geometric analogue, which proves that a superscheme $X$ with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action gives rise to a locally trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-torsor $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$. This result is proven here in an alternative, elementary way. To all of these, a Hopf-algebraic approach is effectively employed.

papers.title: On simplicial maps with non-zero Hopf invariant
papers.abstract: In general, it is interesting to investigate the complexity of simplicial maps under various topological constraints. In this paper, we consider maps between (triangulated oriented rational homology) manifolds with non-zero Hopf invariant and establish bounds on the simplicial complexity of the fiber of a regular point. The lower bound, which is cubic in the dimension, is proved via a refinement of a theorem of S. Eilenberg. The upper bound is notable in that it is uniform with respect to the Hopf invariant.

papers.title: Expanding on Average Diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We study the statistical properties of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms with a two-dimensional center exhibiting mixed behavior, without assuming a dominated splitting inside the center. We introduce the notion of an expanding on average for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism and, under a center jacobian assumption, we prove the existence of finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures, and show the strong positive recurrence property, which implies that each SRB measure, up to a period, satisfies exponential decay of correlations, among other strong statistical laws. We apply our results to several examples.

papers.title: Self-Supervised In-Context Operator Learning for Optimal Mixing in Incompressible Flows
papers.abstract: We develop a self-supervised operator-learning framework for optimal mixing in incompressible flows, aimed at overcoming the computational limitations of classical PDE-constrained optimal control. The objective is to design velocity fields that efficiently homogenize a passive scalar while minimizing kinetic energy, quantified through the $\dot H^{-1}(Ω)$ mix-norm. Classical methods solve a separate optimal control problem for each initial condition using iterative forward-adjoint procedures, leading to substantial computational costs and limited scalability. In contrast, we propose to learn the solution operator that maps initial scalar fields to optimal mixing controls directly. The proposed self-supervised method does not require access to supervised labels, thereby significantly reducing the data-generation burden of supervised operator-learning methods. Our framework integrates a Lagrangian reformulation of the transport equation with a transformer-based neural operator architecture. The transport dynamics are represented through characteristic ODEs, enabling particle-based Monte Carlo optimization, while the learned velocity field is parameterized in a divergence-free spectral basis enforcing incompressibility and no-penetration conditions exactly. Numerical experiments on parametric families of initial conditions in two and three spatial dimensions demonstrate robust generalization to unseen regimes and approximately exponential decay of the mix-norm. The learned controls also transfer consistently to independent Eulerian finite-volume simulations, validating the physical fidelity of the learned operator. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first self-supervised operator-learning framework for optimal mixing and among the first data-driven approaches for optimal mixing in fully three-dimensional incompressible flows.

papers.title: Combinatorics of Seaweed Meanders
papers.abstract: We show that the index of a uniformly random seaweed meander satisfies a central limit theorem and is asymptotically equidistributed with respect to any modulus. We also extend work by Archer, Geary, and Laudone on the enumeration of seaweed meanders whose compositions have restricted parts. Finally, we give a connection to billiards in triangular shapes, which is related to a result of Eu, Fu, and Hsu.

papers.title: Closed locally symmetric spacetimes
papers.abstract: We present some results concerning the geometry and dynamics of closed locally symmetric spacetimes.

papers.title: Energy Estimate and Convergence of Weak Solutions of a Class of Nonlinear PDEs with Robin Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: We establish strong convergence in $L^2([0,T]\times[0,1])$ of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear PDEs with Robin boundary conditions to weak solutions of the corresponding Neumann and Dirichlet problems as the boundary parameter $κ$ tends to $0$ and $\infty$, respectively. Our approach relies on a particle system whose hydrodynamic limits yield the Robin problem for each fixed $κ>0$. An energy estimate derived from the microscopic stochastic dynamics provides the key bounds for passing to the subsequent limits $κ\to0$ and $κ\to\infty$, thereby obtaining the Neumann and Dirichlet problems.

papers.title: The four-dimensional Sklyanin algebras revisited
papers.abstract: We give a theta-function and projective-geometric account of the four-dimensional Sklyanin algebras. We define a family of quadratic algebras by declaring that their relations are precisely the two-tensors vanishing on the graph of a translation automorphism on a quartic complex elliptic curve and the vertex pairs where the vertices are the singular points of the four singular quadrics that contain it. We then use Jacobi's addition formulas for theta functions to produce a set of six explicit relations that coincide with Sklyanin's RLL-relations associated to Baxter's elliptic solutions to the 2 x 2 Yang-Baxter equation. We use the geometric definition to show that these algebras coincide with Feigin and Odesskii's four-dimensional elliptic algebras. Our approach agrees with that of Rains-Ruijsenaars theta function perspective on the four-dimensional Sklyanin agebras. For example, the rank-two secant-line relations of Levasseur-Smith coincide with their two-variable theta function relations. We give explicit theta-function formulas for the degree-two central elements, previously obtained by Levassuer-Smith, that annihilate various families of line modules.

papers.title: Heights of small CM cycles on Unitary Shimura Varieties
