The global counterexample is obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and then using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary. For comparison, on the unit disk we show that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials; the proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a Carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.

papers.title: The Bellaterra graphs are Ramanujan
papers.abstract: The Bellaterra automaton gives three involutions of every set of binary words of a fixed length. We identify their Schreier graph at level $n$ with a cubic arithmetic graph over $\Q(\sqrt{17})$, and prove that every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue satisfies the Ramanujan bound. In particular, this proves Malyshev-Pak's Conjecture that the Bellaterra graphs form a family of two-sided expanders.

papers.title: Critical limits of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps
papers.abstract: We study connected planar maps with a fixed number of numbered faces, whose vertices carry integer labels such that the minimum label along the boundary of each face is one. Each face has its own positive weight, and an edge shared by two faces receives the geometric mean of their weights. For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of faces, we prove that the suitably rescaled generating function converges locally uniformly as the face weights approach the critical value $1/12$, possibly at different positive rates. The limit is a finite, continuous sum of integrals over cubic schemes. Each scheme edge carries a Green kernel for a singular differential operator on the positive half-line, and each face contributes one insertion of the derivative of the tree scaling profile. The main difficulty is obtaining uniform estimates for small vertex labels, where the minimum-label constraints of different faces can interact. A positive corner-marking expansion reduces this problem to establishing uniform bounds on the contributions of marked configurations, both for small and large vertex labels. These estimates prove integrability of the surviving diagrams and show that coincident marks and noncubic schemes contribute only lower-order terms.

papers.title: Projective Decomposition and Intersection Cohomology of Rigid Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove a rigid analytic analogue of the Beilinson--Bernstein--Deligne decomposition theorem for projective morphisms over $p$-adic fields, with $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$-coefficients for every prime $\ell$, including $\ell=p$. As an application, we show that the $p$-adic intersection cohomology of every proper rigid analytic space is de Rham. We also establish an independent criterion for de Rham intersection cohomology with local coefficients in terms of the dimension of the boundary, yielding further results for curves, surfaces, and finite covers. For finite coefficients of characteristic different from $p$, we obtain isotropic analytic upper bounds for singular support and prove that singular support is analytic and Lagrangian for complexes supported in dimension at most one.

papers.title: Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial $Q_{p,q}(t)$ via the Rank-One Chabauty-Coleman Method
papers.abstract: Let $Q_{p,q}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$10$ second cuboid polynomial, with coprime positive integers $p\ne q$. We prove that $Q_{p,q}(t)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$, and hence over $\mathbb{Z}$. More generally, the normalized associated quintic $P_s(x)$ and its composition $P_s(t^2)$ are irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ for every $s\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0,\pm1\}$. The proof reduces linear and quadratic factors to rational points and horizontal conjugate pairs on one fixed genus-$2$ curve. A certified rank upper bound for its Jacobian, together with an exact divisor calculation, gives a rank-one annihilating differential at the prime $3$. For the quadratic-factor case, the symmetric coordinates of a horizontal pair lie on an explicit double cover of an elliptic quartic. All rational affine points on this model are $3$-adically integral and reduce to six smooth residue classes. The pulled-back differential is a unit in each class, proving that six displayed points form the complete list. Their coordinates exclude every admissible parameter. A negative real root of the irreducible quintic then supplies the additional degree argument required for irreducibility of the degree-$10$ polynomial. The rank computation and all exact arithmetic certificates are specified explicitly for reproduction.

papers.title: Exact quantum Hamming-weight computation at optimal depth and minimum width
papers.abstract: Hamming-weight computation and symmetric Boolean functions are basic primitives for quantum arithmetic and state preparation, where circuit depth and qubit overhead matter. We construct an exact circuit computing the Hamming weight of an $n$-qubit register with depth $O(\log n)$ and size $O(n\log n)$, using only the $n$ input qubits and $m=\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil$ binary output qubits. The circuit uses arbitrary one-qubit gates and CNOTs with all-to-all connectivity. Both depth and total width are optimal. Our constructions combine tree structures and pipelining, temporarily using input qubits as workspace. We also give exact circuits for every symmetric Boolean function with the same depth and size bounds, using only $m$ ancillary qubits returned to zero. Finally, we apply the counter to exact preparation of balanced Dicke states for even $n$. With only $O(\log n)$ ancillary qubits, we obtain expected depth $O(\log^2 n)$ using measurements and classical feedforward, and depth $O(n^{1/4}\log n)$ using unitary gates alone.

papers.title: Local rigidity of conformally Euclidean metrics for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation at fixed energy
papers.abstract: We prove local rigidity of smooth conformally Euclidean metrics $g_0$ on smooth compact domains $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge3$, for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation $(-Δ_g -k^2)u =0$ at a fixed energy $k^2>0$ which is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-Δ_{g_0}$ in $M$. Any smooth metric sufficiently close to $g_0$ in $H^s(M)$, with integer $s>n/2+1$, and having the same Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, is its pullback by a smooth diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. The proof uses a Helmholtz embedding to fix the gauge and a compactness argument together with a characterization of the kernel of the linearization.

papers.title: Sharp concentration levels and extremal functions for a planar Choquard-type Trudinger--Moser inequality
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth bounded domain and let $0<α<2$. We study the exponential Choquard functional \[ \mathcal{F}_β(u)=\int_Ω\int_Ω \frac{e^{βu^2(x)}e^{βu^2(y)}}{|x-y|^α}d xd y \] on the unit Dirichlet ball of $H_0^1(Ω)$. We establish the sharp boundedness threshold $β_*=(4-α)π$ and prove attainment of the critical supremum. More precisely, we determine the exact concentration level at every point of $\overlineΩ$ in terms of the regular part of the Dirichlet Green function. The concentration upper bound follows from the classical planar Trudinger--Moser concentration formula and the sharp Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality, after separating the background contribution. A test function obtained by matching a logarithmic profile to the Green function attains this bound asymptotically. Its exact Dirichlet normalization produces a strictly positive lower-order correction, which rules out concentration of maximizing sequences. We also prove the Euler--Lagrange equation, positivity, and regularity of extremals.

papers.title: Derived equivalence classification of twisted and generalized multifold extensions of affine type
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a piecewise hereditary algebra of affine type over an algebraically closed field. In this paper we give a derived and stable equivalence classification of twisted multifold extensions of $B$. The types $\widetilde D$ and $\widetilde E$ are already covered by the classification for tree type. We therefore consider the remaining types $\widetilde{A}_{p,q}$. We show that the $n$th power of the Nakayama functor on the full subcategory of a transjective component determines the twist, including its action on morphisms, up to conjugacy in the derived Picard group of a hereditary algebra. Together with the hereditary derived type and the folding number, this gives a complete invariant for derived equivalence, and also for stable triangle equivalence. We then compute these conjugacy classes in the unbalanced, balanced, bypass, and Kronecker cases, keeping the finite rotation data. Finally, by the normalization theorem of Asashiba--Kimura--Nakashima--Yoshiwaki, we obtain the same classification for generalized multifold extensions with nonzero integer jump.

papers.title: Model Theory and Algorithms for One-Relator Groups
papers.abstract: We study the elementary theories and algorithmic properties of one-relator groups. We give a first-order sentence characterizing Baumslag-Solitar-freeness in this class. For fixed $|m|>1$, we regularly interpret $\BS(1,m)$ as a definable subgroup in every one-relator group containing it. We uniformly, regularly and injectively interpret integer arithmetic in countable groups of cohomological dimension at most two. We obtain one uniform interpretation for all one-relator groups containing a non-unimodular Baumslag--Solitar subgroup. Every fixed finitely presented group is regularly interpretable in these groups, and their elementary theories are undecidable. We also describe the GBS overgroups of a non-unimodular Baumslag--Solitar subgroup. For the unimodular groups we construct finite-index direct products of free groups and $\Z$, and reduce the elementary theory of $\BS(k,k)$ to that of a free group with a named periodic automorphism. Using the recent Open AI result that BS-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic we obtain a terminating algorithm recognizing this class and obtain consequences. From the virtual compact specialness result of another Open AI paper, we obtain an effective construction of virtual free-by-cyclic presentations for hyperbolic one-relator groups, the free kernel may have infinite rank. For classes of torsion-free one-relator groups in which CSA implies toral relative hyperbolicity, we give a uniform algorithm deciding CSA and, in the affirmative case, the existence of a subgroup isomorphic to $\Z^2$.

papers.title: Variance Reduction Note 2: The Convergence of SPIDER
papers.abstract: The stochastic path-integrated differential estimator (SPIDER) tracks a gradient by accumulating small, shared-sample gradient differences and periodically refreshing the estimate. This second expository note on recursive variance reduction explains SPIDER-SFO and gives a self-contained proof of its expected first-order stationarity guarantee. The argument combines an epochwise mean-square error bound with descent under a clipped, normalized update. It yields $O(ε^{-3})$ stochastic gradient evaluations in the online setting and $O(n+\sqrt n\,ε^{-2})$ component gradient evaluations for a finite sum, with the remaining problem parameters fixed. All refresh costs are included. The presentation is pedagogical and makes no claim of a new algorithm or convergence rate.

papers.title: Discrete geometry and de-Rham cohomology of graphs
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of discrete spaces which are built by gluing coordinate patches together into an atlas, much as a manifold is built from charts. Graphs are the main examples, and an atlas on a graph gives it a geometric structure analogous to that of a manifold. This structure leads to a cohomology theory, which we show to be a discrete analogue of de Rham cohomology. We define a "discrete coordinatized space" as a cubical set equipped with the Alexandrov topology, on which differential forms become sheaves. When the atlas is regular, the de Rham cohomology agrees with the sheaf cohomology of the constant sheaf, just as in the smooth case. We compute it for several examples, including a torus graph and a graph resembling a sphere, and recover the cohomology of the corresponding surfaces.

papers.title: Fully quantum fidelity-based entropic continuity bounds
papers.abstract: We present a continuity bound for quantum conditional entropies in terms of fidelity, with no dependence on the dimension of the conditioning system. Our results encompass both the von Neumann entropy and one version of sandwiched Rényi entropy, which is particularly relevant for applications in quantum key distribution (QKD). In such applications, this bound should provide improved results as compared to previous continuity bounds based on trace distance. We also show that the bounds can be sharpened as expected for classical-quantum states, and verify that they hold when the conditioning system has countably infinite dimension. Finally, we present several variants tailored for exponential functions of the Rényi entropies instead, which should be relevant for QKD applications.

papers.title: Pseudoconvex Exhaustions of Hartogs Domains Associated with $L^2$-Optimal Pairs
papers.abstract: By constructing a smooth pseudoconvex exhaustion of the associated Hartogs domain, we give a new proof of the Deng-Ning-Wang's characterization of plurisubharmonic functions without the smoothness assumption.

papers.title: A Common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph
papers.abstract: Let G be a simple connected graph with the vertex set V (G) and the edge set E(G) such that |V (G)| = n and |E(G)| = q. The common neighborhood graph con(G) of G has the same set of vertices as that of G and uv is an edge in con(G) if u and v have at least one common neighbor in G. By a signed graph S, we mean a graph G whose edges has been assigned sign plus or minus. In this paper, the concept of common neighborhood graph has been initiated in the realm of signed graphs, that is, we define a common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph.

papers.title: A discrete-continuous-time stochastic framework for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptom modeling and pharmacological intervention via methylphenidate
papers.abstract: This paper presents an original mathematical and computational framework for modeling the efficacy of methylphenidate as an optimal control policy acting on the nonlinear dynamics of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Neural processes in ADHD are conceptualized as stochastic processes with trajectories that inherently converge towards stable, yet dysfunctional patterns associated with clinical symptoms. The pharmacological intervention is mathematically formalized as an external control signal that reassesses the system's drift and redirects these trajectories towards neurotypical regimes. To bridge these theoretical stochastic models with empirical clinical data, latent representations are inferred using a novel deterministic hybrid deep learning architecture, combining a one-dimensional convolutional neural network and a Vision Transformer, trained on preprocessed functional magnetic resonance imaging data.

papers.title: New Bernstein functions and subordination representations for time-nonlocal evolution equations
papers.abstract: This paper establishes subordination representations from multi-term time-fractional differential equations to single-term ones, a direction complementary to the previously known subordination from single-term to multi-term equations; combining the two complementary directions also yields subordination representations between two multi-term equations. The crucial step is to prove that certain implicitly defined functions are Bernstein functions. We show that the quotient $\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jλ^{α_j}\big)/\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jα_jλ^{α_j}\big)$ is a Stieltjes function whenever $0\leqα_1-α_m\leq 1$, and consequently that the inverse function of $λ=\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\varphi^{α_j}\big)^{1/β}$ is a Bernstein function for every $0<β\leqα_m$. As applications, we obtain subordination representations with a clear probabilistic meaning: from multi-term to single-term time-fractional diffusion-wave equations, between abstract nonlocal-in-time equations with kernels of type $(\mathcal{PC})$ (including equations of tempered stable type), and between nonlocal-in-time telegraph equations. A necessary and sufficient condition for $[(λ+b)^β-b^β]^γ$ to be a Bernstein function also yields a negative result: in general, no such subordination exists from an $α$-stable type dynamics to a tempered $β$-stable one when $α<1$.

papers.title: Noncommutative $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities
papers.abstract: We derive $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups on finite von Neumann algebras, from a spectral gap (PI) or from a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (MLSI). For $p\ge2$, the corresponding coefficients have optimal order $O(p)$ and $O(\sqrt p)$, respectively. Both estimates follow from Beckner inequalities by integration along semigroups. We also establish a non-tracial extension to quantum Markov semigroups satisfying GNS detailed balance. As a direct byproduct, we apply $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities to Schatten-valued functions on graphs in order to obtain the Schatten distortion of expanders.

papers.title: Maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity of finite element methods for stochastic parabolic equations in polygonal domains
papers.abstract: We prove that a spatial semidiscrete finite element method preserves the stochastic maximal regularity of the heat equation on bounded convex polygonal and polyhedral domains in dimensions two and three. A main difficulty is to establish suitable Green-function estimates for stochastic convolutions, whose paths generally lack classical time derivatives. Besides, the failure of the Burkholder-Davis-Gundy (BDG) inequality at the endpoint $p=\infty$ creates additional difficulties. Our approach leverages a hidden symmetry structure of the discrete Green's function, which enables the use of a key integration-by-parts type formula. Then the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^p$ regularity with $p\in [2,\infty)$ is obtained from the discrete local energy estimates and interpolation inequalities. To extend further the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity with the full range of integrability exponents, i.e., $p\in (2,\infty), q\in [2,\infty)$ or $p=q=2$, we also show that the discrete convolution kernel satisfies the stochastic Hörmander's condition, allowing the application of a stochastic version of the Calderón-Zygmund theory.

papers.title: The associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras
papers.abstract: For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$, one can associate a graded algebra (denoted by $\mathrm{gr}(A)$) with the radical filtration of $A$. An interesting question is to compare the representation theories of $A$ and $\mathrm{gr}(A)$. When $A$ is a Brauer graph algebra with defining Brauer graph $Γ$, we have described the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ in terms of the information of $Γ$. In this paper, we describe the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ when $A$ is a biserial fractional Brauer graph algebra - a notion that properly generalizes a Brauer graph algebra - in terms of the information of the defining biserial fractional Brauer graph $Γ$ of $A$.

papers.title: Inverse Zero-Sum Problems: The Property C and Property D Conjectures
papers.abstract: Let $C_n^r$ denote the direct sum of $r$ cyclic groups of order $n$, where $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Properties C and D predict a uniform multiplicity structure for extremal zero-sum problems over $C_n^r$: every sequence of maximum length avoiding nonempty zero-sum subsequences of length at most $n$, or of length exactly $n$, respectively, should have the form $T^{n-1}$. We give negative answers to the general Property C problem posed by Gao, Hou, Schmid and Thangadurai \cite[Open Problems 1.2]{GHST07} in 2007, and disprove the Property D conjecture proposed by Gao and Geroldinger \cite[Conjecture 7.2]{GG06} in 2006.

papers.title: Cellular bases of mirabolic Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that the mirabolic Hecke algebra $\mathscr{H}_{n,R}(q)$ over a commutative ring $R$ is cellular by constructing explicit cellular bases. When $R=\mathbb{K}$ is a field, we also establish a Morita equivalence between $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$ and a direct sum of Hecke algebras associated with symmetric groups. As applications, we classify the irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules and obtain a semisimplicity criterion. Finally, when $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}(q)$, we show that the cell modules arising from one of our cellular bases coincide with Siegel's irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules.

papers.title: Volume-dependent geometry and symmetry transitions of torsion optimizers in infinite cylinders
papers.abstract: We study relative torsional rigidity in infinite cylinders, addressing two geometric questions raised by Caldiroli, Iacopetti and Pacella on the shape of volume-constrained optimizers. The torsion problem has Dirichlet conditions on the free boundary and Neumann conditions on the fixed lateral wall. At small volumes we establish a two-term expansion of the optimal energy, curvature selection, and quantitative convergence of optimizers to boundary half-balls. We also obtain a uniform expansion for the exact torsion states on the explicit curved half-ball comparison domains. At sufficiently large volumes, every optimizer is exactly a finite cylinder, without convexity of the cross-section or an a priori free-boundary regularity assumption. The normalized optimal value is strictly decreasing up to a finite global transition threshold and constant thereafter. We distinguish this threshold from the local spectral stability threshold and prove coexistence of cylindrical and noncylindrical optimizers when the thresholds are separated. Exact one-sided derivative formulas identify nondifferentiability with the range of transverse energies among optimal states. Strict separation holds for all rectangular cross-sections and for sufficiently close smooth convex inner approximations of any rectangle, with no aspect-ratio restriction. These smooth examples exhibit both curvature-dependent small-volume concentration and a global symmetry transition.

papers.title: Upper Bound on the Correlation Energy of a Dense Fermi Gas in the Thermodynamic Limit
papers.abstract: We prove that the random phase approximation provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density. More precisely, we consider a mean-field scaling regime where the kinetic and interaction Hamiltonian are scaled by $ρ^{-2/3}$ and $ρ^{-1}$, respectively. We use a correlated trial state constructed through a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle--hole excitations associated to patches on the Fermi surface. Key of the proof is to control the position-space localization of the collective excitations. Combined with an iterated Duhamel expansion of the expectation values of (localized) particle number operators we obtain extensive estimates, which justify the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian and its approximate diagonalization.

papers.title: Semi-classical Szegő kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $Π_{k,\leq kμ_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, kμ_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szegő projection $Π_k$ converges to the weighted Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szegő projection $Π_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq kδ)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.

papers.title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
papers.abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $π_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

papers.title: Finite Symplectic Automorphism Groups of K3 Surfaces in Characteristic Seven
papers.abstract: We classify all finite groups of order divisible by $7$ that admit a faithful symplectic action on a K3 surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic seven, together with the possible heights and Artin invariants. Combined with the known classification of tame actions, this gives the complete list of finite groups admitting such an action in characteristic seven.

papers.title: Response theory at low temperature for weakly interacting quantum spin systems
papers.abstract: Recent work by Greenblatt, Lange, Marcelli, and Porta (Commun. Math. Phys. 2024) provides the first rigorous justification of adiabatic theory for interacting quantum systems at positive temperature. Their analysis treats weakly interacting lattice fermions and combines a rigorous Wick rotation with fermionic cluster expansion techniques. Here, we study a class of weakly interacting quantum spin systems and derive response theory at positive temperature, thereby covering non-Fermi systems for the first time. Our proof identifies and exploits the locality property of local indistinguishability as a key ingredient in carrying out low-temperature adiabatic expansions. The fact that these systems satisfy local indistinguishability was recently established jointly with Adhikari (arXiv:2508.15907) using cluster expansion methods together with a probabilistic swapping trick.

papers.title: Lucas' Theorem modulo $p^n$ via Harmonic sums
papers.abstract: Lucas' theorem states that for a prime $p$, integers $a,b\geq0$ and $0\leq r,s\leq p-1$, one has $\binom{pa+r}{pb+s}\equiv\binom{a}{b}\binom{r}{s}\bmod p$. Let $D(p^n)$ be the set of pairs $(r,s)$ with $s\leq r$ for which this congruence holds modulo $p^n$ for all $a,b\geq0$. Rowland characterized $D(p^2)$ in terms of harmonic sums and symmetries of Pascal's triangle. For $n<p$, we give a criterion for a point $(r,s)$ to lie in $D(p^n)$ in terms of generalized harmonic sums of order at most $n-1$. We show that $D(p^n)$ is invariant under the reflection $(r,s)\mapsto(r,r-s)$ and the rotation $(r,s)\mapsto(p-1-s,r-s)$, so that with every point it contains its full orbit under the dihedral group $D_3$. Applied to the vertices, our criterion gives a result of Jacobsthal-Ljunggren type modulo $p^n$. In particular, we recover Zhao's result $(0,0)\in D(p^4)$ if and only if $p$ is a Wolstenholme prime. We also study the centroid and the edge midpoints, whose membership in $D(p^3)$ and $D(p^4)$ is governed by Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Wolstenholme primes and super Wieferich primes. In particular, for $p=205129$ the centroid lies in $D(p^3)$, answering a question of Rowland.

papers.title: Pre-Nichols algebras and generation of pointed Hopf algebras in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We study when a finite-dimensional pre-Nichols algebra $R$ of $V$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\nmid\dim R$, is necessarily isomorphic to the Nichols algebra $\B(V)$. A trace identity gives a rigidity criterion involving the twist on minimal defining relations. Using integral forms and Hochschild cohomology, we establish uniform rigidity for Yetter--Drinfeld modules of bounded dimension over fixed finite abelian groups, and obtain related results for certain modules over nonabelian groups. For every finite group $G$ of odd order, outside finitely many characteristics depending only on $G$, every finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $H$ with $G(H)\simeq G$ and dimension prime to the characteristic is generated by group-like and skew-primitive elements. If $G$ is abelian, then, outside a possibly larger finite set of characteristics, every such $H$ is a Hopf $2$-cocycle deformation of its associated graded Hopf algebra.

papers.title: An Exact Mass Threshold for Global Existence and Blow-up in Semilinear Anti-de Sitter Equations
papers.abstract: We study the influence of the mass parameter on global existence and finite-time blow-up for the semilinear anti-de Sitter Klein--Gordon equation \[ φ_{tt}-e^{2t}Δφ+nφ_t+m^2φ=|φ|^p \qquad\text{in }[0,\infty)\times\R^d. \] After removing the damping term, we establish $L^2$ energy estimates for the resulting Klein--Gordon equation with constant coefficient in the potential. They imply global existence for arbitrary sufficiently small energy data, without spatial localization, whenever \( m^2>-\frac{d(2n+d)}{4} \quad\text{and}\quad p>1. \) In the remaining mass parameter interval above the structural threshold, an exact change to conformal time reduces the problem to a scale-invariant effective damped wave equation. Exponentially weighted energy estimates then extend global existence to \( -d(n+d)<m^2\le-\frac{d(2n+d)}4 \quad\text{for every } \quad p>1. \) In the complementary regime $m^2\le-d(n+d)$, we prove finite-time blow-up for every $p>1$ and for weak solutions with finite speed of propagation arising from nonnegative, nontrivial initial data. We further obtain lifespan estimates that are polynomial at the threshold and logarithmic below it. Thus, $m^2=-d(n+d)$ is the exact structural mass parameter threshold separating the global-existence and blow-up regimes.

papers.title: Conventional Inference under Nonstationary Heavy Tailed Fractional Processes & Arrays
papers.abstract: Existing regression inference methods for nonstationary heavy tailed data are largely limited to unit roots tests. Functional central limit theorems (FCLTs), which are commonly used for the asymptotic analysis of nonstationary models, are inapplicable to nonstationary data characterized by a memory parameter $d<1$ and a stability parameter $α<2$. Furthermore, it is well known that inference under nonstationarity is often non-conventional, and this issue is exacerbated in the presence of heavy-tailed data. The interaction of long memory and heavy tails significantly enlarges the nonstationary region---i.e., the covariate model space---where conventional inference methods typically fail. To address these challenges, we propose a new limit theory and methods that facilitate both workable asymptotics and conventional inference in regressions involving general nonstationary heavy-tailed covariate processes. Specifically, our approach develops a limit theory for heavy-tailed weakly nonstationary processes (hereafter, HT-WNPs), which lie on the threshold of nonstationarity (cf. Duffy and Kasparis, 2021, Annals of Statistics). We demonstrate that the proposed methods---including IVX-based and related instrumental-variable procedures---facilitate conventional inference for a broad class of stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariates. This class includes nearly and mildly integrated arrays, as well as nonstationary fractional processes with memory parameter $1-1/α<d<2-1/α$, where $α\in(1,2]$. Our analysis is applicable to both parametric and kernel regression models. The finite-sample performance of the proposed methods is evaluated through a comprehensive simulation study. Additionally, we provide an empirical application to the predictability of stock returns using long-memory heavy-tailed predictors.

papers.title: Boundedness of nonregular bilinear pseudodifferential operators on variable Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce two bilinear, non-regular symbol classes\linebreak $BS\mathcal B^m_δ(r,μ,v;N,λ)$ and $BS\mathcal F^m_δ(r,μ,v;N,λ)$, where $m\in\mathbb R$, $0\leqδ<1$, $0<μ,v\leq\infty$, $1\leqλ\leq2$, $r>n/μ$, and $N>2n/λ$, with $μ<\infty$ for the latter class. For $μ\geq1$, $(1-δ)r\geq n/μ$, and sufficiently large $N$, we establish boundedness of the associated bilinear pseudodifferential operators on Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with variable smoothness, integrability and summation exponents. To the best of the authors' knowledge, these operator estimates are new even on the classical Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with constant exponents. As an application, we establish the multiplication algebra property for both variable exponent spaces.

papers.title: Noise-Awareness in Quantum Software Testing: An Empirical Landscape Analysis
papers.abstract: Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) hardware has transformed quantum computing into a practical experimental platform while introducing fundamental challenges associated with hardware noise, decoherence, and probabilistic execution. Although quantum software testing (QST) has rapidly emerged as an active research area, it remains unclear to what extent existing testing methodologies explicitly engage with noisy and hardware-constrained execution environments. This paper presents a systematic empirical landscape analysis of noise-awareness in QST research through a deterministic, taxonomy-guided analytical framework applied to 61 papers published between 2018 and 2025 across eight testing paradigms, contrasting how contributions are framed with how they are evaluated. Among the analyzed papers, 47 (77.0%) are noise-oblivious and only 14 (23.0%) explicitly engage with noise-related execution concerns, while only 11 (18.0%) report evaluation on physical hardware or a noisy simulator. Test generation, the largest paradigm, exhibits a noise-awareness rate of only 14.3%, and debugging and repair 18.2%; coverage-based, metamorphic, and differential testing contain no noise-aware contributions. Noise-aware methodologies emerged late and remain outnumbered in all analyzed years. Framing and evaluation are strongly associated (odds ratio 40.5, p < 0.001) yet diverge for individual papers: 5 of the 14 noise-aware papers evaluate only on ideal simulators. Inferential statistical tests are reported in only 16.4% of papers. The classification framework was validated against a blinded, human-coded reference sample, achieving almost perfect inter-rater agreement on testing-technique classification and substantial agreement on noise-awareness. The framework provides a reusable empirical basis for longitudinal analysis of hardware-conscious testing practice.

papers.title: Classification of Isometric Immersions of Spherical and HCMU Footballs into $\E^{3}$
papers.abstract: We study global isometric immersions of rotational metrics with two conical ends into Euclidean three-space. For a metric $g=\mathrm{d}u^2+f(u)^2\mathrm{d}θ^2$ of positive Gauss curvature, we prove that vanishing endpoint traces of the weighted mixed shape coefficient $f^2b$ force every smooth isometric immersion to be rotational. The resulting congruence classes are parametrized by an integer angular covering degree bounded below by the two cone-angle parameters. The proof combines a scalar elliptic equation derived from the Gauss--Codazzi system, the maximum principle, and a global angular closing condition. For spherical footballs, isolated-singularity theory and a direct estimate in coordinates conformal for the second fundamental form establish the trace condition for every smooth immersion of the regular part. We also classify all rotational isometric immersions of HCMU footballs, including those whose curvature changes sign. When the minimum curvature is nonnegative, this classification exhausts the immersions satisfying the trace condition, and hence all immersions admitting a $C^2$ polar extension at both tips.

papers.title: Local Approximation of $A$-Harmonic Functions and the Super-Localization Conjecture
papers.abstract: We consider the local energy approximation of $A$-harmonic functions on concentric cubes with a fixed size ratio in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, for bounded, symmetric, uniformly elliptic diffusion tensors~$A$. We give a short proof of the Kolmogorov $n$-width decay rate $\exp(-cn^{1/(d-1)})$ conjectured by Ma [Found.\ Comput.\ Math.\ 26 (2026), 1699--1758], where $n$ denotes the approximation dimension. We apply this result to numerical homogenization, improving local approximation estimates for multiscale spectral generalized finite element methods and proving the conjectured local super-localization rate of Hauck and Peterseim [Math.\ Comp.\ 92 (2023), 981--1003] for interior Cartesian patches.

papers.title: The Streets--Tian conjecture on compact homogeneous quotients
papers.abstract: A Hermitian-symplectic metric is a Hermitian metric whose Kähler form is given by the $(1,1)$-part of a closed $2$-form. Streets-Tian Conjecture states that a compact complex manifold admitting a Hermitian-symplectic metric must be Kählerian (i.e., admitting a Kähler metric). We study Hermitian-symplectic metrics on homogeneous complex manifolds with compact isotropy, and on their compact discrete quotients. If the transitive group is connected and unimodular, we show that an invariant Hermitian-symplectic form gives an invariant Kähler metric, with no lattice assumption. By averaging, the same conclusion holds for compact quotients, even if the initial metric has no invariant lift. The proof uses the top exterior power of a Hermitian-symplectic form to bound the volume functional on an invariant Aeppli slice. Applying this bound to midpoint metrics gives a uniform trace estimate. From this, volume maximization produces a balanced metric in the slice, which is also pluriclosed and hence Kähler. We also describe the resulting Kähler representative and give examples showing the role of the closed lift.

papers.title: Covering finite fields by translates of multiplicative subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $G_d$ be the subgroup of index $d>1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and put $G_d^0=G_d\cup\{0\}$. For a covering $A+G_d^0=\mathbb{F}_q$ with $\#A=s$, we prove $q\le d^{8s/d}$ by shifting the roots of a Bonferroni polynomial. Although a uniform bound in $s$ alone must allow exponential growth, our estimate confines such growth to bounded indices and gives polynomial bounds when $s/d$ is bounded. A cubic specialization gives bounds of degree at most eight for $s\le2d$. For shift sets of logarithmic size, higher moment estimates give a uniform covering-probability formula, including the critical window. Together with the index restriction, this determines the covering indices of almost every shift set of size $\lceil k\log q\rceil$ for each fixed integer $k\ge2$. A subfield construction attains the order of the uniform restriction on the index. We determine its covering number exactly and prove minimality under subgroup inclusion. We also characterize equality in the elementary counting bound by subfield cosets. Fixing a subfield as the shift set in a quadratic extension leads to a sharper projection bound, attained by an infinite family with unique representations outside the shift subfield.

papers.title: An inclusion coupling of prefix laws and the Chan-Pak rank inequality for all finite posets
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a finite poset, let $x\in P$, and let $N_k$ count its linear extensions in which $x$ occupies position $k$. We prove Chan and Pak's conjecture that, for all integers $a,h\ge1$, \[ (a+h-1)N_{a+h-1}N_a\ \ge\ (a-1)N_{a-1}N_{a+h}+hN_aN_{a+h}. \] The key result is an inclusion coupling of the laws of the set of elements preceding $x$, conditional on consecutive positions of $x$. We construct reversible exchange chains on the corresponding layers of order ideals and couple their generators so that the two prefix sets remain nested. Fishburn's correlation inequality gives monotonicity of endpoint probabilities; their unit total masses provide the rate bounds needed for the coupling. A stationary distribution of the coupled chain then has the required marginals. Normalized cover observables yield a four-term nonnegative certificate for the case $h=1$, and the general case follows by telescoping. The argument applies at every width and gives a proof of Stanley's log-concavity inequality with Fishburn's inequality as its sole external inequality.

papers.title: Generalized symmetric pairs, Lie superalgebras, Dirac operators and Kostant constants
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a geometric construction of contragredient Lie superalgebras, with the exceptions of $A(m,n)$ $(m,n>0)$ and $G(3)$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an order 4 automorphism $σ$, the eigenspace decomposition being $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)$. When $\mathfrak{g}(i)$ admits a $\mathfrak{g}(1)$-invariant symplectic structure, $(\mathfrak{g},σ)$ is called a \emph{generalized symmetric pair with symplectic subspace}. In this paper, we classify all such pairs and construct a natural Lie superalgebra structure on $L= L_{\bar{0}}+L_{\bar{1}}$ with $L_{\bar{0}}=\mathfrak{g}(1)$ and $L_{\bar{1}}=\mathfrak{g}(i)$. Furthermore, we investigate the constants arising from the squares of two distinct Dirac operators: $D$ for $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}^{σ^2}+\mathfrak{g}^{-σ^2}$, and $D_s$ for $L=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)$. We prove that the constant $C$ in $D^2$ admits a remarkable factorization \[C=J^*(Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}})\cdot\dim L_{\bar{1}}\cdot h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}},\] where $h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}}$ is the signed dual Coxeter number of $L$ and $J^*(Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}})$ is a mapped Casimir constant of its even part. This formula reveals an unexpected unification of symmetric space geometry and Lie superalgebra invariants. Finally, we prove that the Kostant constant $\mathrm{K_s} = \left.Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}}\right|_{L_{\bar{1}}}=\frac{1}{2}$ is universal for all contragredient Lie superalgebras with non-degenerate Killing form, which implies that the constant $C_s$ in $D_s^2$ satisfies $C_s=\frac{1}{16}\dim L_{\bar{0}}$. We then establish a bijection between such superalgebras and solutions of the superadmissibility index equations $E_s^{I\!I} =\frac{1}{2}, E_s^I = \frac{1}{2}$, recovering the classification from an invariant-theoretic perspective.

papers.title: Non-geometric ideal triangulations with all edge valences at least six
papers.abstract: Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio conjectured that an ideal triangulation in which every edge has valence at least six can be realized by hyperbolic partially truncated tetrahedra on the compact 3-manifold it defines. We show that this is false. Starting from the figure-eight knot complement, we construct an ideal triangulation with $2688$ tetrahedra and edge valences six and eighteen whose manifold is hyperbolic with totally geodesic boundary, but which admits no such realization. The obstruction is a critical point of the covolume energy of Luo and Yang at which three tetrahedra have collapsed: convexity then excludes every geometric competitor, an Euler characteristic count excludes edges of length zero, and the critical point itself is located by a finite certificate in exact integer arithmetic. The obstruction persists in every finite cover, while a complementary theorem shows that no counterexample can have only two edge lengths or only two orbits of edges.

papers.title: LiftDiff: Guided Discrete Diffusion for Quantum Code Construction
papers.abstract: The realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation relies on Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECC). Of particular interest are codes that combine a high encoding rate with sufficient distance. Existing algebraic constructions, such as lifted product (LP) codes, build a large quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code from a classical base matrix. In this work we introduce LiftDiff, a generative approach to the discovery of QECC. A discrete denoising diffusion model is trained to generate base matrices over the group algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[\mathbb{Z}_\ell]$, which are then expanded into LP codes. The reverse diffusion process is guided by an energy function that evaluates quantum code properties, including girth, degree, sparsity and decoding performance, steering the sampler toward matrices that yield LP codes with favorable parameters. Our method discovers codes with parameters such as $[[169,13,11]]$, $[[143,15,9]]$, and $[[260,24,10]]$, including a $[[247,19,14]]$ code that achieves the highest ${kd^2}/{n}$ among the baselines. Moreover, several discovered codes outperform the Gross code across a broad range of the tested physical error rates under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise.

papers.title: Condensation and Non-condensation in the Quasilinear 4-wave Kinetic Equation
papers.abstract: We study finite-time condensation at zero frequency for the isotropic quasilinear 4-wave kinetic equation in three dimensions. With Schrodinger dispersion and a product interaction coefficient with exponent $β\in(0,3/4]$, we construct global measure solutions $(g_t)_{t\geq0}$ for every nonnegative initial measure $g_0$ with finite wave action and energy. We then establish the sharp threshold $β=1/4$ for finite-time condensation of the constructed solutions. For $β\in[1/4,3/4]$, the constructed solutions satisfy $g_t(\{0\})=g_0(\{0\})$ for all $t\geq0$. For $β\in(0,1/4)$, every constructed solution with $(g_0)_{\mathrm{ac}}\neq0$ satisfies $\|g_t-\mathcal{N}_0δ_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq C\mathcal{N}_0(1+\mathcal{N}_0^2t)^{-(1-4β)/40}$ for all $t\geq0$, where $\mathcal{N}_0=g_0([0,\infty))$ and $C=C(β,g_0/\mathcal{N}_0)>0$. In particular, for every $ζ\in(0,1)$, there exists $T_ζ<\infty$ such that $g_t(\{0\})\geq(1-ζ)\mathcal{N}_0$ for all $t\geq T_ζ$.

papers.title: A relationship between three-dimensional Bessel processes in terms of Pitman's transformation
papers.abstract: For every $x\ge 0$, let $R^{x}=\{ R^{x}_{t}\} _{t\ge 0}$ be a three-dimensional Bessel process started at $x$. Given $x>0$, with the aid of Pitman's theorem, a path transformation $T_{x}$ under which the process $T_{x}(R^{y})$ is distributed as $R^{x}$ for any $y>0$ is constructed. In fact, we prove that, for every $x,y>0$, the two three-dimensional processes \begin{align*} \bigl( R^{x},T_{y}(R^{x}),\mathcal{P}(-R^{x})+x\bigr) && \text{and} && \bigl( T_{x}(R^{y}),R^{y},\mathcal{P}(-R^{y})+y\bigr) \end{align*} are identical in law, where $\mathcal{P}$ is Pitman's transformation. In the course of our exploration, it will be revealed that, for any $x>0$, the process $\mathcal{P}(-R^{x})+x$ has the same law as the standard three-dimensional Bessel process $R^{0}$, which is then applied to derive a disintegration formula for the law of $R^{x}$ in terms of Pitman's transformation. An application of the formula to three-dimensional Bessel bridges is also presented.

papers.title: Crossing numbers of complete bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: Zarankiewicz's long standing conjecture states that the crossing number $cr(K_{m,n})$ of the complete bipartite graph is \[ Z(m,n):=\bigg\lfloor{\frac{m}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{m-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor. \] Using flag algebras, we show that $cr(K_{n,n}) \geq 0.96936 \cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. We also show that the rectilinear crossing number $\overline{cr}(K_{n,n})$ of $K_{n,n}$ is at least $0.987\cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. Additionally, we prove the following for complete bipartite graphs: if a drawing of $K_{n,n}$ contains no induced subdrawing of $K_{3,4}$ with exactly two crossings whose endpoints intersect in exactly one vertex, then it has at least $Z(n,n)+o(n^4)$ crossings. This is a local restriction inspired by Turán-type problems that gives an asymptotically tight result. A closely related conjecture is Hill's conjecture stating that the crossing number $cr(K_{n})$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is \[ H(n):= \frac14 \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor \] for all $n \geq 3$. By an averaging argument, the asymptotic Zarankiewicz conjecture implies the asymptotic Hill conjecture. We improve the lower bound on $cr(K_{n})$ from $(0.985+o(1)) H(n)$ to $(0.9899+o(1)) H(n)$. Both conjectures were claimed to be true in manuscripts by OpenAI dated Sep 23, 2026 and made public on Oct 6, 2026. This paper represents the state of knowledge before those publications and shows how far we can push the flag algebra method.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Quantum Forensics for QKD: Machine Learning Attack Detection and Signature Extraction
papers.abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) supports secure key establishment under ideal protocol assumptions, but practical systems remain exposed to implementation-level attacks against optical channels, detectors, and controller behavior. This study presents Quantum Forensic Log (QF-LOG), a simulation-based forensic framework for analyzing aggregated QKD operational logs rather than raw quantum states. QF-LOG uses four observable features: quantum bit error rate (QBER), photon count, latency in milliseconds, and abort flag. The framework classifies normal operation and three simulated attack-related conditions: partial intercept-resend, detector-blind, and fiber-tap. A physics-inspired Generator-A dataset with 5 million balanced records was constructed using explicit mathematical generation models for all four features. A transparent threshold baseline, logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were evaluated on Generator-A. The full-feature learning models achieved macro F1-scores from 0.8211 to 0.8243 and outperformed the transparent two-feature comparator. Feature diagnostics showed that QBER contributed most, followed by latency in milliseconds and photon count, while no single feature reproduced the full feature set performance. Robustness was assessed on a separately generated Generator-B dataset of 5 million records that uses the same governing equations under shifted simulated operating parameters. Without retraining or tuning, their macro F1-scores decreased to values from 0.5645 to 0.5669. These findings show that QF-LOG can support interpretable forensic classification in a controlled synthetic setting, but stable internal evaluation does not establish reliability under changed simulated QKD operating conditions. The framework provides a documented basis for future evaluation across broader simulated settings and hardware-generated QKD logs.

papers.title: A nontopological triangulated category which is $θ$-dg enhanced
papers.abstract: For every nonzero commutative ring $R$ and infinite cardinal $θ$, we construct a nontopological triangulated category over $R$, whose thick subcategories generated by $<θ$ objects admit $R$-linear dg enhancements, while the scalar action of $R$ is faithful.

papers.title: Exact probability laws of random inner products: Dirichlet splines, overlaps, uncertainty, and Bargmann invariants
papers.abstract: Inner products of random matrices and random quantum states---such as orbital inner products, expectation values, overlaps, and cyclic Bargmann invariants---are shown to follow from two underlying mechanisms: the diagonal of an induced random state is Dirichlet distributed, and the expectation value of a random pure state in a rank-one or two-by-two operator is a numerical shadow on an elliptical disk. For states induced by an environment of dimension $K$, the expectation value of any observable is a Curry--Schoenberg spline with each eigenvalue repeated $K$ times, and the vector of moments has an explicit density on a simplex; for a qutrit, the variance law is obtained in finite form. The overlap of two random qubit states attains its mode at its mean for every rotation-invariant ensemble, but for Hilbert--Schmidt qutrits the density at the mean has a strictly negative derivative, so mode and mean separate; for large environments, the centred overlap converges to a variance-gamma law rather than a Gaussian. For two noncommuting qubit observables, the joint law of the two standard deviations is derived for all $K$, and the probability of coming within a small distance of the optimal sum of variances scales as a power of that distance, with a different exponent when the Bloch axes are orthogonal. For three Haar-random qubit states, the exact density of the Bargmann invariant is given in terms of a complete elliptic integral, together with its local behaviour and elementary marginals. In every dimension, the probability that its real part is negative---certifying basis-independent coherence---is computed, along with all mixed moments. For cycles of arbitrary length, the invariant is shown to be driven by an exact three-parameter Markov chain, and the logarithm of its modulus obeys a law of large numbers and a central limit theorem.

papers.title: When Are Monomial Symmetric Polynomials Hard?
papers.abstract: For a partition $\boldsymbolλ = (λ_1,\ldots,λ_r)$ and $n\ge r$, the monomial symmetric polynomial is defined as $$m_{\boldsymbolλ}(x_1,\ldots,x_n) := \sum x_{i_1}^{λ_1} x_{i_2}^{λ_2} \cdots x_{i_r}^{λ_r},$$ where the sum ranges over all distinct monomials obtained by assigning the parts of $\boldsymbolλ$ to pairwise distinct variables. We establish an almost-complete dichotomy for the complexity of the monomial symmetric polynomials $m_{\boldsymbolλ}$: If a family of partitions contains polynomially many distinct parts, then the corresponding monomial symmetric polynomials (on sufficiently many variables) are VNP-complete. If the number of distinct parts is constant, the family admits polynomial-size circuits. Thus the only remaining gap concerns the intermediate regime where the number of distinct parts grows subpolynomially. As part of our proof, we use combinatorial properties of matching polynomials to establish VNP-hardness of the perfect matching polynomial for blow-up graphs; these are graphs with non-generic edge-weights that are obtained by "blowing up" a smaller graph. We reduce these matching polynomials to monomial-symmetric polynomials by combining classical techniques from algebraic complexity theory with structural properties of Sidon sets.

papers.title: Sharp quantum logarithmic Sobolev inequalities via semigroup interpolation
papers.abstract: We develop a semigroup interpolation method for sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities using spectral calculus and estimates of $\mathrm{Re}\langle\,Lx,x^2\rangle_2$, where $L$ generates an auxiliary symmetric quantum Markov semigroup. We apply the method to free groups and to crossed products of a finite von Neumann algebra $\mathcal N$ by $\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb Z_n$, for $n=2$ or $n\ge4$, when the action commutes with the semigroup on $\mathcal N$. In particular, the word-length generators on quantum tori and the Weyl word-length generators on $M_n(\mathbb C)$ satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with optimal constant $2$.

papers.title: Non-existence of Negative Weight Derivations of the Moduli Algebras of Isolated Weighted Homogeneous Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: Mather and Yau proved that the analytic isomorphism class of an isolated complex hypersurface singularity is determined by its dimension and its moduli algebra. Yau's conjecture asserts that the moduli algebra of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity over $\mathbb{C}$ has no nonzero derivation of negative degree. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses Varchenko\textquotesingle s theorem on the $μ$-constant stratum of an isolated weighted homogeneous singularity, also stated by M. Saito.

papers.title: The minimum number of vertices of a triangulation of $\mathbb{RP}^5$
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that every finite simplicial triangulation of real projective five-space has at least twenty-four vertices. Together with the construction of Guyer, Steinerberger, and Yang, this determines the minimum. A cup-product argument produces an induced subcomplex on sixteen or seventeen vertices. Transfer to the spherical double cover then imposes a covering condition on its lifted faces. In the sixteen-vertex case, a direct capacity bound excludes twenty-two vertices. For twenty-three vertices, a cochain extension argument reduces every relevant completion to one of 115 critical signed complexes; integer weights and exact covering certificates exclude all of them. The argument requires no assumption that the triangulation is combinatorial.

papers.title: Increased-Order Generalized Synchronization in Memristive Neurons: Analytical and Data-Driven Approaches
papers.abstract: We investigate increased-order generalized synchronization between four- and five-dimensional memristive Hindmarsh--Rose neurons, focusing on the selection and stabilization of the synchronization map. An analytical construction combines a prescribed nonlinear map with adaptive control, retaining the memristive switching contribution explicitly in the error dynamics. Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic synchronization under uniform strict dissipativity and yields a switching-independent decrease estimate outside an explicit error neighborhood. Numerical simulations exhibit error decay beyond the sufficient convergence conditions. A complementary data-driven construction uses next-generation reservoir computing to learn predictors from uncoupled full-state trajectories and an affine synchronization map through dynamical consistency. The resulting sampled-data controller achieves small residual tracking errors without access to the governing equations. Relative to a reference map within the data-driven framework, the learned map reduces median control effort approximately eightfold while improving tracking accuracy. These results connect synchronization-map selection with conditional convergence guarantees and reduced control requirements.

papers.title: An optimal inequality between nonlinear eigenvalues in convex sets
papers.abstract: Let $λ_p(Ω)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian in a bounded convex open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. We prove that $p\mapstoλ_p(Ω)^{1/p}/π_p$ is strictly decreasing, where $π_p^p$ is the first eigenvalue on the unit interval. Consequently, for $1<q<p<\infty$, the sharp upper bound for $λ_p(Ω)^{1/p}/λ_q(Ω)^{1/q}$ is $π_p/π_q$. This bound is not attained and is approached by slabs, resolving the conjecture on the supremum formulated in the plane by Parini (J. Convex Anal. 2017). The proof combines log-concavity of the first eigenfunction with a vector field constructed from the one-dimensional eigenfunctions. The endpoint limits recover the Hersch--Protter and reverse Cheeger (or Buser) inequalities.

papers.title: Photon production at Kepler escape threshold
papers.abstract: We obtain an exact closed-form total photon count for a prescribed Newtonian Kepler parabola, with a fully relativistic treatment of its radiation. We also obtain closed expressions for the angularly resolved photon spectrum and elementary expressions for the total radiated energy and momenta. The count is finite, scale-independent, and analytic in subluminal speed at closest approach. At large maximum rapidity $η$, $N\sim(7α/\sqrt6)η$, while $E\propto e^{3η}$ at fixed passage timescale: the radiation chiefly hardens. For slow motion at fixed coupling and closest distance, a nearby ellipse emits fewer photons but more energy and angular momentum per orbit. The hyperbolic photon count remains IR divergent arbitrarily close to threshold, while the count at the exact parabolic threshold is finite.

papers.title: Non-canonical Oscillator Representations of Orthogonal Lie Algebras and Pfaffian Varieties
papers.abstract: Associated varieties are fundamental geometric invariants in the study of infinite-dimensional representations of semisimple Lie algebras. Luo and Xu (2013) constructed a large family of infinite-dimensional irreducible representations of orthogonal Lie algebras by applying Fourier transforms to the natural oscillator representations. In this paper, we prove that the associated varieties of these irreducible representations are isomorphic to explicitly described coordinate linear sections of Pfaffian varieties. The modules are realized as spaces of polynomial solutions of transformed Laplace equations. We construct filtrations from weighted polynomial degrees and determine the annihilator ideals of the corresponding associated graded modules. The defining equations consist of linear coordinate equations, minors and quadratic Pfaffian relations. The even and odd orthogonal Lie algebras are treated separately. The associated varieties are viewed as reduced affine schemes over a field of characteristic zero. In each irreducible family with fixed Fourier parameters, the associated variety is independent of the grading parameter. When the two Fourier parameters coincide, the projectivizations in the even case are Grassmannians.

papers.title: A counterexample to Reich's fixed point problem
papers.abstract: This note provides a negative answer to the well-known Reich's problem in fixed point theory.

papers.title: Higher-order disorder correlations control reflected phonon counting statistics
papers.abstract: We investigate how structural correlations beyond the power spectrum affect phonon counting in a one-dimensional acoustic stack. An integer-thickness construction cancels the extensive leading backscattering term and leaves a finite-chain reflection amplitude determined by endpoint innovations. For symmetric independent innovations with unit variance and fourth moment $μ_4$, the normalized reflected-power second moment tends to $(μ_4+5)/4$. With vacuum environmental inputs, a two-phonon Fock input therefore gives an ensemble-averaged reflected factorial correlation $g^{(2)}=(μ_4+5)/8$. Two explicitly constructed ensembles with identical mean and complete two-point correlation function yield $g^{(2)}=3/4$ and $9/8$, placing their counting variances on opposite sides of the Poisson value. Conditional tensor averaging also gives a general fourth-order resistance-growth coefficient for arbitrary impedance contrast, including a positive higher-scattering contribution not recovered by shifting the lowest-order spectrum. Exact enumeration confirms the fixed-$N$, small-detuning limit and shows that increasing $N$ at fixed detuning produces a crossover governed by accumulated higher-order bulk scattering rather than convergence to the endpoint formula. Further calculations test bandwidth, thickness error, propagation loss and thermal background. The result concerns disorder-averaged pulse statistics; it neither creates nonclassicality from coherent input nor changes the conditional factorial correlation of an individually resolved passive sample.

papers.title: Prekosmic Grothendieck/Galois Categories
papers.abstract: We develop a theory on duality between groups and the categories of their representations, by providing an abstract characterization of such categories. The theory has two parallel formulations, each presenting a duality analogous to one of the two that were originally proposed by Grothendieck: the one between profinite groups and the abstract categories of their continuous representations on finite sets, and the other between affine group schemes over a field and the abstract categories of their finite-dimensional linear representations. In the present theory, groups and their representations are internal to a symmetric monoidal base category, with no finiteness condition imposed. The role of a fiber functor is played by a fiber point, an abstraction of the forgetful functor with its chosen adjoint. Over each base, a group determines the category of its representations equipped with the canonical fiber point, and a pointed abstract category determines the group that represents the presheaf of automorphisms of its chosen fiber point. These constructions yield mutually quasi-inverse equivalences of $(2,1)$-categories. By introducing change of base, we gather the dualities over individual bases into a single duality in each formulation. For a pointed abstract category, fiber points of the category are in perfect correspondence with torsors under the group associated to the chosen point. As an illustration of the theory, we reformulate the Galois theory of covering spaces for nonempty, path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected spaces.

papers.title: Directional Fineness for Radiant and Co-Radiant Sets: Separation and Quantitative Approximation
papers.abstract: A prescribed directionally fine family of cones yields separation and primal bipolar identities for closed radiant and co-radiant sets in real normed spaces. Positive levels of adapted positively homogeneous functions separate points from closed radiant sets, while a correction by the norm provides bounded radiant neighbourhoods for co-radiant separation. The resulting classes also calibrate radial thresholds and represent gauges and cogauges through strict separators. For convex directionally fine families, the separating generators can be chosen Lipschitz and superlinear, yielding convex separating superlevels. Closed co-radiant sets with compact direction sets admit finite relative outer approximations by positive superlevels of selected generators, with separation preservation and directional and bounded-section error estimates, without requiring continuity or boundedness of the radial profile. Superlinear generators yield a global residual error bound, exact penalization for Lipschitz objectives, recovery estimates, and convergence of bounded approximate minimizers. An explicit convex directionally fine axial family is available in every real normed space. Its norm-corrected functions realize separation and bipolarity without rotundity assumptions, while an axial recovery map improves the relative distance factor from $η/(1-η)$ to $η$. A three-ray production model illustrates the quantitative recovery estimates.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Level-Synchronized Tree Automata for Quantum Circuit Verification
papers.abstract: Reliable quantum computation requires methods for verifying quantum circuits. Level-synchronized tree automata (LSTAs) were recently introduced to represent sets of quantum states for this purpose. We study LSTAs along two axes relevant to verification: the complexity of their decision problems and the size of their representations under circuit operations. We prove that acyclic LSTAs have NP-complete nonemptiness and $Π_2^P$-complete language inclusion, and that general language inclusion is EXPSPACE-complete. We further prove inherent quadratic representation growth under individual quantum gates in a fixed qubit order, and give an adjacent-qubit reordering construction that preserves level synchronization. These results clarify the scope of applicability of the automata-theoretic toolbox for quantum circuit verification.

papers.title: Sharp Pointwise Error Estimates of Finite Element Methods for the Biharmonic Equation
papers.abstract: We prove sharp pointwise error estimates for finite element approximations of the clamped biharmonic equation on convex polygonal domains. For $C^1$-conforming elements, we establish $W^{2,p}$-stability for all $2\le p\le \infty$, together with best-approximation type estimates in $W^{1,\infty}$ and $L^\infty$. For the nonconforming Morley element, we derive optimal estimates in $W^{2,p}$, $W^{1,\infty}$, and $L^\infty$; in particular, the $L^\infty$-error is of order $O(h^2)$ without an additional logarithmic factor. The analysis is based on three ingredients: local energy estimates for conforming and nonconforming plate elements, a removal of the local $L^2$-error term in these estimates, and Hölder estimates for derivatives of the Green's function. These tools are combined with a dyadic decomposition argument for regularized Green's functions. The results remove logarithmic losses present in earlier pointwise estimates for fourth-order problems and yield sharp rates for classical plate elements such as the Argyris, Bogner--Fox--Schmit (BFS), Hsieh--Clough--Tocher (HCT), and Morley elements.

papers.title: Lucas recurrences and Lambert series in coprime double sums
papers.abstract: For the Lucas numbers $L_0=2$, $L_1=1$, and $L_n=L_{n-1}+L_{n-2}$, we obtain \[ \sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}}\frac{1}{L_{2n}L_{2m}L_{2(n+m)}}=\frac1{45}. \] This follows from the absolutely convergent identity \[ \sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}}\frac{q^{n+m}} {(1+q^n)(1+q^m)(1+q^{n+m})} =\frac{q^2}{(1-q^2)^2},\qquad |q|<1. \] We give a self-contained proof by local cancellation on the Calkin--Wilf tree, as a specialization of Hata's Farey-interval telescoping principle. Specializations yield a hyperbolic-cosine identity \[\sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}} \frac{1}{\cosh(nx)\cosh(mx)\cosh((n+m)x)} =\frac{2}{\sinh^2(2x)}, x>0\] and weighted sums for canonical second-order Lucas recurrences. Decomposing arbitrary positive pairs according to their greatest common divisor gives an unrestricted sum expressed by a Lambert series and the quasimodular Eisenstein series $E_2$. Conversely, Möbius inversion recovers the primitive identity from a double Lambert-series result of Cui, Kumar, and Singh.

papers.title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D
papers.abstract: Despite having an asymptotically optimal rate of convergence on convex quadratics, the acceleration of Polyak's heavy-ball method and a characterization of its dynamics within more general settings have remained long standing open problems. Recently, the work of Goujaud et al. [Math. Program. (2025)] made progress regarding acceleration in the context of smooth, strongly convex minimization: for a small enough inverse condition number, either the method does not accelerate on quadratics, or there exists a smooth strongly convex function such that heavy-ball cycles over the roots of unity. The constructed functions have two variables, thus leaving the question of acceleration over univariate functions open. In this work, we use a Fourier-based analysis to i) provide a proof for the non-acceleration of the heavy-ball method over the class of univariate smooth strongly convex functions. We also ii) provide a strict enlargement of the previous root-of-unity cycling region, with insights regarding the "fractional" sets of Goujaud et al. [arXiv:2502.19916], and iii) give a higher dimensional cycling instance which is not covered by root-of-unity cycling.

papers.title: The center conjecture for cyclotomic Hecke algebras and cohomology of quiver varieties
papers.abstract: For a quiver without edge loops, we construct an isomorphism from the cohomology of a Nakajima quiver variety with coefficients in an arbitrary field to the Jucys--Murphy center of the corresponding cyclotomic KLR algebra over that field. In affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, combining this with a dimension count shows that this Jucys--Murphy center coincides with the full center in characteristic $0$, when the characteristic does not divide $e$, and when the characteristic equals $e$. This follows from a geometric theorem showing that the sum of these cohomology rings is cocyclic as a module over an integral form of a loop algebra. As a consequence, we prove that the center of a cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type $G(r,1,n)$ with $q\neq 1$ over any field is generated by symmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements, and the same holds over any commutative domain in which $q-1$ is invertible. We also prove a generalization to the integral case of the conjecture of Krylov, Paegelow and Shlykov identifying the equivariant $K$-theory of the core of a Gieseker variety with the cocenter of the generic cyclotomic Hecke algebra, including the natural extension of this conjecture to positive characteristic.

papers.title: Identity crisis on tightly $C^{(2)}$-compact cardinals
papers.abstract: Bagaria and Goldberg asked if $κ$ being tightly $C^{(n)}$-compact implies $κ\in C^{(n+1)}$ for natural numbers $n\ge 1$? Usuba gave a negative answer for $n=1$. In this paper we give a negative answer for $n=2$.

papers.title: Refined proper descent for left completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces
papers.abstract: We refine the proper descent of Postnikov completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces to the dualizable world.

papers.title: On the isoperimetric profile in infinite dimensional pro-Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nontrivial compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric. On the compact pro-Lie group $K^{\N}$ we define a weighted variation by summing the distributional variations in its Lie group coordinates. We prove that all sublevel sets with bounded $L^1$-norm and weighted variation are compact in $L^1$ if and only if the coordinate weights tend to infinity. The proof gives a quantitative estimate for approximation by Haar averages over normal subgroups, illustrating that it is possible to apply a methodology which is typical of the geometric measure theory in a specific area of the topological group theory. The resulting perimeter is invariant under left and right translations and is preserved under pullback by quotient homomorphisms equipped with quotient metrics. Isoperimetric minimizers exist at every prescribed Haar probability. For the infinite torus, the compactness condition is equivalent to properness of a weighted length on its character group and to compactness of a Fourier multiplier's resolvent. Finally, we show that locally compact noncompact groups require an additional condition of tightness, in order to be treated as an appropriate generalization of the compact case.

papers.title: A sound pure type system with ranks as sorts and Type-in-Type
papers.abstract: We present a dependently typed pure type system that contains a circular axiom $s : s$ for a certain sort $s$ and is nonetheless strongly normalizing. Girard's paradox is avoided because our sorts are not closed under a $Π$-former: function types are placed in sorts according to their rank. Turns out that this system has a unique set of characteristics: it has similar normalization behaviour as STLC (so complexity of normalization is TOWER-complete) while at the same time allowing non-uniform representation of arbitrary elementary recursive functions; furthermore, it has a nontrivial set-theoretical model in ZF+GCH and allows to carry out nontrivial proof developments. Base normalization proof is surprisingly simple (modulo general metatheoretical properties of pure type systems) and has been fully formalized in vanilla Rocq (formerly Coq) without additional axioms.

papers.title: $\varepsilon$-$\mathcal{VU}$ spaces and approximate leaves\\ for sublinear composite functions
papers.abstract: Let \(h\) be proper, closed and sublinear, and let \(F\) be of class \(C^1\). The exact \(\mathcal{VU}\) calculus of the composite \(f=h\circ F\) is taken as known. This paper studies enlargements \(\bar\partial_\varepsilon h\subset\partial_\varepsilon h\) and the resulting \(\varepsilon\)-spaces of \(f\). Nested inclusions give one-sided Painlevé--Kuratowski limits of \(\mathcal{V}_\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon\) at points of the lineality space \(\mathcal{U}h(0)\). An additional transversality transfers those limits through \(F\); without it only the exact chain rule is available. Approximate leaves \(\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(x)=F^{-1}\bigl(F(x)+\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon h(F(x))\bigr)\) are inner semicontinuous under the nesting \(\mathcal{U}h(F(\bar x))\subset\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon h(F(x))\). For a polyhedral outer function the activity set freezes along the exact leaf for small \(\varepsilon\), so the dimension identity holds on that leaf and not necessarily in a full neighbourhood of \((\bar x,0)\). Partial smoothness of \(h\) relative to \(\mathcal{U}h(0)\) extends a known result from the origin to the lineality space; it is not used by the transfer theorems.

papers.title: On an open question about the equivalence of monotone maximality and surjectivity condition in $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces: Negative and partially positive answers
papers.abstract: In a Hilbert space, it is known that a monotone operator is maximal if and only if the \emph{surjectivity condition}, \ie its resolvent has a full domain, holds. This equivalence is an open question in a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space, knowing only that the surjectivity condition implies the monotone maximality. In fact, there have been three approaches to generalize the monotonicity from a Hilbert space into a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space $X$ --- \textbf{A:} the ones of dual space $X^{\ast}$, \textbf{B:} of linear dual space $X^{\diamond}$, and \textbf{C:} of tangent bundle $TX$. In this paper, we answer \emph{negatively} on the first two approaches by constructing counterexamples on an $\mathbb{R}$-tree. We then go on proving that the equivalence is \emph{affirmative} on the same $\mathbb{R}$-tree, without any assumption on the domain. Moreover, we show that the answer is still \emph{positive} in some other cases, through a flat slice principle that transfers Minty's principle from Hilbert spaces to flat convex subsets, and through Minty's principle on proper Hilbert-Hadamard spaces satisfying a convex half-space condition. The question of equivalence \emph{remains open} under the general setting with the tangential approach.

papers.title: A sharp lower bound for $h$-fold restricted sumsets of integers
papers.abstract: Let $A\subseteq[0, L]$ be a set of $k\geqslant 9$ integers such that $0, L\in A$ and $\gcd(A)=1$. Define the $h$-fold restricted sumset $$h^{\wedge}A=\{a_1+\cdots+a_h: a_i\in A,\ 1\leqslant i\leqslant h, \ \ a_i\neq a_j\ {\rm for}\ i\neq j\}. $$ In this paper, we prove that, for every $1\leqslant h\leqslant k-1$, we have $$|h^{\wedge}A|\geqslant h(k-h)-k+2+\min\{L, h(k-h)-\mathbf{1}_h\}, $$ where $\mathbf{1}_h=1$ for $h\in\{2, k-2\}$ and $\mathbf{1}_h=0$ otherwise. The bound is sharp for every $1\leqslant h\leqslant k-1$ and the cardinality threshold $k\geqslant 9$ cannot be decreased. We also give a lower bound for the union of two consecutive restricted sumsets in a cyclic group and characterize equality.

papers.title: Large Deviations in Switching Diffusion: Dynamical Condensation and Diffusivity BBP Transition
papers.abstract: We consider a Brownian particle with position $x(t)$ whose diffusivity changes at Poissonian switching times, with each new value drawn independently from a bounded distribution $W(D)$. Assuming $W(D)\sim C(D_{\max}-D)^ν$ near its upper edge, we study the large-deviation regime $x(t)\simeq yt$ with $y = O(1)$ at large times, far beyond the typical diffusive scale.
