For any $\varepsilon>0$, we also show \begin{align*} &\#\left\{n\leq x:1\leq \frac{P^+(n+1)}{P^+(n)}<1+\varepsilon\right\}\gg_\varepsilon \frac{x}{\log x}, \end{align*} which improves a previous result $\gg x(\log x)^{-50}$ due to S. Kim (2020).

papers.title: The Compactness Theorem for Enriched Logic
papers.abstract: The framework of enriched logic extends positive logic (also known as coherent logic) from sets to structures internal to a symmetric monoidal closed category $\mathcal{V}$. This framework was developed by Rosický and the second-named author. The main novelty of this logic is that the arities of the function and relation symbols are now objects in $\mathcal{V}$. We prove the compactness theorem for this enriched logic. That is, a set of $\mathcal{V}$-enriched sequents has a model (internal to $\mathcal{V}$) if every finite subset has a model. To achieve this, we define ultraproducts of enriched structures and prove enriched versions of Łos' theorem. We then develop some model-theoretic applications. We start with an enriched version of the model-theoretic method of diagrams, establishing a correspondence between homomorphisms whose domain is some enriched structure $A$ and models of the set $\operatorname{Diag}(A)$ of all enriched atomic formulas with parameters from $A$ that are true in $A$. Combining this with our compactness theorem, we prove amalgamation results, laying the foundations for enriched syntactic types (in the model-theoretic sense). We finish the paper with a collection of examples of $\mathcal{V}$ that our results apply to. Besides recovering the classical case when $\mathcal{V} = \mathbf{Set}$, these include many presheaf toposes, categories of monoid acts, the category of abelian groups and related additive categories, categories of (small) enriched categories, and the categories of posets and pseudometric spaces.

papers.title: A Generalized Half-Singleton Bound for List Decoding of Insertion/Deletion Errors
papers.abstract: We derive an upper bound on the rate of a linear code capable of list decoding from insertion and deletion errors. Subsequently, we show that a linear code can list decode from at most $n - \frac{L}{L+1}k + 1$ insdel errors with fixed list size $L$, and that this bound is strict when the code does not contain the all-ones vector. We also provide a simple construction of codes achieving the optimal rate for any given list size capable of correcting a single insdel error. All the results hold for linear codes over finite fields of size $q \geq 3$.

papers.title: Unconditional Quantum PAC Learning Advantage in the Large Error Regime
papers.abstract: We establish an unconditional super-polynomial separation between quantum and classical PAC learning of Boolean functions under the uniform distribution in the large error regime. For every advantage $λ(n) = n^{-ω(1)}$, we construct a concept class that a polynomial-time quantum learner learns to agreement $1/2+λ(n)$ with success probability at least $1-1/n^k$. The learner uses only quantum random examples and outputs a polynomial-size deterministic classical circuit. In contrast, no polynomial-time classical learner achieves agreement $1/2 + λ(n)/n^k$ with success probability greater than $1/n^k$, even with membership queries. To achieve this, we develop a nearly-optimal quantum learner that uses quantum random examples to produce a hypothesis achieving a prescribed correlation with an arbitrary Boolean function. The learner generalizes Fourier sampling from parity hypotheses to quadratic hypotheses. While standard Fourier sampling is insensitive to the sign of the correlation, we use interference to bias sampling toward positively correlated hypotheses. This is combined with a careful analysis of the resulting distribution to boost both the learner's success probability and its agreement with the target function. We believe that the resulting quantum learning algorithm might be of independent interest. Finally, although a robust quantum PAC learning advantage holds unconditionally in the large error regime, we note that an analogous separation between quantum and classical learning in the small error regime would imply that $\mathsf{NP} \nsubseteq \mathsf{BPP}$.

papers.title: Anticommuting Displacement Operators, Exact Pauli Algebras,and the Singlet State from the Oscillator Vacuum
papers.abstract: We give an explicit construction of a pair of anticommuting Weyl displacement operators for a harmonic oscillator and use bounded functional calculus to obtain exact dichotomic representatives of the Pauli algebra. Two independent oscillators provide commuting Pauli algebras for Alice and Bob. The standard singlet-sector projector, written entirely in terms of these bounded oscillator observables, is then applied to the two-oscillator vacuum. We show explicitly that the projected vacuum has nonzero norm, so its normalization is well defined, has the exact singlet correlations, and reaches the Tsirelson value $2\sqrt2$ for the usual Bell--CHSH settings. We also clarify that the construction generally realizes a singlet sector with multiplicity, rather than selecting a unique vector in the full oscillator Hilbert space, and we compare the construction with the older pseudospin approach to continuous-variable Bell tests.

papers.title: Harnack-type inequalities for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations
papers.abstract: We establish intrinsic Harnack inequalities for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations in the slow-diffusion range: \begin{equation*} (u^q)_t+ \operatorname{P.V.} \int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{|u(x, t)-u(y, t)|^{p-2}(u(x, t)-u(y, t))}{|x-y|^{N+sp}}\,dy=0,\quad s\in(0,1),\quad 0<q < p-1. \end{equation*}

papers.title: A configurational numerical viscosity for thermodynamically compatible finite volume schemes of compressible multiphase flows
papers.abstract: We consider the fluid subsystem of a variationally derived hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (HTC) model of compressible multiphase flows. Its total energy is in general not convex in the natural state variables, so a scalar numerical viscosity acting on them need not produce non-negative entropy. Reformulating the equations in terms of the volume fractions separates changes in the amount of each phase from changes in its intrinsic state. This guides the construction of a configurational numerical viscosity in phase variables, in which the energy is convex, while the scheme retains the structure of the HTC model. At the semi-discrete level, the new schemes satisfy: I) local conservation of the phase masses, the mixture momentum and the total energy; II) a cell entropy inequality whose production is non-negative face by face and phase by phase, with no convexity assumption in the evolved variables and no clipping; III) positivity of the partial densities and volume fractions under explicit time-step conditions; IV) exact preservation of contact equilibria; V) equivalence with a scheme for the density-weighted volume fractions. The key ingredients are: i) an exact decomposition of the jump of each phase across a face into a configurational part, dissipated with the material speed, and an intrinsic part, dissipated with the acoustic speed; ii) an exchange form of this dissipation between neighbouring cells, with non-negative weights; iii) a side-wise transfer of the dissipation to the evolved variables through the chain rule of each cell, which turns the energy defects into Bregman divergences of the single-fluid energies; iv) a thermodynamic correction of the reversible part built in the phase variables. Properties I)-V) are proved and verified numerically, including a shock tube in which the Rusanov viscosity produces negative entropy and a shock-water column interaction.

papers.title: On the complexification of $ q $-deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups
papers.abstract: For the quantised algebra of functions on a simply connected compact semisimple Lie group, we study the relationship between the primitive spectrum, topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on Hilbert spaces, and quantum holomorphic evaluations induced via the Drinfeld double. In terms of the Joseph stratification of the primitive spectrum, we prove a sharp dichotomy: primitive ideals in homogeneous strata always arise as kernels of topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on a Hilbert space, whereas those in inhomogeneous strata do not admit any such realisations. We further show that, unlike in the classical situation, quantum holomorphic evaluations typically fail to be topologically irreducible, and that their kernels do not determine the primitive spectrum. Finally, we describe the Iwasawa decomposition of the Drinfeld double in terms of polynomial functions, extending work by Podleś-Woronowicz for the quantum Lorentz group to all complex semisimple quantum groups, and clarifying the structure of quantum holomorphic evaluations.

papers.title: Electronic structure and optical properties of antiferromagnetic $3d$-oxides from a Wannier-localized optimally tuned screened range-separated hybrid functional

By comparing WOT-SRSH with established hybrid functionals, self-consistent quasiparticle GW, dynamical mean-field theory, and available experimental data, they demonstrate its ability to offer quantitative improvement in the description of fundamental band gaps, spin magnetic moments, photoemission, and optical spectra. These results establish WOT-SRSH as a promising framework for predictive studies of the electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of magnetic insulators.

papers.title: On Mbekhta's conjecture and pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: We give negative answers to Mbekhta's conjecture \cite[p.~261]{Mbekhta} and to a related conjecture on pseudo-B-Fredholm operators \cite[p.~202]{AZO}. A sufficient condition for pseudo-Fredholmness on Banach spaces is established. It yields a characterization on Hilbert spaces in terms of the closedness of $\cc(T)$, $\cc(T)+\qn(T)$ and $\Ran(T)+\qn(T)$, as well as characterizations of pseudo-B-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Weyl operators on Banach spaces. A counterexample on a separable Banach space shows that the three closedness conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness in general. We also construct two operators having the same analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and kernels and ranges of all powers, although only one is pseudo-Fredholm. Moreover, a semi-B-Fredholm operator on a Banach space need not be a direct sum of a semi-Fredholm operator and a nilpotent operator, answering the question raised in \cite[p.~113]{AznayKato2023}. Finally, the three closedness conditions in the Hilbert-space characterization are shown to be independent.

papers.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed. The proof compares homomorphisms from the tangent bundle to line bundles of negative degree with normal bundles of arithmetic fixed subvarieties. We describe these homomorphisms through coincident marked points and prove vanishing statements for their kernels. The comparison, together with integrality of Chern classes and the invariant theory of finite reflection groups, gives the nonexistence theorem without a Fano assumption on the GIT quotient.

papers.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
papers.abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.

papers.title: Regularity, depth and Serre depth of symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $I_c(G)$ denote its complementary edge ideal. In this paper, we study the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, the depth and Serre depth for $(S_{2})$ of the symbolic powers of $I_c(G)$. We derive explicit formulas for $\operatorname{reg} I_c(G)^{(k)}$ and $\operatorname{reg} I_c(G)^{(k)}/I_c(G)^k$ for every $k\geq1$, in terms of the number and the sizes of the connected components of $G$. As applications, we determine their asymptotic behavior, and completely characterize the symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals having linear resolutions. We then investigate the symbolic depth function $k\mapsto\operatorname{depth} S/I_c(G)^{(k)}$. We determine explicitly its values for $k=2,3,4$, and establish bounds for the asymptotic depth. More generally, for an arbitrary squarefree monomial ideal $I$, we compare the local cohomology modules of $S/I^{(k)}$ for different symbolic powers, and derive corresponding inequalities for the depth and the Serre depth. Applying this to complementary edge ideals, we obtain $\operatorname{depth} S/I_{c}(G)^{(t)}\geq\operatorname{depth} S/I_{c}(G)^{(k)}$ for $k\geq 2t-1$, despite the fact that the symbolic depth function need not be non-increasing. Finally, we characterize complementary edge ideals satisfying Serre's condition $(S_r)$, and determine the Serre depth for $(S_{2})$ of all symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals. In particular, we obtain combinatorial characterizations of Serre's condition $(S_{2})$ and of the Cohen-Macaulayness of $S/I_{c}(G)^{(k)}$ for every $k\geq 1$.

papers.title: Models of Arbitrary Sets
papers.abstract: There is a growing literature on arbitrary objects as other types of mathematical objects, besides particular mathematical objects. In this paper we study arbitrary sets in the context of ZFC set theory. An arbitrary object is one that is determined by a state space across which it varies and by its instantiations. We compare two semantic strategies. First, we analyse the possibility of modeling arbitrary sets using direct powers of a ZFC structure. This yields a natural setting, but one where Extensionality and, crucially, the full Separation scheme fail. Second, we consider structures composed of arbitrary sets using a direct power construction evaluated in a Boolean-valued semantics. Within this setting, we develop the cumulative hierarchy of arbitrary sets, arbitrary ordinals, cardinals, and filtrations of the structure of arbitrary sets. The final section develops a combinatorial interpretation in terms of independent assignments across a fixed state space. Its connection with the iterative conception is then discussed.

papers.title: Emergence of Correlations Between Records and Maximum in Random Time Series
papers.abstract: We compute exactly the covariance between the maximum $M$ and the number of records $K$ in a discrete time series of $n$ entries as a quantitative probe of the history leading to an extreme event. For continuous IID series, with a common probability distribution function (PDF) $p(x)$, we find the striking result that $M$ and $K$ are uncorrelated for any $n \geq 1$. We show that this independence is rather fragile and the covariance $C_q(n)$ between $M$ and $K$ becomes nonzero when $p(x)$ becomes discontinuous due to a delta-component at $x=0$ with an amplitude $0< q < 1$. This time series models the occurrence of dry days with probability $q$ in a precipitation time series when there is no rainfall. We show that there is an interesting shape transition at a critical value $q_c$ where the covariance $C_q(n)$, as a function of $n$, changes from monotonic ($q<q_c$) to non monotonic behavior (for $q>q_c$). We compute the critical strength $q_c$ exactly. Furthermore, for large $n$, we show that $C_q(n)$ decays as a power law, with an exponent that depends on the tail of $p(x)$. We then compare our theoretical predictions with real precipitation data from several weather stations across Germany, finding a very good agreement.

papers.title: The Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for p >= 11
papers.abstract: We show that the Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for all primes p >= 11. This improves on the recently announced result by OpenAI that V(4) exists at the prime 1009.

papers.title: Regular Additive Scalar Invariants of ${\mathcal N}=1$ Hyperbolic Spin Supertriangles
papers.abstract: We classify regular cyclic scalar invariants of non-degenerate hyperbolic ${\mathcal N}=1$ spin supertriangles which are additive under geodesic subdivision. After fixing the spin lift, the common-first gauge (introduced in earlier work by the second-named author and further developed here) gives a complete $3|4$ modulus of such supertriangles.. The space of additive scalar invariants is proved to have superdimension $3|1$: ordinary hyperbolic area in degree zero, two even generators in degree two, and one odd generator in degree three; the degree-one and degree-four sectors vanish. One degree-two generator is the fermionic first variation of body area, equivalently the nilpotent correction from ordinary body angle defect to super angle defect. The degree-three generator changes sign under reversal of the spin lift, while the other generators are fixed, so ordinary supertriangles carry only three even invariants.

papers.title: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
papers.abstract: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.

papers.title: Synthesis of the Transient Behaviour of Optimization Algorithms for Strongly Convex Objective Functions
papers.abstract: We study the transient behavior of first-order optimization methods for unconstrained minimization of smooth and strongly convex objective functions. These methods are modelled as linear systems over finite-time intervals embedded in feedback with the gradient nonlinearity. By characterizing the function class through discrete-time Zames-Falb integral quadratic constraints, we employ a robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ control framework to obtain convex semidefinite programs certifying tight worst-case bounds on the terminal distance to the optimizer. Building on the same formulation, we derive a convex synthesis procedure for a transient-optimal method that achieves the optimal finite-horizon bounds and guarantees error reduction over any prescribed number of steps. The framework naturally extends to delayed gradient measurements, enabling both transient performance analysis and synthesis of optimal algorithms under feedback delays.

papers.title: Multilevel Gaussian Processes with Applications to Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: We present a multilevel Gaussian process (GP) regression framework for approximating functions that are accessible only through a hierarchy of approximations of increasing accuracy and computational cost. One example is the response surface of a parametrized partial differential equation, where the hierarchy arises from the resolution of the numerical solver. Modeling level increments independently with Matérn-kernel GPs and allocating samples flexibly across discretization levels yields substantial computational savings over single-level GP regression. We derive $L^2$ convergence rates for the posterior mean and variance, accounting for maximum likelihood estimation of the marginal variance and for kernel misspecification. When increment regularity or solver cost is unknown a priori, an adaptive sequential-design algorithm with cost-adapted active learning criteria allocates samples across levels. We apply the surrogate to Bayesian inverse problems, for which Hellinger distance bounds between the true and approximate posteriors are known. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical rates and the resulting computational savings.

papers.title: A $\mathrm{GL}_3$ level analog of Selberg's result for $S(t)$
papers.abstract: Let $π$ be a spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newform of prime level $N$ and trivial central character, and define $S(t,π)=π^{-1}\arg L(1/2+\textrm{i}t,π)$. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,π)$, we establish an asymptotic formula for each fixed weighted moment of $S(t,π)$ as $N\to\infty$, for fixed $t>0$. Consequently, under the same weights, $S(t,π)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to a centered Gaussian distribution of variance $1/(2π^2)$. The key input is a weighted orthogonality formula derived from the Kuznetsov formula of prime level.

papers.title: Rough Stochastic Viscous Camassa-Holm equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish well-posedness results for the viscous Camassa--Holm equation driven by the additive Gaussian noise $(1-\partial_x^2)^{-η}ξ$, where $ξ$ denotes the space-time white noise and $η>-1/12$. This formulation includes spatially colored noise for $η>0$, space-time white noise for $η=0$, and rough noise for $-1/12<η<0$. More precisely, we establish a pathwise solution theory via approximation by equations driven by regularized noises. The main difficulty arises from the singular interactions between the nonlinear terms and the irregular stochastic convolution. By introducing suitable enhanced stochastic objects and applying paracontrolled techniques, we obtain local well-posedness for the full range $η>-1/12$. Furthermore, when $η>1/4$, we establish global well-posedness by deriving suitable energy estimates.

papers.title: Controlled PROP: Theory and Applications to Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Control is a fundamental concept in quantum and reversible computational models. It enables the conditional application of a transformation to a system, depending on the state of another system. We introduce a general framework for diagrammatic reasoning featuring control as a constructor. To this end, we provide an elementary axiomatization of control functors, extending the standard formalism of PROPs to controlled PROPs. As an application, we show that controlled PROPs facilitate diagrammatic reasoning for quantum circuits. In particular, they admit a simple and complete axiomatization involving at most three qubits, whereas in the standard PROP setting, completeness necessarily requires axioms involving arbitrarily many qubits.

papers.title: Solutions to the Fokker-Planck equation with time-dependent force and source in $\mathbb R^3$
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the global solutions of the kinetic Fokker-Planck (KFP) equation in $\mathbb R^3$ driven by a given external force $E=E(t,x)$ and an inhomogeneous source term $S_0=S_0(t,x,v)$. First, when $E$ and $S_0$ are sufficiently small in a suitable hybrid homogeneous Besov-Sobolev framework without any time-decay assumption, we establish the global well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in the hybrid homogeneous space $L_v^2(\dot B^{ {1}/{2}}_{2,\infty}(\mathbb R^3_x) \cap\dot H^N(\mathbb R^3_x))$ with $N\geq 3$. We further obtain the uniform stability of the Cauchy problem via semi-group theory and a refined energy method. Second, when both $E$ and $S_0$ are time-periodic of the period $T$, we show the existence of time-periodic solutions with the same period $T$ and their asymptotic stability as $t\to \infty$. Moreover, we derive the time-decay estimate of the perturbation around time-periodic solutions for initial data in $L^p$-norm with $ {3}/{2}< p \leq 2$. Finally, when both $E$ and $S_0$ are independent of $t$, we establish the existence of stationary solutions and their asymptotic stability. Our results provide a unified treatment of time-periodic dynamics and stationary states for the KFP equation with small force and source terms.

papers.title: Singular Stochastic Heat Equations with Fractional Memory
papers.abstract: We extend the paracontrolled distribution approach of Gubinelli, Imkeller, and Perkowski to singular stochastic heat equations with Caputo fractional time derivatives. By establishing Schauder estimates for the time-fractional heat flow and controlling history terms, we address the difficulties arising from temporal memory and the lack of the semigroup property. For the one-dimensional rough Burgers-type equation driven by space-time white noise with spatial dissipation \((-Δ)^σ\), we prove global well-posedness for \(σ\in(5/6,1]\) and \(ν\in(6σ/(12σ-5),1]\). For the heat equation with nonlinear multiplicative spatial white noise on the two-dimensional torus, we establish local well-posedness of renormalized solutions and an \(L^\infty\) blow-up criterion for every \(ν\in(0,1]\).

papers.title: Critical cusp cancellation and analytic response for a Bernoulli random interval map
papers.abstract: We show that the critical cusp exponent $β=-1/2$ admits $W^{2,1}$ invariant densities in an explicit family of expanding full-branch interval maps. The usual estimates exclude this exponent because two zero-order coefficients in the second derivative of the transfer operator are individually non-integrable. Their signed combination, however, contains the factor $β(2β+1)$ for a pure power cusp. We exploit its cancellation at $β=-1/2$ to prove a $W^{2,1}$ Lasota--Yorke inequality and a spectral gap for the explicit family. We also identify a separate obstruction caused by an interior cusp value. As an application, a small Bernoulli probability perturbation between two fixed maps has a stationary density that depends real-analytically on the perturbation parameter in $W^{2,1}$, with explicit formulas for all response derivatives.

papers.title: Nondimensionalization, Variational Inequalities and Uncertainty Quantification in a Morphoelastic Model for Burn Injury Healing
papers.abstract: Mathematical modelling of burn injury healing involves coupling biological processes with mechanical deformation, resulting in computationally stiff, nonlinear partial differential equations that severely limit the scalability of existing numerical solutions. We present a computational framework addressing these challenges. By nondimensionalizing the model and performing scaling analysis, we show that chemotaxis and inertia are negligible, permitting a quasi-static momentum approach. To enforce non-negativity constraints, we implement a Variational Inequality formulation using the Finite Element Method in FEniCSx, and verify it via numerical convergence studies and mass balances. We identify high-order parameter interactions, specifically equilibrium collagen density and signalling dynamics, as the primary drivers of solver stability. A sensitivity analysis of nearly four million simulations reveals that isolated parameter variations predominantly govern the maximum wound contraction. In contrast, higher-order interactions determine the timing of maximum contraction and the permanent contracture. However, no significant pairwise parameter interactions were found, suggesting that the model's behaviour is governed by higher-order interactions, highlighting the inherent complexity of the wound-healing process.

papers.title: Point Modules of Non-Connected Graded Algebras
papers.abstract: As part of a program to extend the homogeneous coordinate ring techniques of Artin-Tate-Van den Bergh to twisted graded Calabi-Yau (tCY) algebras, we initiate the study of point modules of non-connected graded algebras. We define weak and strong point modules of graded quotients of path algebras and compute their respective moduli stacks. We describe the relation between these point stacks and the classical point schemes in the connected graded setting, and we analyze the point stacks of several 2 and 3-dimensional tCY algebras.

papers.title: Whittaker Functionals for Exceptional Representations
papers.abstract: In the study of automorphic forms on covering groups, Kazhdan-Patterson gives a formula that determines when the Whittaker functionals of induced representations can be descended to exceptional representations. In this paper, first, following the original approach given by Kazhdan-Patterson and applying the block-compatible 2-cocycle of Banks-Levy-Sepanski, we fill in several details omitted in the original proof. Secondly, we compare the formula of Kazhdan-Patterson with that of McNamara and Gao, which is formulated in a more general setting.

papers.title: Rational torus equivariant spectra VII: the Cousin complex
papers.abstract: We explore the analogy between rational G-spectra for an r-torus G and sheaves over an r-dimensional scheme, in the context of the author's algebraic model for rational G-spectra. In particular, the resolution of the sphere of a virtual representation in the standard model corresponds precisely to the Cousin complex resolution of a line bundle. The tom Dieck splitting for the sphere of an actual respresentation corresponds to the collapse of the Cousin spectral sequence by degrees, and the the non collapse in other cases corresponds to familiar geometric behaviour.

papers.title: Stability and Error Estimates for Convolution Quadrature under Radial Symbol Bounds
papers.abstract: We develop stability and error estimates for multistep convolution quadrature (CQ) under general radial bounds on the Laplace symbol. Instead of the classical single-power condition $|F(z)|\leq M|z|^{-μ}$, we assume $|F(z)|\leq CΦ(|z|)$ and consider two classes of radial functions: monotone bounds satisfying a scaling condition and regularly varying bounds with locally bounded above and away from zero. For strongly $A(α)$-stable multistep methods, we derive approximation and stability estimates for the CQ weights, as well as error bounds for power-type inputs $g_β(t)=t^{β-1}/Γ(β)$ with $β>0$. These estimates explicitly retain the dependence on the memory law through the factor $Φ(t_n^{-1})$. The framework accommodates symbols whose behavior cannot be described by a global single-power. It also preserves slowly varying and multiscale factors that would be lost under a coarser power majorant. The theory is applied to fractional viscoelastic models, distributed-order operators, and logarithmic-power memory operators. Numerical experiments with backward Euler and second-order backward differentiation CQ confirm the expected temporal convergence orders for direct responses. Complementary evolution examples demonstrate the corresponding temporal behavior for smooth and nonsmooth initial data.

papers.title: Nonconvex Carnot Limit Shapes for Branching Random Walks on the Heisenberg Group
papers.abstract: We study a supercritical branching random walk on the discrete Heisenberg group driven by the four standard horizontal generators. Horizontal position has scale $n$, whereas the central coordinate records discrete area and has scale $n^2$. On the Galton-Watson survival event, we prove almost sure Hausdorff convergence, under Carnot scaling, of both the rescaled particle positions and the collections of enhanced ancestral paths. The path limit consists of area lifts of horizontal paths $ω$ satisfying $J_t(ω)\le t\logρ$ for every $t\in[0,1]$, where $ρ$ is the offspring mean. In contrast to the classical Euclidean case, the deterministic limit shape is nonconvex for every $ρ>1$. We identify its horizontal projection and interval vertical fibers, determine the saturated shape for $ρ\ge4$, and characterize the origin fiber below saturation by Wulff duality. A hyperbolic representation gives an elliptic integral formula for the Wulff area. The maximal central coordinate $Γ_ρ$ is nondecreasing and concave in $ρ$, equals $1/4$ for $ρ\ge4$, and satisfies $Γ_ρ=(\logρ)/π-(\logρ)^2/(4π) +O((\logρ)^3)$ as $ρ\downarrow1$. For fixed $1<ρ<4$, we obtain $M_n^Z=Γ_ρn^2+O(n^{3/2}\sqrt{\log n})$ almost surely. Above saturation the first correction is a random linear term; at $ρ=4$, under a finite second moment assumption, the deficit $Γ_4n^2-M_n^Z$ has order $n\log\log n$ in probability.

papers.title: Generalization of Navascués' $α$-fractal operator on lifted Sierpiński gasket
papers.abstract: The primary objective of the present article is to extend Navascués' class of $α$-fractal interpolation functions ($α$-FIFs) from a Euclidean domain to a non-Euclidean domain. Precisely, we consider the lifted Sierpiński gasket $\big(\widetilde{SG}\big)$, which is a subset of the first Heisenberg group equipped with a \textit{non-Euclidean metric} (popularly known as the Heisenberg metric), and demonstrate the existence of the class of $α$-FIFs in the continuous space on $\widetilde{SG}$. Subsequently, we derive certain conditions on the parameters so that the same class lies in the Hölder space on $\widetilde{SG}$. Next, we extend the theory of Navascués' $α$-fractal operator from the Euclidean space to the Heisenberg space, and we also report several properties of the same operator. Additionally, we discuss certain dimensional results of the graphs of the functions with respect to the Heisenberg metric besides the Euclidean metric. We also cover some of the dimensional preserving and the set-valued results corresponding to the dimension of the graphs of the functions.

papers.title: Endpoint Lorentz Inequality for Riesz Potentials with Respect to General Measures
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $α\in(0,n)$, and $μ$ be a locally finite nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that, for any $f\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$, \begin{align*} \|I_αf\|_{L^{\frac{n}{n-α},1}(μ)} \le C_{n,α} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} |Rf(x)|[Mμ(x)]^{1-\fracα{n}}\,dx, \end{align*} where $I_α$ is the Riesz potential, $R$ is the Riesz transform, $Mμ$ is the Hardy--Littlewood maximal function of $μ$, and $C_{n,α}$ is a positive constant depending only on $n$ and $α$. This answers a question posed by Bortz, Moen, Olivo, Pérez, and Rela, with the case $α=1$ already known, and extends Spector's optimal unweighted Lorentz inequality to general measures. As applications, we obtain a Lorentz estimate for curl-free vector fields, Sobolev--Lorentz and Hardy inequalities with respect to general measures, and an $A_1$-weighted Lorentz estimate with a sharp exponent of the $A_1$ characteristic.

papers.title: Minimal asymptotic \(g\)-adic bases from arbitrary partitions
papers.abstract: Let $g>h\ge2$ be integers. For a nonempty set $W\subseteq\N$, let $\mathcal F^*(W)$ denote the set of its finite nonempty subsets. Let $$A_g(W)=\left\{\sum_{f\in F}a_fg^f: 1\leq a_f \leq g-1,F \in \mathcal F^*(W)\right\},$$ and let $\N=W_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. We prove that $A=\bigcup_{i=1}^h A_g(W_i)$ is a minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$ for every such partition.

papers.title: Derivations and quasi-derivations of Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$
papers.abstract:
We compute the homogeneous derivations and the homogeneous quasi-derivations of the Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$, whose even part is the Block Lie algebra $\mathcal{B}(q)$. For every $q\in\mathbb C$, the space $\mathfrak{Der}_θ(S(q))$ is the direct sum of the inner derivations and an explicitly given finite-dimensional space of outer derivations; in particular, for $q
eq0$ a new odd outer derivation appears if and only if $q\in2\mathbb Z^*$. For $q\in\mathbb C^*$ we prove that $\mathfrak{QDer}(S(q))=\mathfrak{Der}(S(q))\oplus\langle \idangle$ if $q
otin\mathbb Z$, and that for $q\in\mathbb Z^{*}$ the superalgebra $S(q)$ has an infinite-dimensional space of nontrivial quasi-derivations, namely all graded linear maps with values in the center. For $q=0$ we also describe all homogeneous quasi-derivations: modulo maps with values in the center, they are spanned by $\id$, three further maps and infinite families of maps shifting the $\mathbb Z^2$-grading; in particular, $\mathfrak{QDer}(S(0))/\mathfrak{Der}(S(0))$ is infinite-dimensional. As corollaries, we obtain the complete description of homogeneous $δ$-derivations of $S(q)$, $q
eq0$, and prove that, in contrast with the Block Lie algebras $\mathcal{B}(q)$, the superalgebras $S(q)$, $q
eq0$, do not admit nontrivial transposed $δ$-Poisson superalgebra structures for any $δ
otin\{0,1\}$.

papers.title: Generalized Mock-Poisson Algebras: Constructions and Structural Properties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce generalized mock-Poisson algebras as a mock analogue of generalized Poisson algebras. We prove that $A_\ast^3$ is an ideal annihilated by both operations and that the quotient $A/A_\ast^3$ is a mock-Poisson algebra. We also show that the dimension seven is the smallest dimension in which a generalized mock-Poisson algebra need not be a mock-Poisson algebra. We give several constructions using derivations, anti-Zinbiel algebras, tensor products, and one-dimensional extensions. We study polarization and depolarization and characterize the corresponding admissible algebras. We prove that every finite-dimensional generalized mock-Poisson algebra over a field of characteristic zero is nilpotent. Finally, we describe representations in terms of semidirect products.

papers.title: Sample-Based Quantum Linear Solver and Bounds on Krylov-State Sampling
papers.abstract: To solve linear systems $Ax=b$, we propose a sample-based quantum linear solver combining quantum Krylov-state sampling with classical variational diagonalization. Rather than simulating the cost Hamiltonian $H_b(A)=A^\dagger(I-|b\rangle\langle b|)A$, we measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ generated by the original Hermitian operator $A$ in the computational basis. We then classically diagonalize the projected cost Hamiltonian to reconstruct an approximate solution. Using a representation of $A^{-1}|b\rangle$ as a linear combination of quantum Krylov states, we derive lower bounds on computational-basis sampling probabilities from solution amplitudes. We establish support-discovery guarantees for finite nonnegative-time grid sampling and signed-time sampling, which permits both positive and negative evolution times. The former bounds the maximum evolution time, whereas the latter improves ideal shot complexity at the cost of occasional long evolutions. For a condition-number bound $κ$ on $A$, a lower bound $β_L$ on the solution probability weight of each of $L$ target basis states, and failure probability $δ$, signed-time sampling achieves $O(κ^2β_L^{-1}\log(L/δ))$ shots, matching a worst-case lower bound up to constants within an evolution-only observation model in a specified parameter regime. Finally, we analyze the effects of finite-length qDRIFT compilation and circuit reuse on sampling and derive an infidelity bound for the reconstructed solution.

papers.title: Information-Geometric Blind Spots of Conformal Test Martingales
papers.abstract: Conformal test martingales (CTMs) are e-processes for sequentially testing exchangeability via p-values produced by a conformity function $A$. However, any distribution shift that preserves the push-forward $P\circ A^{-1}$ leaves the p-value distribution invariant, rendering it invisible to every CTM based on $A$. We formalise this blind spot through the \emph{$A$-equivalence class} $[P]_A$ and show that, for any target distribution $T$, there is a unique closest element $Q^\ast\in[P]_A$ in KL divergence---the \emph{$A$-cryptic I-projection}---with explicit density $q^\ast(z) = t(z)\,p_S(A(z))/t_S(A(z))$ and a Pythagorean decomposition into detectable and cryptic components. When $A$ is the Neyman-Pearson likelihood ratio, the cryptic component vanishes, connecting our result to optimal e-value design. We demonstrate the theory on high-dimensional image data by empirically constructing this I-projection. By conditionally resampling EMNIST letters to identically match the conformity scores of MNIST digits, we demonstrate that a distribution can be shifted to a disjoint support while leaving the test martingale mathematically blinded.

papers.title: A prime isoartinian ring that is not noetherian
papers.abstract: A right module is isoartinian (resp., isonoetherian) if every descending (resp., ascending) chain of submodules is eventually constant up to isomorphism, and a ring R is right isoartinian (resp., isonoethe- rian) if RR is isoartinian (resp., isonoetherian). Facchini and Nazemian proved that a semiprime right isoartinian ring is right noetherian if and only if it is right isonoetherian if and only if it has finite Goldie dimen- sion and that every commutative semiprime isoartinian ring is noether- ian. We construct, over an arbitrary field K, a (non commutative) prime (right and left) isoartinian ring that is neither right nor left noetherian.

papers.title: On the residual polynilpotence of tree products of groups with locally cyclic edge subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a non-empty class of nilpotent groups closed under taking subgroups, quotient groups, finite direct products, and unrestricted direct powers of the form $\prod_{x \in X}Y_{x}$, where $X \in \mathcal{N}$ and $Y_{x}$ ($x \in X$) are isomorphic copies of a group $Y \in \mathcal{N}$. Let also the symbols $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ and $\mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ denote the class of all torsion-free $\mathcal{N}$-groups and the class of polynilpotent groups such that $X \in \mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ if and only if $X$ has a subnormal series of length at most $k$ whose factors belong to $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$. We prove that if all free groups are residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups and $2 \leqslant n < \infty$, then any tree product of $n$ residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups with non-trivial torsion-free locally cyclic edge subgroups is residually a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n+1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group. In particular, all cyclically-pinched one-relator groups are residually finitely generated $(\mathit{Poly}_{3}\overline{\mathcal{N}}\mbox{}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-groups, where $\overline{\mathcal{N}}\mbox{}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ is the class of all torsion-free nilpotent groups. We prove also that any tree product of $n$ $\mathcal{N}$-groups with non-trivial torsion-free locally cyclic edge subgroups has a homomorphism onto a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n-1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group that is injective on all edge subgroups.

papers.title: Degenerated scalar balance laws: stability of the critical wave
papers.abstract: We consider scalar balance laws whith degenerated growth function at one infinity. It is the transition point between monostable and bistable waves. We find it admits smooth profiles arising from both settings, and show stability for the slowest of these waves, under a sign assumption on the flux. The presence of a characteristic point at infinity weaken the temporal decay: an exponential spatial localization loss is necessary to get algebraic temporal decay.

papers.title: Linearization in nonlocal elasticity via Gamma-convergence
papers.abstract: Linearization is a classical tool in continuum mechanics that connects nonlinear models of solids to their linear counterparts through the small-strain limit, as in the passage from finite to linear elasticity. Here, we study a nonlocal analogue of this limit process in the context of state-based peridynamics, starting from a class of models in nonlocal hyperelasticity subject to nonlocal Dirichlet boundary conditions. Recent formal calculations in the literature indicate that the linearized versions of these models are closely related to the widely used Eringen models. The main purpose of this note is to make this connection rigorous by establishing $Γ$-convergence of the associated energy functionals and a corresponding compactness result that together imply strong convergence of minimizers. Our proof relies on a local-to-nonlocal transfer argument that reduces the problem to a well-known local linearization result.

papers.title: Regularising Flows and Singular Fractional SDEs with Superlinear Dissipation
papers.abstract: We study stochastic differential equations driven by the fractional Riemann-Liouville process with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1)$, whose drift is the sum of a possibly distributional vector field $b$ and a smooth, one-sided Lipschitz, dissipative vector field $F$ with coercivity of order $k+1$ and polynomially growing derivatives. If $b \in \mathcal{C}^γ(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ for some $γ<1$ satisfying $γ>\max\{1-1/(2H),2-1/H\}$, and if $H+1/(k-1)>(1-γ)H/2$, we construct a solution by smooth approximation and prove uniqueness in a class defined through local comparison with the flow generated by the dissipative drift. We also establish quantitative temporal regularity and stability estimates. The proof combines a conditional decomposition of fractional Brownian motion, Malliavin integration by parts, uniform non-degeneracy estimates for the regularising flow, and the stochastic sewing lemma.

papers.title: Multiscale Quantum-Classical Simulation of Protein Autoproteolysis in a Million-Atom Membrane Environment
papers.abstract: Predicting chemical reactions in biomolecules is challenging because reactive centers are embedded within complex environments that strongly influence their energetics and mechanisms. Here, we present a hybrid quantum-classical workflow that combines molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and correlated wavefunction methods, tightly integrating CPUs, GPUs, and quantum processing units (QPUs) to enable simulations across multiple length and accuracy scales. We apply this approach to ADGRG1 autoproteolysis, a maturation reaction in an adhesion G protein-coupled receptor that has not previously been studied using correlated electronic-structure methods. Our simulations treat a biologically realistic system containing more than one million atoms, including the full-length uncleaved receptor embedded in an endoplasmic-reticulum membrane, while incorporating a 54-qubit IQM quantum processor and up to 1,200 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. These results demonstrate how quantum computers can serve as accelerators within scalable scientific workflows, extending correlated electronic-structure methods to biologically relevant systems.

papers.title: From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots
papers.abstract: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.

papers.title: Watanabe's Learning Coefficients in Item Response Theory
papers.abstract: We study the joint-parameter two-parameter logistic (2PL) model in item response theory, in which both item parameters and respondent abilities are treated as unknown fixed parameters. We first characterize its singular structure through the Fisher information matrix. The parameterization has an inherent scale indeterminacy; when all discrimination parameters are nonzero and the ability parameters are not all equal, its tangent direction is the only null direction and the quotient model is locally regular. We then classify the additional rank deficiencies caused by zero discrimination parameters and degenerate ability configurations. This classification separates the strata governed by a nondegenerate quadratic approximation from those requiring an analysis of higher-order product singularities. Under an asymptotic regime in which the numbers of items and respondents are fixed and the number of independent response matrices tends to infinity, we derive explicit local and global learning coefficients and multiplicities for every realizable true response distribution. The global formulas depend only on the true response probabilities, including cases in which some probabilities equal \(1/2\) or are constant across respondents. These results extend previous calculations restricted to nonzero true discrimination parameters and provide the quantities required for applying sBIC to the joint-parameter 2PL model. Key Words: item response theory; two-parameter logistic model; singular learning theory; learning coefficient; real log canonical threshold; Fisher information matrix; sBIC.

papers.title: Comparing word probabilities in finite groups
papers.abstract: We use results from extremal graph theory and analysis to compare word probabilities in finite groups. In particular, we show that the probability of satisfying the 2-Engel word admits a positive lower bound in terms of the probability that an element has order dividing 3. More generally, using a group removal lemma, we obtain analogous bounds for $x^m$-good words.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions in the Extended Agassi Model
papers.abstract: We investigate dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) in the extended Agassi model following sudden quenches of same level pairing ($Σ$), monopole-monopole ($χ$) and cross level pairing ($Λ$) strengths. Using exact diagonalization, we characterize the non-equilibrium dynamics through the Loschmidt echo and intensive return-rate function. Quenches across equilibrium phase boundaries produce cusp-like structures in the return rate that shows non-analyticities with increasing system size. Equilibrium finite size to large scaling identifies the $χ$-driven transition as a second order phase transition similar to mean-field, Dicke, and Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) models critical behaviour with the exponent of the order parameter $β\simeq 1/2$, while the $Σ$- and $Λ$-driven transitions are first order. We further characterize the associated dynamical singularities through a local scaling exponent $α$, with $α_χ\simeq 2/3$, $α_Λ\simeq 1/3$, and $α_Σ\simeq 3/2$ of all three parameters. The distinct scaling behaviours across the parameter channels show that dynamical criticality is not determined solely by the equilibrium order of the transition, revealing multiple dynamical scaling regimes. These non-analyticities are associated with the Fisher zeros of the Loschmidt amplitude, which cross the real time axis at critical times and the time derivatives of the return-rate function to characterize the order of DQPTs within the extended Agassi model.

papers.title: Time-optimal vaccination in state-dependent SIR models: a single switch criterion and numerical examples outside its regime
papers.abstract: In a susceptible, infected, and recovered (SIR) model with constant rates, a time-optimal vaccination policy has at most one switch from no vaccination to maximal vaccination. We allow the transmission and recovery rates $β(S,I)$ and $γ(S,I)$ to depend on the state. If $β+I\partial_Iβ>0$ and $G:=\partial_S(βS-γ)>0$ throughout the forward invariant state space, then every optimal control is bang-bang with at most one switch. The incidence condition allows the transmission coefficient to decrease with prevalence. The Pontryagin analysis shows that $G$, the sensitivity of per capita infected growth to the susceptible fraction, and the infected costate together determine the crossing direction of the switching function. We also prove existence of an optimal control, derive explicit a priori upper bounds on the eradication time and characterize the switching time by an optimization over one variable. For parameter sets that violate $G>0$, numerical optimization gives controls with two switches and smaller eradication times than the computed minima over the single switch family. These computations provide a reproducible numerical counterexample to an unrestricted single switch claim. In a prescribed parameter sweep satisfying $G>0$, delayed vaccination reduces the eradication time relative to immediate full vaccination by more than $1\%$ in $10.9\%$ of the cases, with a maximum reduction of $26.3\%$. In examples near this maximum, the delay increases peak prevalence by more than an order of magnitude and cumulative incidence more than fourfold. Hence minimizing eradication time does not in general minimize epidemiological burden.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations in 3D bounded domains under a new smallness condition
papers.abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations involving vacuum in a bounded domain with Navier-slip boundary conditions. It is shown that such a model admits a unique global strong solution provided the gradient of the initial velocity and the initial pressure deviation are suitably small in $L^2$. In particular, \textit{the smallness threshold depends only on the known parameters and the prescribed density bounds.} Our result provides a new analytical framework for the global well-posedness theory of the compressible Navier--Stokes equations.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Latent Representation Learning for Drag Coefficient Prediction of Irregular Particles
papers.abstract: Predicting the drag coefficient $C_\mathrm{d}$ of irregular particles requires representing their complex three-dimensional geometry in a form suitable for predictive models. Empirical drag correlations and many data-driven models represent particle geometry through a small set of hand-crafted shape descriptors. Geometric differences omitted by these descriptors are unavailable to the predictor. We propose a variational autoencoder-multilayer perceptron (VAE-MLP) framework that learns a latent representation directly from voxelized particle geometry. Geometry reconstruction and drag coefficient prediction jointly guide the learning of this representation. We compare VAE-MLP with a descriptor-based MLP (Descriptor-MLP) and established empirical correlations using CFD data for synthetic particle geometries at Reynolds numbers of 10--200. When the evaluated geometric variations are represented in the training data, the two learned models achieve comparable accuracy for regular ellipsoids, while VAE-MLP yields lower errors for irregular particles. When high-order surface perturbations are excluded from training, VAE-MLP achieves lower overall mean absolute relative error in all five training runs. At the strongest tested perturbation, the mean errors across these runs are 4.97% for VAE-MLP and 9.88% for Descriptor-MLP. These results support learning geometric representations directly from particle geometry to improve drag prediction for the irregular geometries and unseen surface perturbations examined here.

papers.title: Sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb{S}^n$
papers.abstract: We prove sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb{S}^n$, $n\ge 4$, for functions whose critical density $|u|^{2n/(n-2)}$ has zero barycenter, without any symmetry assumption. The Dirichlet coefficient improves by the optimal factor $2^{-2/n}$, while the coefficient of the $L^2$ term remains one. Equality holds precisely for constant functions. This establishes the sharp form of Aubin's improved Sobolev inequality in every dimension $n\ge4$.

papers.title: ParetoChat: An LLM-Based Interface for Interactive Multi-Objective Optimization
papers.abstract: Multi-objective optimization models are often deployed in settings where decision makers (DMs) must balance some conflicting criteria. In practice, however, stakeholders must translate their qualitative preferences between different criteria into numerical weights, priorities, or reference points required by optimization methods, which can be difficult to specify and interpret. This paper proposes \emph{ParetoChat}, an LLM (large language model)-based expert-agent interface for interactive multi-objective optimization. The agent translates natural-language user input into structured scalarization parameters, invokes an optimization system, presents candidate solutions, and iteratively elicits feedback. We describe a multi-agent architecture that separates input processing, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) expertise, solution presentation, and feedback processing. We then present a simulation study using an LLM-based DM agent and benchmark ParetoChat against interactive methods implemented in DESDEO, including reference-point and NIMBUS methods. The computational experiments on multi-objective binary knapsack and set-partitioning instances show that ParetoChat can guide the search efficiently toward solutions that match the DM's preferences. An application to historical courier-order assignment instances illustrates how users can explore objective extremes and intermediate trade-offs through natural-language requests. The results indicate that LLM agents may provide a practical interaction layer between business stakeholders and optimization tools.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Two Conjectures on Tangles in Matroid Minors
papers.abstract: We give counterexamples to two conjectures of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle concerning tangles in matroid minors. We construct a matroid $P_0$ with a tangle $\mathcal T$ of order seven. For each $i\in\{4,5,6,7\}$, let $\mathcal T_i$ denote its order-$i$ truncation. No proper minor $N$ of $P_0$ admits, for every such $i$, a tangle of order $i$ whose breadth equals that of $\mathcal T_i$, and $P_0$ is not weakly $4$-connected. We also construct a matroid $P_1$ with a tangle of order four and breadth six, but no internally $4$-connected minor of $P_1$ admits a tangle of order four.

papers.title: A note on the non-wandering dynamics in the $n$-fold symmetric products
papers.abstract: We construct a homeomorphism on a compact metric space whose non-wandering set consists of a single fixed point, while the induced map $F_n(f)$ possesses infinitely many (non-fixed) non-wandering points.

papers.title: Typical representations of admissible type I algebraic supergroups
papers.abstract: We study typical representations of an admissible type I algebraic supergroup $G$. We prove that, for a dominant weight $λ$, the induced supermodule $H^0_G(λ)$ is simple if and only if $λ$ is typical and the induced module $H^0_{G_{\mathrm{ev}}}(λ)$ for the even subgroup $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$ is simple. We establish equivalences between typical blocks for $G$ and blocks for $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$, and give a projectivity criterion for Kac modules over every Frobenius kernel. For connected $SpO(2\ell|2)$ over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic, we classify all simple projective supermodules over Frobenius kernels.

papers.title: Zagier's 2-3-2 formula for multiple Eisenstein series
papers.abstract: We prove a multiple Eisenstein series analogue of Zagier's formula for the multiple zeta values $ζ(2,\ldots,2,3,2,\ldots,2)$. The multiple Eisenstein series identity contains correction terms given by derivatives of odd Eisenstein series. Using the Goncharov coproduct and Brown's motivic version of Zagier's formula, we show that the normalized difference has rational Fourier coefficients. We then use the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-structure and a modularity criterion of Yu to prove the identity by induction.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of weak solutions to the Serrin-critical $p$-Laplace equation
papers.abstract: We classify isolated singularities of nonnegative weak solutions to the Serrin-critical quasilinear Lane-Emden equation $-Δ_p u=u^{\frac{n(p-1)}{n-p}}$ in $B_1\setminus\{0\}$, where $1<p<n$, $Δ_p$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian operator and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We prove that either the origin is a removable singularity or $u$ satisfies $\lim_{x\to0}|x|^{\frac{n-p}{p-1}}(\log\frac1{|x|})^{\frac{n-p}{p(p-1)}}u(x)=[\frac{n-p}{p}(\frac{n-p}{p-1})^{p-1}]^{\frac{n-p}{p(p-1)}}$. This extends the result of Aviles (Comm. Math. Phys. 1987: 177--192) from the semilinear case $p=2$ to the full range $1<p<n$, without assuming radial symmetry. We develop a new BV-based argument for weak solutions. We also give a direct construction of positive radial singular solutions with the same asymptotic behavior.

papers.title: Discrete time crystals and classical logic gates in coupled open Dicke models
papers.abstract: We investigate the dynamics of coupled discrete time crystals (DTCs) in the coupled Dicke model or Dicke dimer (DD) with dissipation. By numerically simulating the mean-field dynamics of the system, we show that coupling two DTCs decreases their oscillation amplitude following a transient relaxation period. For sufficiently strong coupling, the coupled DTCs become unstable, resulting in the system relaxing towards the normal phase (NP). We demonstrate that the relaxation time diverges near the critical coupling strength, suggesting a continuous phase transition. Using the truncated Wigner approximation (TWA), we explore how the dynamics are affected by the introduction of quantum fluctuations. We also consider a scenario in which an NP is briefly coupled to a DTC, seeding the NP to transform into a DTC that is either synchronized or anti-synchronized relative to the DTC. We investigate the robustness of this phenomenon in the presence of noise. Using these results, we propose a scheme to perform NAND and NOR operations with three DTCs by sequentially coupling the input and output sites. We identify the parameter regimes in which the logic gate architecture remains valid, and investigate how the protocol is affected by the presence of quantum fluctuations.

papers.title: Arithmeticity of critical $L$-values for Hilbert-Siegel modular forms in the left half plane and $s = 1$
papers.abstract: For a cuspidal automorphic representation $π_f$ generated by a Hilbert-Siegel modular form $f$ and a Hecke character $μ$ with parallel signature, we show the arithmeticity of critical $L$-values of the standard $L$-function $L^S(s,π_f, μ)$ twisted by $μ$ in the left half plane. As a consequence, we show the arithmeticity at $s=1$ under the assumption that there exists a nonarchimedean place $v$ such that $π_v$ is unramified and $μ_v$ is ramified.

papers.title: Stieltjes-generated moment functionals and orthogonality: a transfer principle and an image theorem
papers.abstract: We study the orthogonality induced by Stieltjes derivatives from the point of view of ordinary polynomial moment functionals. If \(g\) is a derivator and the Stieltjes monomials \(g_{x_0,n}\) are linearly independent, the map \(Φ(t^n)=g_{x_0,n}\) is an isomorphism of differential algebras onto the ordinary polynomial algebra, and the intrinsic \(\star\)-bilinear form on \(g\)-polynomials is the pull-back of a single ordinary moment functional \(\mathcal L\). The object of interest is therefore not a new polynomial algebra but the functional generated by the derivator, and our main theorem determines exactly which functionals occur. Let \(c_-\) and \(c_+\) be the increments of the continuous part of \(g\) on the two sides of the centre, and let \(A\) and \(B\) be the multisets of jump sizes to its right and to its left. Then \(\mathcal L\) is Lebesgue measure on \([-c_-,c_+]\), plus an endpoint derivative functional governed by the elementary symmetric functions of \(A\), plus an absolutely continuous left tail whose density is the survival function of a sum of independent exponentials with means in \(B\); the positions of the jumps disappear. Every quadruple \((c_-,c_+,A,B)\) occurs and is recovered from \(\mathcal L\), so the fibres are described exactly, and \(\mathcal L\) is representable by a positive measure precisely when \(|A|\le1\). A weighted lattice extension, in which the transported moments are the factorial moments of the weight, is treated separately.

papers.title: Liouville theorems for $-Δ_{m,g}u=λe^u|\nabla u|^q$ in the full range of gradient exponents
papers.abstract: We study the equation \[ -Δ_{m,g}u=λe^u|\nabla u|^q \] on complete, connected, noncompact Riemannian manifolds of dimension $n\ge2$ with $\Ric_g\ge0$. For every $m>1$, $q\in\mathbb R$ and $λ>0$, we prove that every positive $C^1$ weak solution is constant when $q>0$, while no such solution exists when $q\le0$. For $q>m$, we derive a local gradient estimate independent of the solution by Nash--Moser iteration, which leads to automatic boundedness and resolves the question raised by Lu and Zhu~\cite[Remark~1.6(B)]{LZ}. For $m-1<q<m$, we use an auxiliary function and a divergence inequality to extend the Liouville result beyond the range covered by existing gradient-inequality methods. The remaining cases are treated by suitable changes of variables and integral estimates. The conclusions also extend to real-valued solutions bounded below.

papers.title: The geometric exceptional set for Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the geometric exceptional set in Manin's conjecture for smooth Fano threefolds. We prove that every adjoint rigid surface with $a$-invariant one on a non-product smooth Fano threefold is normal. This yields a description of the geometric exceptional set in terms of the higher-$a$ locus, anticanonical conics, and del Pezzo fibrations. Zariski density arise only from the latter two contributions. For del Pezzo fibrations, we construct a finite collection of parameter covers which controlling the associated breaking maps. We classify their low-genus components for general smooth Fano threefolds yielding examples with potentially Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets in $22$ of the $105$ deformation families. Extending Batyrev-Tschinkel's example, we construct Fano fourfolds with quartic del Pezzo fibrations and an explicit Fano threefold with two degree-six del Pezzo fibrations, all with Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets. For this threefold, the original form of Manin's conjecture fails on every non-empty open subset for every anticanonical height.

papers.title: Hemicompactness and the $k_ω$-property of free topological vector spaces
papers.abstract: For a Tychonoff space $X$ we consider the vector space $E(X)$ with basis $X$ endowed with one of the following topologies: the weak topologies $L_b(X)$ and $L_p(X)$ generated by $C_b(X)$ and $C(X)$, the free locally convex space $L(X)$, the free locally $r$-convex space $L^{(r)}(X)$ ($0<r\le1$), the free locally pseudoconvex space $L^{(0)}(X)$, and the free topological vector space $V(X)$. We prove that $L_b(X)$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is finite; that for every vector topology between $L_p(X)$ and $L^{(0)}(X)$ hemicompactness is equivalent to $X$ being countable with all compact subsets finite; and that $V(X)$, as well as the free topological groups $F(X)$ and $A(X)$, are hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact. In particular, $V([0,1])$ is hemicompact, while $L([0,1])$ and $L_p([0,1])$ are not. We also describe when these spaces are $k_ω$-spaces: $L_b(X)$ and $L_p(X)$ only for finite $X$, and $L^{(r)}(X)$, $0\le r\le1$, only for countable discrete $X$.

papers.title: Spectral Schwarz Lemmas and Parallel Obstructions to Metric Comparison
papers.abstract: In this paper, we characterize when comparison of contracted Chern curvatures implies comparison of Hermitian bundle metrics with the same constant on compact Hermitian bases. If the curvature contraction of the reference metric is semipositive, this implication holds for every Hermitian metric if and only if the kernel of this contraction contains no nonzero subbundle parallel with respect to the Chern connection of the reference metric. The equality terms of a $C^2$ spectral truncation identify the parallel summand on which comparison can fail, without regularity assumptions on the curvature kernel. We also establish a sharp operator estimate, with a constant independent of the bundle ranks, for holomorphic bundle maps on complete Kähler bases under curvature bounds and bounded base-map energy density. Smooth Schatten moments give global control without a separate boundedness assumption on the bundle map. Finally, we obtain rank bounds and conditions for vanishing on compact Hermitian bases from directional curvature traces over fiber subspaces. For higher-dimensional subspaces, these conditions allow mixed signs on individual fiber lines.

papers.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension four
papers.abstract: We present an exhaustive, coordinate-free, and self-contained classification of four-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. In dimension three, classification schemes frequently exploit Bryant's classical exterior duality isomorphism $Λ^2\mathfrak{g} \cong \mathfrak{g}^* \otimes Λ^3\mathfrak{g}$, which reduces the Jacobi identity to an elegant linear algebraic condition on a single $3\times 3$ matrix. We explicitly demonstrate that this accidental isomorphism breaks down in dimension four due to the dimensional mismatch $\dim Λ^2\mathfrak{g} = 6 \neq 4 = \dim(\mathfrak{g}^* \otimes Λ^4\mathfrak{g})$, transforming the Jacobi identity into a non-linear system of 16 quadratic constraints on 24 structure constants. To overcome this geometric obstruction without relying on brute-force polynomial elimination, we employ an intrinsic Lie-theoretic reduction: the Levi--Malcev decomposition isolates the non-solvable sector into direct products with three-dimensional simple ideals, while the solvable sector is classified by anchoring the structure to its nilradical $\mathfrak{n}$, which is an intrinsic characteristic ideal. For codimension-one nilradicals ($\dim\mathfrak{n} = 3$), the problem is reduced to classifying outer derivations of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the Heisenberg algebra $\mathfrak{h}_3$ under the action of the automorphism group modulo global rescaling and central translations. For two-dimensional nilradicals, the structure is resolved via maximal abelian sub-algebras of $\mathfrak{gl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ lacking nilpotent elements. Complete proofs are supplied for all reductions, precise moduli parameter ranges are established to eliminate redundancies, and an explicit isomorphism dictionary is provided bridging our structural models with classical tabulations in mathematical physics.

papers.title: A cubulation of the associahedron using a torus-equivariant degeneration of the brick variety
papers.abstract: We describe a mixed subdivision of the $(n-1)$-dimensional Loday associahedron into $(n-1)!$ maximal cells which are combinatorial cubes, and we show that the face poset of this subdivision is isomorphic to the face poset of the subdivision of the $1\times 2\times \dotsb \times (n-1)$ box into unit cubes. More generally, we describe mixed subdivisions of generalized associahedra into pieces which are Minkowski sums of Bruhat interval polytopes. Our subdivisions arise from a torus-equivariant embedded (in a product of flag varieties) degeneration of brick varieties into reduced unions of products of Richardson varieties. The subdivision of Loday's associahedron allows us to `embed' the 1-skeleton of the permutahedron in the boundary of the associahedron.

papers.title: Perron-Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for regular inhomogeneous random graphs
papers.abstract: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and regular compact type kernels. Let $C_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u\,dμ=1$, and put $α=\int u^2\,dμ$ and $β=\int u^3\,dμ$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $ρ$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $ρ(1)=1$ and $\logρ(t)=\frac{α^2}{2β}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L < \infty$, $C_t(k,r)=w_rβ^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}ρ(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At $t_n=1+λn^{-1/3}$, these asymptotics yield local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollobas-Janson-Riordan models satisfying projective quadratic regularity. After rescaling component sizes by $β^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $αβ^{-2/3}λ$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)μ(dx)$. For every regular countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.

papers.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension one, two and three
papers.abstract: We present an exhaustive, self-contained, and coordinate-free structural classification of real Lie algebras of dimensions one, two, and three up to isomorphism. In dimensions one and two, the classification is governed entirely by the derived ideal and elementary derivation theory. In dimension three, we develop the classical exterior duality isomorphism $Λ^2\mathfrak{g} \cong \mathfrak{g}^* \otimes Λ^3\mathfrak{g}$ pioneered by Bryant and Milnor, which reduces the quadratic Jacobi identity on the $3 \times 3$ structure matrix $C = S + \hat{a}$ to the linear orthogonality relation $S \cdot a = 0$, where $a = \frac{1}{2}χ$ is the trace covector. We systematically bifurcate the three-dimensional category into unimodular ($a = 0$) and non-unimodular ($a \neq 0$) sectors, completely recovering the nine classical Bianchi isomorphism classes (Bianchi types I through IX) alongside their continuous moduli invariants. Furthermore, we establish the Levi--Malcev decomposition for low dimensions, compute the exact minimal representation dimension $μ(\mathfrak{g})$ via Ado's Theorem by constructing explicit matrix realizations in $\mathfrak{gl}(μ, \mathbb{R})$, and formulate a deterministic, coordinate-free decision algorithm for algebra identification.

papers.title: A Label Noise Robust Algorithm for Graph Data using Neighborhood Label Distribution
papers.abstract: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have demonstrated exceptional performance on graph-structured data. However, their success heavily relies on the availability of clean labels, an assumption that often fails in real-world scenarios. The learnability of GCNs is intrinsically linked to the neighborhood structure of nodes, making it critical to understand how this structure changes in the presence of label noise. In this work, we investigate how the neighborhood label distribution of a node changes under label noise. We mathematically derive that label noise smooths this distribution, which inherently increases its entropy and severely decreases interclass distinguishability. To address this challenge, we propose Leave-one-out Entropy Node Screening (LENS), an end-to-end framework that identifies noisy nodes by measuring the reduction in neighborhood entropy when a specific node is removed. LENS further incorporates a relabeling mechanism to recover and preserve valuable feature information instead of entirely discarding the identified noisy nodes. Crucially, the end-to-end computational overhead of LENS is remarkably low. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our algorithm achieves state-of-the-art node classification accuracy while executing an order of magnitude faster than existing noise-robust approaches.

papers.title: Hypergraphs of Low Degree Without Independent Transversals
papers.abstract: For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and every integer $b\ge 2$, we construct a finite vertex-partitioned $k$-uniform hypergraph with blocks of size $b$ and no independent transversal. We show that the maximum number of edges meeting a block is $\left(\frac{(k-1)^{k-1}}{k^k}+O_k(b^{-1})\right)b^k,$ while the maximum vertex degree is $\left(\frac{(k-2)^{k-2}}{(k-1)^{k-1}}+O_k(b^{-1})\right)b^{k-1}$. This shows that the known bound on the number of edges meeting a block is asymptotically sharp even when the leading constant in the maximum vertex degree tends to zero, which answers a problem of Groenland, Kaiser, Treffers, and Wales. By blowing up the same construction, we further obtain for arbitrarily large $n$, there exists a $k$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ blocks, each of size at least $n$, and $Δ(G)<\left(1-\frac1k\right)^{k-1}n^{k-1}$, but with no independent transversal. This gives a negative answer to a problem of Haxell and Wdowinski.

papers.title: Rigorous verification of period-doubling bifurcations in maps
papers.abstract: We present a computer-assisted approach for proving period-doubling bifurcations in one-parameter families of maps $x \mapsto f(x,λ)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We solve a square augmented system, called the period-doubling map, whose unknowns are the fixed point, the parameter, the right eigenvector attached to the eigenvalue $-1$, the left eigenvector with its eigenvalue, and the vector which describes the center manifold to second order. A contraction argument gives a solution close to a numerical approximation, at which the Jacobian is invertible. The determinant of this Jacobian factors into a simple expression, so that it is nonzero exactly when $1$ is not an eigenvalue and $-1$ is a simple eigenvalue crossing the unit circle transversally. Apart from the sign of the cubic normal-form coefficient, computed afterwards, it remains to check with Gershgorin disks that no other eigenvalue lies on the unit circle. The method is applied to a $10$-mode Galerkin projection of the Kot--Schaffer growth-dispersal model, for which we prove a supercritical period-doubling bifurcation.

papers.title: Quantum Tsallis Entropy Estimation: Near-Optimal Bounds and High-Precision Improvements
papers.abstract: Estimating statistical properties of probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistics and theoretical computer science. We develop quantum algorithms for estimating the $q$-Tsallis entropy $\mathrm{H}_q^{\mathrm{Tsa}}(P) =\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n p_i^q-1}{1-q}$ when $0<q<1$, given purified quantum query access to a distribution $P$ on $[n]$. When $0<q\leq \frac{1}{2}$, we provide a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\rbra{\left(\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\frac{1}{2q}}}$, which is optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. When $\frac{1}{2}<q<1$, we introduce a two-stage simultaneous probability estimation procedure, yielding a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{n^{\frac12+\frac{1}{2q}}}{\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2q}}}+\frac{n^{1-q}}{\varepsilon}\right)$, which improves the result given by Chen et al. (ICALP 2026) when $\varepsilon=O\rbra{n^{1-2q}}$.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of Bloch wall for dispersive Landau-Lifshitz equation
