papers.abstract: We consider the Bloch wall stationary solutions to the dispersive Landau-Lifshitz equation with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI). First, we establish a dichotomy for the orbital stability and instability depending on the value of a coupling constant. Then, under symmetric perturbations, we prove that the Bloch wall is asymptotically stable in the energetically favorable regime.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotics for the Lovász number of random circulant graphs
papers.abstract: We study the LOVÁSZ number of dense random circulant graphs generated by independent Bernoulli bits indexed by cyclic distances. Although only $O(n)$ independent random inputs determine $O(n^2)$ globally dependent edge indicators, we prove sharp expectation asymptotics along all odd orders, including composite orders, with leading constant one. This resolves a conjecture posed for random circulant graphs in 2025. The proof combines an exact Fourier reduction and complementary duality with a positive interior smoothing that reveals a nonlinear random fixed-point equation. To analyze this equation under the strong dependence of the distance-bit model, we construct canonical tree fields, establish growing-degree Gaussian approximations through polynomial comparison and Wick/Hermite expansions, and transfer the resulting approximation back to the original sign model. A deterministic residual estimate together with an explicit exceptional-event integration yields the sharp expectation asymptotics.

papers.title: Rational Area Profiles of Regular Polygons Cut by Two Congruent Diagonals
papers.abstract: Two congruent diagonals of a regular hexagon cut it into four regions whose areas are all rational multiples of the area of the hexagon. We determine when this phenomenon occurs in a regular $n$-gon. For every regular polygon cut by two intersecting congruent diagonals, neither of which is a diameter, we classify all unions of the four resulting regions whose areas are rational fractions of the total area. The hexagon is the only configuration in which all four regions are simultaneously rational. One of the two regions on the axis of symmetry is rational in exactly five sporadic configurations, with $n=6,18,30$, whereas the other region and the adjacent two-region unions belong to infinite families with simple geometric explanations. The two lateral regions have rational area ratios in exactly two configurations, with $n=6$ and $n=12$. The proof reduces each area ratio to a trigonometric quotient, bounds its rational values by norms in cyclotomic fields, and settles the remaining equations using Myerson's classification of equal products of two sines and the Poonen--Rubinstein classification of a three-sine-product equation.

papers.title: Ricci pinching on complete Kähler manifolds with nonnegative bisectional curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that a connected complete Kähler manifold of complex dimension at least two with nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature and uniformly pinched Ricci curvature is compact or flat. This removes the Euclidean volume growth assumption from the flatness theorem of Liu and Ni \cite{LiuNi} for uniform Ricci pinching. We first construct a Lipschitz plurisubharmonic function with finite total Monge--Ampère mass by solving a global Bellman equation. Weighted estimates for a holomorphic canonical section then give a finite top Ricci integral. Ricci pinching implies that the Ricci form belongs to $L^n$, and its Hodge heat evolution has zero top integral by a Stokes argument and scalar heat decay. \par\noindent\textit{Keywords.} Kähler manifolds, Ricci pinching, nonnegative bisectional curvature, Bellman equations, Monge--Ampère mass.

papers.title: An Erdős-Pósa theorem for induced packings of even cycles
papers.abstract: We show that for every graph $G$ and every positive integer $k$, $G$ contains either $k$ vertex-disjoint even cycles with no edges between distinct cycles, or a set of $O(k^2\log k)$ vertices whose closed neighborhood meets every even cycle of $G$. Moreover, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that outputs one of the two outcomes. As an application, we show that every $K_{1,t}$-free graph containing no induced packing of $k$ even cycles has tree-independence number $O(tk^2\log k)$, with a corresponding decomposition computable in polynomial time.

papers.title: Encodings and Node Architecture: Lessons from the Fault-Tolerant Distributed Transversal Fanout
papers.abstract: An encoding choice specifies the quantum error-correcting code used to encode logical qubits at a given node. Different encoding choices may differ in the number of physical qubits, the number of encoded logical qubits, the code distance, and the available fault-tolerant operations. We study different encodings for a distributed transversal fanout operation and look at its implications on node architecture. Our experiments suggest that an encoding with higher distance, even if requiring more ebits, can yield a lower logical error rate for distributed operations, and that ``upgrading'' an encoding prior to distributed operations and having a cache, as part of node architecture, for qubits can be useful for distributed operations.

papers.title: On the tradeoff between robustness and geometric accuracy in adversarial training
papers.abstract: For non-parametric binary classification in the presence of an adversary, we prove an optimal quantitative estimate for adversarial classifiers controlling geometric accuracy, as measured by the Hausdorff distance to the Bayes classifier, in terms or their robustness, as encoded by the adversarial budget $\varepsilon$. This rigorously shows that robust classifiers sacrifice at most $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ or $O(\varepsilon)$ in accuracy, depending on the regularity of the underlying Bayes classifier. In contrast to prior work on the incompatibility of robustness and accuracy over low-complexity hypothesis classes, our work shows that high-complexity hypothesis classes allow for robust classifiers with precisely quantified accuracy. Our results apply for adversaries determined by any norm on Euclidean space and in both the infinite and finite data settings.

papers.title: Quantum-Assisted Unambiguous Discrimination of Pure States with Robustness Bounds
papers.abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum-classical framework for the unambiguous discrimination of pure states by combining the noisy intermediate-scale quantum semidefinite program solver (NSS) with the reciprocal-state representation. In NSS, a given semidefinite program (SDP) is represented within a subspace spanned by chosen ansatz states, with the required quantities estimated using quantum circuits, and the resulting optimization is performed classically. This makes NSS naturally applicable to discrimination problems involving circuit-prepared states, as finding a discrimination measurement can be formulated as an SDP. By choosing the discriminated states themselves as the ansatz and exploiting the reciprocal-state representation, the general matrix-variable NSS formulation is reduced to an optimization over N scalar variables, where N is the number of discriminated states. The resulting formulation reduces the number of optimization variables and positive-semidefinite constraints compared with the original NSS formulation. We further establish robustness guarantees against Gram matrix estimation errors, including a rescaling procedure that guarantees a valid positive operator-valued measure (POVM) under bounded perturbations. The resulting bounds quantify both the deviation in average success probability and violations of the no-error condition using only the estimated Gram matrix, its SDP solution, and a characterized perturbation bound, without access to the ideal Gram matrix. Numerical simulations validate the derived robustness bounds and characterize finite-shot scaling. We also perform experiments on IBM quantum hardware to estimate pairwise overlaps, and then evaluate the performance of the resulting POVMs.

papers.title: Riemann problem for the isentropic Cargo-LeRoux system with extended Chaplygin fluids
papers.abstract: This study deals with the Riemann solutions of the isentropic Cargo-LeRoux system of conservation laws along with an extended Chaplygin fluid model and a generalized equation of state that captures nonlinear compressibility and non-ideal fluid behavior. It is shown that in the vanishing pressure limiting case, the Riemann solution yields a delta shock and a vacuum state. Delta shocks form when mass concentrates due to vanishing pressure, while vacuum states emerge in the rarefaction-dominated regions. These wave patterns are crucial in modeling real-world problems like discontinuous and multi-phase astrophysical fluid flows, underwater explosions, and combustion fronts.

papers.title: Type I estimates for the Kähler-Ricci flow II
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish geometric consequences of our Type I scalar curvature estimate for finite-time solutions of the Kähler-Ricci flow on compact Kähler manifolds. We prove a uniform global diameter bound and a Type I diameter bound for every fibre of finite time holomorphic contraction. These estimates yield Gromov-Hausdorff convergence to a unique compact metric space homeomorphic to the normal Kähler space determined by the limiting cohomology class. We also establish a local partial $C^0$ estimate for the normalized flow and show that the tangent shrinkers are normal complex analytic varieties with log terminal singularities.

papers.title: Improved explicit Burgess-strength bounds for composite moduli
papers.abstract: Consider the character sum $S(M,N)=\sum_{n=M+1}^{M+N}χ(n)$ for a non-principal Dirichlet character $χ(n)$ to a (possibly composite) modulus $q$. Burgess proved that $S(M,N)\ll N^{1/2}q^{3/16+\varepsilon}$, for any $\varepsilon>0$. This was made explicit by Jain-Sharma et al., but only for moduli $q\geq \exp(\exp(9.594))\approx 8.03\times 10^{6373}$. We prove a stronger result that holds when $q\geq 1.627\times 10^{19}$.

papers.title: Enumeration of small vertex-transitive directed strongly regular graphs
papers.abstract: We find the 728 vertex-transitive directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(v,k,t,λ,μ)$ where $1 \le v \le 39$ and $k < v/2$ and $0 < t < k$. A table with parameters and automorphism groups and some additional data is given.

papers.title: Integer Parameter Shifts in One-Variable Restrictions of Lauricella's $F_C$
papers.abstract: We construct rational functions of the coefficient index for one-variable restrictions of Lauricella's function $F_C$ at arguments related by cube roots of unity, with arbitrary integer differences among the lower parameters. We express the product coefficients in each residue class as these rational functions times the coefficients of Henrici's known triple product. We obtain finite sums of ordinary ${}_8F_7$ functions whose lower parameters have positive real part, with each summand multiplied by a nonnegative integer power of the variable, and give an explicit formula when the first of three equal lower parameters is increased by one, together with bounds for the polynomial degrees and number of summands. We interpret the expressions for the three residue classes by taking limits of the entire summands when upper and lower parameters approach singular values together. We prove that the Taylor series has radius of convergence exactly $1/4$ whenever all original lower and upper parameters avoid nonpositive integers, without assuming integer differences among the lower parameters.

papers.title: Unconditional Bounds for Two, Three and Four Consecutive Moderate Gaps between Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.abstract: We prove unconditional positive-proportion results for consecutive moderate gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function. More precisely, for every fixed \(0<c\leq 1/4\), the lower asymptotic densities, normalized by \(N(T)\), of the occurrences of two, three, and four consecutive gaps, each of length at least \(2πc/\log T\), are at least \(0.3450014\ldots\), \(0.1812517\ldots\), and \(0.0175021\ldots\), respectively. Here, zeros are ordered by ordinate and counted with multiplicity, and \(N(T)\) denotes the number of nontrivial zeros with ordinates in \((0,T]\). These bounds address the corresponding cases of a question of Gonek and Sahay. The proof combines the methods of Alpöge--Furman and Lamzouri with local spectral estimates and cluster counting.

papers.title: Approximation and extension theorems for normal affine toric varieties
papers.abstract: We study approximation and extension problems for holomorphic maps from Stein spaces to normal affine toric varieties, continuing the work of Lärkäng and Lárusson. Normality allows us to obtain twisted factorizations for arbitrary holomorphic maps from factorial complex spaces, including degenerate maps. This yields approximation and extension theorems under weaker cohomological assumptions. We also prove a simultaneous approximation and extension theorem under an additional codimension condition on the inverse image of the singular locus and a cohomological condition on the union of the interpolation submanifold and the approximation set. Finally, an explicit example with target $\{w^2=uv\}\cong\mathbb{C}^2/\{\pm1\}$ shows that simultaneous approximation and extension can fail even when the relevant cohomological obstructions vanish. Thus normality alone does not recover the full approximation and interpolation property of Oka manifolds.

papers.title: Bounded Leaf Volumes and Analytic Quotients of Singular Holomorphic Foliations
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation of dimension $k$ on a compact Kähler manifold $M$ of dimension $n$. Suppose that the volumes of its regular leaves are uniformly bounded, $\dim(Sing\mathcal{F})<k$, and the union of the leaf closures meeting $Sing\mathcal{F}$ has finite $2k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. We prove that the quotient by chains of intersecting leaf closures is a normal compact complex analytic space of dimension $n-k$. The quotient map is proper and holomorphic, with connected fibers. The proof uses Bishop's theorems, Remmert and Stein extension, Barlet's cycle space, and Stein factorization. Away from the images of separatrices, the quotient has local charts given by finite holonomy groups. Examples show that these images need not coincide with the singular set of the quotient, and that bounded leaf volumes alone do not imply Hausdorffness. In codimension one, Malgrange's theorem makes the separatrix measure assumption automatic when $codim(Sing\mathcal{F})\geq 3$.

papers.title: Signed dual graphs and face spectral gaps of Cayley 2-complexes
papers.abstract: We construct a weighted signed dual multigraph for the Cayley $2$-complex of a finite presentation and represent its $\ell^2$ face Laplacian as a signed graph Laplacian with a diagonal potential. We prove that the face spectral gap above the kernel vanishes for the Baumslag--Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(1,m)$, $m\ge2$, using explicit finitely supported face chains. Our main vanishing theorem gives the same conclusion for every finitely presented amenable group with ordinary first Betti number at least two.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Common Spanning Forests under Color Refinement
papers.abstract: We study the common spanning structure of connected finite simple graphs that are indistinguishable by uniformly initialized color refinement. We prove that any two such graphs with common cyclomatic number $r\ge2$ contain isomorphic spanning forests with at most $r-1$ components. This bound depends only on $r$ and is sharp for every $r\ge2$. We also determine the maximum, over all such graph pairs without restricting their order, of the minimum edge symmetric difference under vertex bijections: it is exactly $4(r-1)$.

papers.title: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
papers.abstract: For each $α\in(0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous planar iterated function system of similarities satisfying the strong separation condition, whose attractor $E_α$ has positive finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure and, for all sufficiently small $δ>0$, satisfies $\sup_{0\leθ<π}H^1(π_θ(N_δ(E_α)))\lesssim_α(\logδ^{-1})^{-α}$. The defining system depends only on $α$ and is fixed at every scale. For these same sets, we prove the sharp analytic capacity law $γ(N_δ(E_α))\asymp_α(\logδ^{-1})^{-1/2}$ as $δ\rightarrow0$. Consequently, each $E_α$ satisfies the quantitative Vitushkin comparison $\operatorname{Fav}(N_δ(E_α))\lesssim_αγ(N_δ(E_α))^{2α}$ for every $δ\in(0,1)$. These comparisons are superlinear for $α>1/2$, with exponents arbitrarily close to the optimal upper limit two for this class of self-similar sets. A completely specified sixteen-map system gives $α=53/100$ and comparison exponent $53/50$. Inspired by Falconer's Venetian blind constructions, the projection argument combines exact collinear cylinder subfamilies, quantitative distribution of word orientations, and a cover indexed by first successful symbolic blocks. The rotation parameters are explicit powers of a real algebraic number, linking the construction to simultaneous Diophantine approximation. The capacity estimate follows from the curvature characterization of analytic capacity and a telescoping inequality for cylinder masses.

papers.title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
papers.abstract: The physics-informed neural network (PINN) faces significant challenges when solving compressible multi-medium flows, including the inability to locate interface positions, poor approximation of discontinuities, and difficulty in handling high-pressure-ratio problems between media with large stiffness differences. To address these issues, we propose PINN with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition (PINN-LPCDD), a framework that incorporates the sharp interface method (SIM) into PINNs for solving compressible multi-medium flows. Firstly, we design separate sub-networks for each medium with learnable parameters to automatically learn interface positions, so that the domain decomposition is physically consistent, and the contact discontinuity at the interface is naturally sharp. Secondly, the Euler equations with artificial viscosity are solved to enhance robustness when handling problems involving shock waves. Lastly, the scaling invariance of the Euler equations is exploited to facilitate the solution of high pressure ratio problems. Numerical experiments on air-air, air-helium, air-water, and air-R22 problems demonstrate the acceptable accuracy of the proposed method in simulating multi-medium flows.

papers.title: Triangle-free Rank--Ramsey graphs from ordered incidence lifts
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ with adjacency matrix $A_G$ and a coefficient field $\mathbb K$, put $ρ_{\mathbb K}(G)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb K}(A_G+I)$. We answer the triangle-free Rank--Ramsey existence question of Beniamini, Linial and Shraibman. For every order $n$, we construct a triangle-free graph $H_n$ such that, simultaneously over all coefficient fields, $$ ρ_{\mathbb K}(H_n)=\bigl(4(2/3)^{3/4}+o(1)\bigr)n^{3/4}, $$ with an error uniform in the field. The graphs can be chosen Hamiltonian for all sufficiently large $n$. Our method combines ordered layers of point--line incidence flags with a common low-dimensional endpoint space. We determine the exact real rank, independence number and chromatic number of the affine lifts. For all triangle-free complete incidence lifts, we obtain a sharp two-term lower bound for complete incidence lifts, with sharpness witnessed by projective-plane incidence graphs over suitable coefficient fields. We also establish a third-order estimate and stability near equality. On the same explicit graphs, both the Lovász number and minimum semidefinite rank exceed the prescribed Boolean-matrix rank by polynomial factors. Thus neither parameter has a universal constant-factor upper bound in terms of complement rank. We determine Shannon capacity in the short-layer range.

papers.title: New lower bounds for binary constant-weight codes from prescribed-automorphism search, and two quantum codes meeting their upper bounds
papers.abstract: We give explicit binary constant-weight codes that raise the lower bounds on $A(n,6,w)$ in eight cells of Brouwer's table, all now listed there. The first round (9 October 2026) gave four values: $A(27,6,11)\ge 19305$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24453$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 18642$ and $A(28,6,9)\ge 11154$, together with an explicit $A(24,6,12)$ code of 5566 words, now in the table's list of lost codes. The second round (14 October 2026) gave seven values, listed in the table since 15 October 2026: $A(29,6,10)\ge 27183$, $A(29,6,11)\ge 42042$, $A(29,6,9)\ge 14781$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 19110$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24804$, $A(28,6,9)\ge 11388$ and $A(27,6,13)\ge 27783$, three of which replace first-round values. Every code is a union of orbits of the semilinear affine group $\mathrm{AΓL}(1,27)$, its index-2 subgroup, or $\mathrm{AGL}(1,23)$, acting on all but at most two coordinates. The orbits were chosen by maximum-weight independent set search on the orbit conflict graph: branch and bound in the first round, iterated local search in the second. Each code was checked by two separately written programs over all pairs of words and was regenerated from its generators and orbit representatives. We also report two qubit stabilizer codes, $[[20,11,4]]$ and $[[43,32,4]]$, which raise the lower bounds of 3 listed at codetables.de to the listed upper bound 4.

papers.title: Compact Toeplitz Operators and the Geometry of Fixed-Radius Averages
papers.abstract: We characterize compact Toeplitz operators with bounded complex-valued symbols on the Bergman space of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain with $C^2$ boundary. For any fixed $R>0$, the operator $T_f$ is compact if and only if the Euclidean-volume averages of $f$ over Bergman geodesic balls of radius $R$ tend to zero at the boundary. This answers Zhu's fixed-radius question affirmatively on the unit ball. On the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$, $n\ge2$, averages over products of Bergman discs of fixed radii characterize compactness, whereas averages over genuine Bergman geodesic balls need not. For every sufficiently small fixed radius, we construct a bounded real-valued symbol, smooth in the domain, whose geodesic-ball averages tend to zero along every sequence approaching the boundary, while its Berezin transform converges to a positive value along one such sequence. Boundary scaling reduces the strongly pseudoconvex case to a uniqueness problem for fixed-radius ball averages on complex hyperbolic space. We prove the required uniqueness theorem under a sharp decay condition expressed in terms of a Busemann height function.

papers.title: Solving the Tikhonov Regularization of the Total Least Squares Problem by matrix simultaneous diagonalization via congruence
papers.abstract: We are concerned with solving the Tikhonov regularization of the total least squares (TRTLS) which minimizes a sum of a quadratic fractional function and a nonnegative penalty quadratic form. If the penalty is nonsingular, the problem is attained and has been solved efficiently. However, if the penalty is singular, the problem becomes much more complicated, it may not be attained. In this paper we explore the property of simultaneously diagonalizable via congruence of matrices to make a change of variables and transform the problem into one of three tractable formats. Each of which is then thorough analyzed.

papers.title: Quantum approximate stochastic combinatorial optimisation
papers.abstract: Two-stage stochastic combinatorial optimisation concerns discrete decisions made before all relevant information is known. An initial decision is made; once uncertainty is resolved, it can be adapted to the realised scenario, at a cost. The aim is to find the initial decision that minimises the upfront cost plus the expected cost of optimal adaptation. The first-stage decision problem is often NP-hard, and computing the expected minimum recourse cost can be $\#\mathrm{P}$-hard for a single first-stage candidate. We introduce Quantum Approximate Stochastic Combinatorial Optimisation (QASCO), a variational quantum-walk ansatz that coherently incorporates scenario-dependent recourse into its dynamics to search over first-stage decisions without explicitly evaluating expected minimum recourse costs. We demonstrate QASCO for MaxCut with stochastic edge weights, obtain a circuit with polynomial per-layer gate complexity, and study the ansatz via exact state-vector simulation. Across the instances considered, QASCO concentrates amplitude more effectively on stochastic-optimal first-stage decisions than a previously proposed two-stage QAOA construction. We further show that the ansatz can be calibrated using a depth-independent number of parameters and applied to unseen instances without further circuit-parameter optimisation, including joint decision--scenario--recourse spaces spanning more than $2^{32}$ configurations. Under a query-cost model, comparison with the tested classical heuristics using sample-average approximations of the expected minimum recourse cost shows that QASCO more reliably reaches globally optimal first-stage solutions while requiring fewer cut evaluations. These results show how to incorporate scenario-dependent recourse into the ansatz dynamics, providing a general framework for variational quantum walks in two-stage stochastic combinatorial optimisation.

papers.title: Overtake and the recursive-line equality for second-order Zarankiewicz numbers
papers.abstract: We study two questions about the second-order Zarankiewicz numbers. The first is the recursive-line equality $z_2(m,n)=z_{RL}(m,n)$, known to hold in every computed case and conjectured in general. The second, here called \emph{overtake}, is the strict inequality $z_{2A}(m,n)>z_2(m,n)$ between the second-order augmented number and the second-order number. Both are governed by the number $H_{\mathrm{limited}}(m,n)$ of unoccupied cells in a limited extremal configuration. We prove that the first increase $z_2\to z_2+1$ already costs three unoccupied cells, forcing a unit of one-edge deficit, and the cell identity then bounds the excess $z_{2A}-z_2$ by $\lfloor(H_{\mathrm{limited}}-1)/2\rfloor$. In particular, when the recursive-line hole count is at most two, no overtake occurs. We conjecture the sharp budget $\lfloor H_{\mathrm{limited}}/3\rfloor$ and that $H_{\mathrm{limited}}\ge5$ is the threshold for an overtake. In the computed range $n\le7$, no overtake occurs at any order, the sole exception being the known case $(4,4)$. The recursive-line equality $z_2=z_{RL}$ is verified at every order in the range where both values are determined; the orders at which it remains unsettled are $(12,4)$ and $(14,4)$ at width four, $(11,5)$ at width five, and $(8,7)$ at width seven.

papers.title: Continuity of biaccessibility dimension for polynomials
papers.abstract: For a polynomial $f$ of degree $d\geq 2$, its biaccessible set $B(f)$ consists of angles whose external rays are smooth and land at a point receiving at least two smooth external rays. We prove that the function $f\mapsto {\rm dim}_H(B(f))$ is continuous on the entire space of degree-$d$ polynomials. Therefore $(\log d){\rm dim}_H (B(f))$ gives a continuous extension of classical core entropy from the postcritically finite case to all polynomials of degree $d$.

papers.title: Chirality-resolved imaging of spin waves with a quantum spin
papers.abstract: Spin waves carry their propagation direction in the handedness of their circularly polarized stray field, a property inaccessible to scalar magnetometers. In the Damon-Eshbach surface wave of an in-plane magnetized film, the dipolar field above the film rotates with a handedness fixed by the direction of travel. The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre in diamond is an intrinsic polarization analyser: a right-handed field about the NV axis drives one spin transition, and a left-handed field drives the other, in both the ground and the excited state. Here, we exploit the two excited-state transitions, which lie inside the spin-wave band of yttrium iron garnet (YIG), as a pair of chirality channels and image Damon-Eshbach waves in both directions. Because reflection from an etched boundary reverses the handedness, the incident and reflected waves appear as two lines in one spectrum and are imaged separately. In the ground state, the same rule applies, and the selected field drives Rabi oscillations, a route to chirality-selective control of the NV spin by magnons. Reading the two channels gives the direction of a spin wave at one point, without a phase reference. This advances chirality-resolved quantum sensing and provides insight into chiral spin-wave dynamics.

papers.title: Geometric multigrid preconditioners for unfitted discretisations of the de Rham complex
papers.abstract: We propose two families of multigrid preconditioners for unfitted finite element discretisations of the Riesz maps of the de Rham complex, in H(grad), H(curl) and H(div), stabilised by cell aggregation. The first is a geometric multigrid method applied directly to the unfitted operators, on a hierarchy of background meshes that share the same boundary representation. Its smoothers are star patches built on the aggregated mesh, so that each patch captures the kernel of the stabilisation. The second is a multilevel auxiliary-space preconditioner that combines a patch smoother localised around the cut cells with the body-fitted problem on the active mesh, which is in turn solved by a non-nested geometric multigrid method. Both are used as building blocks of block-diagonal preconditioners for the mixed Hodge Laplacians. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on geometries with a controlled cut fraction and on general geometries, show iteration counts that are robust with respect to the cut configuration, the mesh size and the number of levels. We also report results for higher-order discretisations, weakly imposed Dirichlet boundary conditions and a face-based stabilisation.

papers.title: The Source of Data Value: Consumer Disclosure, Access Design, and Platform Monetization
papers.abstract: Digital marketplaces increasingly earn revenue from transaction commissions and seller-facing data services. Sellers may purchase data to increase revenue or avoid competing with an informed rival. We examine how consumer disclosure rights shape these motives and the platform's incentive to provide data. We develop a game-theoretic model of a commissioned platform, two differentiated sellers, and privacy-sensitive consumers. Data generates value through bilateral sales-revenue gains and competition threats arising from asymmetric access. Under mandatory collection, the platform can monetize defensive adoption, even when bilateral personalization reduces seller revenue. Under voluntary disclosure, anonymous purchasing and strictly positive privacy costs make unilateral disclosure unattractive in the baseline. Exclusive access thus yields no usable information, restores sellers' no-data rejection payoffs, and eliminates defensive fees. Profitable provision therefore requires nonnegative bilateral revenue gains. Under full fee extraction, sellers retain their no-data net profits. This revenue alignment does not guarantee welfare gains: additional transactions may benefit consumers, whereas segmentation in an already covered market can raise anonymous prices and reduce welfare. Capping anonymous offers at their no-data benchmark protects individual consumers and limits positive-mass provision to the transaction-creation region. Extensions consider access choice, heterogeneous privacy costs, imperfect identification, and limited contractual credibility. Platforms should evaluate data services based on both bilateral-use and seller-rejection outcomes, and sellers should distinguish revenue-enhancing from defensive investments. Regulators should distinguish equal-access rules from effective consumer control and monitor pricing in anonymous channels.

papers.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_2^7$
papers.abstract: We prove that a nonempty subset of the binary vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ is spectral if and only if it tiles $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ by translations. This is the smallest binary dimension left open by Ferguson and Sothanaphan. For the implication from tiling to spectrality we show that every eight-point subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ admits $2^{d-3}$ frequencies whose pairwise differences avoid the zeros of its Fourier transform; consequently every tile of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ with at least $2^{d-3}$ elements is spectral. For the converse implication, we use the Smith normal form of the Walsh matrix to exclude every spectral subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^7$, and of $\mathbb{F}_2^8$, whose size is not a power of two. The sizes $16$ and $32$ are reduced, by a projection argument, to the tiling of point sets attached to binary log-Hadamard matrices of small rank. Using the published classifications of Hadamard matrices of orders $16$ and $32$, we find that exactly sixteen order-$32$ classes up to transposition have dephased binary rank at most seven, and we give explicit tilings for both orientations of each.

papers.title: Separable elements and Bruhat orders
papers.abstract: We prove the curious fact that, in any Coxeter group, the intersection of a principal left weak order ideal $[e,x]_L$ with a principal right weak order ideal $[e,y]_R$ has a unique maximal element $\mathrm{lr}(x,y)$ under Bruhat order. We apply this to resolve a conjecture of Hart and Rowley on involutions in weak order ideals. This fact arises from, and is applied to, our study of the theory of separable elements in finite Weyl groups. We use it to prove that for $U=[e,u]_R$ in a Coxeter group $W$, the multiplication map $W/U\times U\rightarrow W$ is surjective, where $W/U$ is the Björner-Wachs generalized quotient. This resolves and generalizes a conjecture of the authors. For finite Weyl groups, we further prove that this map is bijective if and only if $u$ is separable, thereby classifying the splittings of finite Weyl groups into weak order intervals, and resolving the natural extension of a question of Björner-Wachs.

papers.title: Exact lattice resonances and a sharp second Picard obstruction for the two-dimensional inviscid primitive equations
papers.abstract: We study periodic perturbations of a rest state with constant stable stratification for the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations without viscosity or thermal diffusion on a fixed rectangular torus. Fourier resonance analysis and Sobolev estimates show that, despite unitary linear evolution, the polarized second Picard operator admits no bilinear bound losing less than one derivative at any Sobolev order and any fixed nonzero time for real data with zero vertical means. The loss is sharp for \(s\ge2\), with matching bounds on every sufficiently high physical dyadic shell. We classify exact lattice resonances in all signed channels and compute their polarized coefficients. A mixed-branch family with fixed vertical frequencies isolates diagnostic transport and shows that finite vertical regularity cannot reduce the loss below one horizontal derivative in tensor-product Sobolev spaces. In contrast, for \(s\ge2\), the horizontal mean of the second Picard operator admits a time-uniform one-derivative bound. In interaction variables, the response divided by time converges to the resonant operator, with an \(O(|t|^{-1})\) error after a four-derivative loss for \(s\ge4\). Finally, among real linear spaces defined solely by a common Fourier-support constraint on both components, the maximal spaces on which the full nonlinearity vanishes for all smooth states are precisely those supported on primitive lattice rays. On these rays, we construct explicit global solutions and obtain an exact criterion for uniform strict stratification.

papers.title: Marchal-type lemmas for the restricted $(N+1)$-body problem with their applications
papers.abstract: The direct methods of calculus of variations have had a great success in the classical Newtonian $N$-body problem in this century. First in finding periodic solutions and more recently in the existence of parabolic, hyperbolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions. The foundation of many of these results is Marchal's lemma, which guarantee's fixed-end local minimizers are collision-free and hence classical solutions of the $N$-body problem. Meanwhile almost no result is available in the restricted problem through the direct methods of calculus of variations, mainly due to the lack of a Marchal-type lemma. In this paper such a lemma and its variation will be obtained for the restricted problem. We then apply them to the restricted problem to study unbounded (hyperbolic, parabolic, bi-hyperbolic and bi-parabolic) solutions, and bounded (periodic and quasi-periodic) solutions. We emphasize that the extension to the restricted case does not follow from the standard arguement for the unrestricted case.

papers.title: The Spectral Theory of Threshold Graphs: A Survey
papers.abstract: Threshold graphs-the $\{P_4, C_4, 2K_2\}$-free graphs, equivalently those built from a single vertex by repeatedly adding isolated or dominating vertices-are among the most thoroughly studied graph classes in spectral graph theory. This survey collects results on the spectrum of threshold graphs across the full range of matrices studied in the literature: the adjacency, Laplacian, and signless Laplacian matrices; the distance, distance Laplacian, and distance signless Laplacian matrices; the eccentricity and Seidel matrices; and the normalized adjacency, Laplacian matrix-together with the associated graph energies, cospectrality questions, extremal spectral radius problems, and several generalizations (weighted, quasi-threshold, hypergraph, and random threshold graphs). We emphasize results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Chvátal--Hammer, Merris, Bapat, and Jacobs--Lazzarin--Trevisan--Tura. We also present a study of integral threshold graphs (those with all-integer spectrum) across all seven matrices. We close with a list of open problems and conjectures drawn directly from the surveyed literature and from this new analysis.

papers.title: On Niu's Conjecture for Two-Station Tandem Queues
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a long standing conjecture in queueing theory made by Niu (1980): in a two-station tandem queueing system with constant service time (c) at station 1, the stationary average waiting time at station 2 is nonincreasing in c. Two very different proofs are provided: one for the general case and one for a special case in which the arrival process is Poisson and the service time at station 2 is exponential.

papers.title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 1: The Case \(n+\log n\)
papers.abstract: We prove that $(α(n+\log n))_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for Lebesgue almost every real $α$. This solves a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 2, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021].

papers.title: Normal approximation for total magnetization in subcritical long-range Ising models
papers.abstract: We establish Berry--Esseen bounds and 1-Wassershtein bounds for the total spin of strictly subcritical zero-field Ising models with summable interactions. Let $J:\mathbb Z^d\to[0,\infty)$ be symmetric, satisfy $J(0)=0$, and $\|J\|_1:=\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^d}J(x)<\infty$. For a nonempty finite set $Λ\subset\mathbb Z^d$, consider zero-field Gibbs measure with free boundary conditions, in which a spin configuration $σ\in\{-1,+1\}^Λ$ has probability proportional to \[ \exp\!\left\{ β\sum_{x,y\inΛ} J(x-y)σ_xσ_y \right\}. \] Let $S_Λ:=\sum_{x\inΛ}σ_x$ be the total spin and $β_{\mathrm c}$ denote the critical inverse temperature. For every fixed $0\leqβ<β_{\mathrm c}$, we prove that \[ d_{\mathrm K}\!\left( \frac{S_Λ}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(S_Λ)}},G \right) \leq C_{β,J}|Λ|^{-1/2}, \] where $d_{\mathrm K}$ is the Kolmogorov distance, $G\sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$, and $C_{β,J}$ depends only on $β$ and $J$. For the fully periodized model on $(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$, the corresponding rate is $L^{-d/2}$, uniformly in $L$. For the classical nearest-neighbor model, the Kolmogorov bound also holds for $-β_{\mathrm c}<β<β_{\mathrm c}$, covering both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions. We also obtain $1$-Wasserstein bounds with the same rates in the respective subcritical regimes. Both the Kolmogorov and $1$-Wasserstein bounds hold with the same rate under the corresponding infinite-volume free-boundary Gibbs measures.

papers.title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 2: The Case \(n\log n\)
papers.abstract: We prove that $(αn\log n)_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for almost every real $α$, solving a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 3, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021]. Our main contribution is a new four-point counting estimate with a fixed power saving over $N^{7/3}$ at tolerance $N^{-1}$, valid on the ranges left after a first-moment and Borel--Cantelli argument. Its proof reduces the counting condition to the required proximity of an implicitly defined real root to an integer; a Fejér kernel majorizes this condition, and multidimensional van der Corput $A$- and $B$-processes supply the saving. A localized Mellin argument then yields the second-moment estimate needed for the metric conclusion.

papers.title: KKM meets colorful Carathéodory
papers.abstract: The colorful Carathéodory theorem states that if $V_1,\dots,V_{d+1}\subset\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $0\in\mathrm{conv}\;V_i$ for every $i$, then there exist points $v_i\in V_i$ such that $0\in\mathrm{conv}\;\{v_1,\dots,v_{d+1}\}$. We give a new proof based on triangulations and the classical KKM lemma. We lift the sets $V_i$ to parallel affine copies of $\mathbb R^d$ in $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ and use a triangulation of the resulting point configuration to construct a KKM cover. Using the same approach, we prove the very colorful Carathéodory theorem.

papers.title: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
papers.abstract: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.

papers.title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: For $T > 0$ large, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $ζ$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|^β$ on $I_θ := [ - (\log{T})^θ,(\log{T})^θ]$, for every $θ> 0$ and $β> 0$. As $β$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|ζ|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $σ$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $β_{c}(θ) := 2\sqrt{1 + θ}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $β\leq β_{c}(θ)$, and assigns masses $β_{c}(θ)/β$ and $1 - β_{c}(θ)/β$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $β> β_{c}(θ)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Low-weight compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ and the extended Torelli morphism
papers.abstract: We study the weight zero and weight two graded pieces of the compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus $g$ of compact type and show that they are computed by bridgeless graph complexes. In weight two, we construct a natural embedding of shifted weight zero cohomology from lower genus. For unmarked curves, we construct canonical classes represented by pinched odd wheel graphs and prove that distinct wheel monomials give linearly independent classes in the dual of $W_0H_c^{2g}(\mathcal M_g^{ct};\mathbb Q)$. By relating the bridgeless graph complex to the $K$-theory of graphs and the Quillen spectral sequence, we show that these classes remain linearly independent after pushforward along the extended Torelli morphism $\mathcal M_g^{ct}\to\mathcal A_g$. Finally, we prove that the realizations of the motivic Lie algebra arising from $\mathcal M_g$ and $\mathcal A_g$ have the same image in the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_g^{ct}$.

papers.title: Complete characterization of disconnected one-point unions of cycles with local antimagic chromatic number 2
papers.abstract: A graph $G = (V, E)$ that admits a bijective edge labeling $f:E \to\{1,\ldots ,|E|\}$ is local antimagic if $f$ induces a vertex labeling $f^+$ such that for any pair of adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$, $f^+(x)\not= f^+(y)$, where the induced vertex label $f^+(x)= \sum f(xu)$, with $u$ ranging over all the vertices adjacent to $x$. The minimum number of distinct induced vertex labels over all local antimagic labelings of $G$ is the local antimagic chromatic number of $G$, denoted $χ_{la}(G)$. In this paper, we completely characterize all the disconnected one-point unions of cycles (having at most 3 components) with local antimagic chromatic number 2. Our approach allows the complete characterization of all such graphs with at least 4 components by a case-by-case analysis and every edge is assigned a unique label, up to isomorphism.

papers.title: Integral Volume Criteria for Semilinear and Quasilinear Liouville Theorems on Complete Manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a connected complete noncompact Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $V_o(R)$ denote its ball volume. We prove Liouville theorems without any curvature assumption. For $p>1$ and $q>p-1$, divergence of $\int^\infty R^{pq/(p-1)-1}V_o(R)^{-(q-p+1)/(p-1)}\dd R$ forces every nonnegative Sobolev weak supersolution of $-Δ_pu\ge u^q$ to vanish. For $q>\max\{1,p-1\}$, divergence of $\int^\infty R^{p-1}V_o(R)^{-(q-p+1)}\dd R$ forces every nonnegative global distributional energy supersolution of $u_t-Δ_pu\ge u^q$ to vanish. Consequently, the corresponding Cauchy problem has no global solution in this class with a nonzero nonnegative local $L^1$ initial trace.

papers.title: The fractional Hénon-Lane-Emden conjecture and some critical nonexistence phenomena
papers.abstract: We refine the proof method for the Hénon-Lane-Emden system and extend it to fractional orders $0<s<1$, proving subcritical nonexistence of positive classical solutions. And we find examples with $0<s<1/2$ and fixed nonzero weights for which existence and nonexistence occur at different points of the same critical hyperbola.

papers.title: Single-Letterization of Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Static Time-Invariant Control (STIC) Systems
papers.abstract: In settings such as online recommendation platforms, medical decision-making with interim summaries, and stochastic control with static plants, the underlying system is often static so that the next state depends only on the most recent action. Moreover, the true system state is high-dimensional and cannot be observed directly, so actions must be selected based on information received through a rate-limited communication link, which constrains the control performance. This leads to a fundamental rate-cost tradeoff$\unicode{x2014}$the minimum communication rate required to achieve a prescribed average control cost. We study this tradeoff for a class of static systems we term static time-invariant control (STIC) systems, namely, control systems in which the next state depends on the history only through the most recent control action via a time-invariant kernel. For general control systems$\unicode{x2014}$not necessarily static or time-invariant$\unicode{x2014}$our prior work characterized this tradeoff through the limit of a sequence of directed-information minimization problems. However, the dimension of these problems grows with the time horizon, making the limiting formulation computationally intractable. In the present paper, we show for STIC systems that this growing-size formulation admits a single-letter characterization. This identifies STIC systems as the control-side counterpart of Noisy Output is the STate (NOST) channels$\unicode{x2014}$one of the few channel models whose feedback capacity admits a single-letter characterization. This yields, to our knowledge, the first constant-size convex characterization of the rate$\unicode{x2013}$cost tradeoff beyond linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the local antimagic leaf conjecture
papers.abstract: It has been conjectured that $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+2$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three, where $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)$ is the local antimagic chromatic number and $\ell(T)$ denotes the number of leaves. We disprove this bound and show that no absolute constant can replace $2$ in an inequality of this form. Our approach uses degree-based intervals containing all possible induced vertex weights under bijective edge labelings, together with a separation criterion that forces selected internal vertex weights to be distinct. We first construct caterpillars $T_3$ and $T_4$ satisfying $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T_3)=\ell(T_3)+3$ and $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T_4)=\ell(T_4)+4$, respectively. We then construct, for every positive integer $r$, infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic caterpillars with exactly $r$ internal vertices for which every bijective edge labeling is antimagic. Each such caterpillar $T$ satisfies $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)=|V(T)|=\ell(T)+r$. Consequently, $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)-\ell(T)$ is unbounded even within the class of caterpillars, and no absolute constant $C$ can satisfy $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+C$ for every tree $T$.

papers.title: Exotic symplectomorphisms of strong fillings
papers.abstract: We prove a criterion for detecting exotic symplectomorphisms of strong fillings of closed contact manifolds. The criterion concerns symplectomorphisms induced by free contact circle actions on the boundary, and it is expressed purely in topological terms. As an application, we show that one-point blow-ups of an infinite family of Brieskorn varieties admit exotic compactly supported symplectomorphisms.

papers.title: Development of a fabrication-to-benchtop process for SiN-based quantum devices
papers.abstract: Silicon nitride has emerged as a key material for the advancement of future quantum communication and computational devices. However, challenges persist in establishing a comprehensive development process, spanning from fabrication to optical characterization, essential for advancing these devices to their next stage of potential. Maintaining control over the entire process, from start to finish, alongside device modeling, enables more efficient and timely iteration and optimization. Here we introduce a fabrication-to-benchtop process. We employ an in-house stoichiometric recipe for device fabrication and conduct comprehensive characterization of optical losses and material properties. Understanding and controlling the refractive index of the device are vital for predicting device geometries and group indices. Implementing the refractive indices of our fabricated devices, we simulate microring resonators and demonstrate their application in generating optical solitons.

papers.title: On the existence of mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors
papers.abstract: Orthogonal arrays are foundational objects in combinatorial design theory and experimental design theory, with broad applications in computer science, coding theory, and cryptography. In this paper, we investigate the existence for mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors, and propose several new constructions based on incomplete orthogonal Latin squares, incomplete transversal designs, and $Σ$-resolvable transversal designs. As a result, we show that the necessary conditions for the existence of such mixed orthogonal arrays are also sufficient, except for a small number of known exceptions and nine unsettled cases.

papers.title: The Involution Rank of $\MCG(Σ_3)$ Is Four
papers.abstract: For the closed orientable surface $Σ_3$, we prove \[ \irank\MCG(Σ_3)=4.\] Thus $\MCG(Σ_3)$ can be generated by four involutions, but not by three. This settles the genus-three case of Farb's problem on generation by involutions.

papers.title: Spectral asymmetry and odd cycles in integral graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that the triangle $C_3$ is the only integral unicyclic graph with an odd cycle. The main tool is a spectral inequality that does not require integrality: if $G$ is a connected non-bipartite graph and $G-e$ is bipartite for some edge $e$, then the eigenvalues $λ_1\ge\cdots\geλ_n$ of $G$ satisfy $\sum_{i}(λ_i+λ_{n+1-i})^+\le 2$ and $0<λ_1+λ_n\le 1$. It follows from comparing $A(G)$ with the signed adjacency matrix obtained by reversing the sign of $e$, which is similar to $-A(G)$, through a common rank-one perturbation and Weyl's monotonicity theorem. For integral graphs in this class, an arithmetic lemma then gives $λ_n=1-λ_1$ and at least $λ_1-1\ge1$ triangles, which yields the classification. We also prove that an integral graph of odd girth $g$ has at least $(g-1)!/2$ cycles of length $g$, with equality for the Petersen graph when $g=5$, and we derive consequences for quantum periodicity a

papers.title: Semialgebraic ${C^m}$ solutions to a univariate system of linear inequalities with Nash forcing
papers.abstract: Let $(A_{ij}(x))_{1 \leq i \leq N, 1 \leq j \leq M}$ be a matrix of univariate semialgebraic functions. We study the solvability of the system of linear inequalities \begin{equation*} \sum_{j=1}^M A_{ij}(x)F_j(x)\leq f_i(x) \ \ \text{ for } i = 1, \ldots, N, \end{equation*} where we assume each forcing $f_i$ is a Nash function. We show that the $C^m$ solvability of the system can be characterized by finitely many linear ordinary differential inequalities in $f$ with semialgebraic coefficients depending only on $(A_{ij})$. When the system is solvable, the solution may be chosen semialgebraic, and the proof gives a constructive procedure in the semialgebraic sense. We also study the semimodule structure of admissible forcings, establishing finite generation and lack thereof in various settings.

papers.title: Galois Groups of Trinomials with Small Coefficients
papers.abstract: We calculate the Galois group of $f = x^n + ax^k + b \in \mathbb{Z}\left[ x \right]$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all $1 \leq \left| ab \right| \leq 3$, $n$ sufficiently large and $k$ coprime to $n$. In particular, we prove that the Galois group of $f$ is the maximal one that its factorization type allows. We do it by proving a new sufficient condition for the Galois group of a factor of a trinomial to be symmetric, which perhaps can be used to derive stronger results of this kind in the future.

papers.title: Cavity-less Brillouin strong coupling in a solid-state continuous system
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03458-2Strong coupling between light and matter is typically realized in resonators. Now it is shown that this can happen in a cavity-less waveguide scenario in which the light passes through only once.

papers.title: Chaos control with broken symmetries
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03480-4By breaking both material and cavity symmetries, waves can be funnelled into robust closed-loop patterns. This dual-symmetry-breaking approach enables the development of a new class of devices for wave-based signal processing and sensing.

papers.title: An Adjoint Criterion for Left-Invariant $m$-Modified Conformal Vector Fields on Even-Dimensional Lie Groups
papers.abstract: For a fixed positive real constant $m$, a real Lie algebra of even dimension $2k$ admits a nonzero left-invariant $m$-modified conformal vector field for some nondegenerate metric if and only if an adjoint operator has a nonzero real eigenvalue. In that case, a solution exists with neutral signature $(k,k)$ and zero conformal factor. As an application, we classify the admissible four-dimensional Lie algebras and metric signatures; the only Lorentzian exceptions among the admissible algebras are $\mathfrak{aff}(\mathbb{C})$ and the diamond algebra. On a pseudo-Riemannian manifold of arbitrary indefinite signature, a nonzero $m$-modified conformal vector field forces lightlike geodesic incompleteness, even when its conformal factor is variable.

papers.title: $R$-trivial Galois cohomology classes and cohomological $p$-dimension
papers.abstract: Given a prime $p$, a field $F$ of characteristic different from $p$ and a finite $p$-primary Galois module $V$, a Galois cohomology class in $H^n(F,V)$ is called $R$-trivial if it can be connected to $0$ by a class defined over an open subscheme of the projective line. All classes of $H^n(F,V)$ are $R$-trivial if $F$ has cohomological $p$-dimension at most $n$, by the Bloch-Kato conjecture. We show that this bound is sharp: working over fields of iterated Laurent series, we produce, for every $n\geq 1$, a field $F$ of cohomological $p$-dimension $n+1$ and a Galois module $V$ such that $H^n(F,V)$ contains classes which are not $R$-trivial. The module $V$ is a quotient of the permutation module on the affine hyperplanes of an elementary abelian $p$-group, arising as a quotient of the absolute Galois group of $F$. We also describe $R$-trivial classes as sums of corestrictions of cup products involving a Kummer class.

papers.title: $a$-numbers of covers in characteristic two: semigroups and Riemann-Roch spaces
papers.abstract: We compute the $a$-numbers of the Garcia-Güneri-Stichtenoth curves, the Beelen-Montanucci curves, and the Skabelund covers of Suzuki curves in characteristic two. The proofs use the identity $a(X)=\ell(\tfrac12\operatorname{div}(dt))$ and reduce the calculations to Riemann-Roch spaces on the base curves. We obtain transfer formulas for odd-degree radical covers, with one or several points at infinity, and evaluate them using Weierstrass semigroups and plane sections of the Hermitian curve. For the first two families we also give cyclic models over the projective line and relate the formulas to Elkin's rank formula. We then treat two classes of Artin-Schreier fibre products. A supersingular genus-six family has a-number $3$ at the zero parameter and $2$ elsewhere, although the genera and $a$-numbers of its quadratic quotients remain fixed. We determine its Ekedahl--Oort types as $(0,0,0,1,2,3)$ and $(0,1,1,2,3,4)$,

papers.title: The Classical Boundary of Quantum Computation: History-Resolved Causal Stochastic Machines and the Cost of Classicalization
papers.abstract: What separates quantum computation from classical computation when a classical model may retain every branch history and arbitrary causal memory? We study this question using history-resolved causal stochastic machines (HCSMs), which describe positive causal history laws. Probabilistic Turing machines (PTMs) embed in stochastic-ensemble models (SEnMs), which in turn embed in HCSMs. We prove that HCSM history laws coincide exactly with the fixed-basis, prefix-preserving diagonal sector of ideal quantum processes, denoted by $\mathsf{PTM}_{\rm proc}$ and distinguished here from algorithmic quantum Turing machines (QTMs). Coherent quantum processes extend strictly beyond this sector. The boundary is already visible in reversibility. Born-probability shadows of unitary gates preserve inverse composition exactly for basis permutations with phases. Outside this class, an exact positive stochastic simulation that supports universal quantum continuations must retain predictive information absent from visible probabilities. An inverse-recovery identity quantifies this phase ledger, and universal continuation forces the retained probability law to be tomographically sufficient for the quantum state. Under continuous full-state encoding assumptions, this requirement yields quantum-state dimension lower bounds. The familiar slogan $\mathsf{PTM}\subseteq\mathsf{QTM}$ is thereby sharpened into a precise classical boundary and a no-free-classicalization principle. Complete classical branching does not remove the predictive information needed to represent quantum coherence.

papers.title: Density Bounds in Hua's Theorem for Prime Squares
papers.abstract: We prove a density version of Hua's theorem in the five-variable case: if $\mathcal P$ is a subset of the primes with relative lower density greater than $0.82$, then every sufficiently large $n\equiv5\pmod{24}$ is a sum of five squares of primes from $\mathcal P$.

papers.title: Negative-binomial ensemble filtering for discrete-time Hawkes network reconstruction
papers.abstract: We develop a sequential ensemble filter for reconstructing directed excitation networks from overdispersed multivariate counts observed on a regular time grid. The data-generating model is a discrete-time negative-binomial Hawkes process, for which we prove exact first- and second-moment stability conditions and derive a row-wise sufficient condition. The filter learns the network and the dispersion online, and a row-composition parameter forecast keeps enough ensemble variation to respond to structural change. In synthetic experiments, we demonstrate that a Poisson-based filter provides comparable point-estimate accuracy of the network, while the proposed filter provides substantially better calibrated predictive and parameter uncertainty. Under an abrupt redistribution of influence, the filter recovers connections that are absent before the change. An application to daily property-crime counts in sixteen Chicago community areas gives broadly calibrated one-step predictions and a recovered network consistent with independent temporal and geographic information.

papers.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
papers.abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. We experimentally realize silicon photonic topological superlattices in which the nonlinear generation pathway itself becomes programmable via tailored excitations. The superlattices host a multiband manifold of co localized topological interface modes, while coherently controlled inputs synthesize pump superpositions within this protected basis. We showcase this principle by selectively addressing topological biphoton eigenstates, steering correlations to produce a desired target state in a high-dimensional Hilbert space, and inverse-designing pump states that generate targeted Schmidt dimensionalities. Site-resolved two-photon correlation measurements remain reproducible across nominally identical fabricated devices, demonstrating robustness to realistic nanofabrication-induced disorder. Programmable preparation of topological entangled states establishes a pathway towards exploiting topological photonic modes as application-specific quantum resources, enabling tailored input states for high-dimensional quantum communication, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing.

papers.title: Metric and Dispersive Dynamics of Phase Perturbations in Bohmian Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: By linearizing the hydrodynamic equations associated with the Madelung transformation in the context of Bohmian dynamics, we derive an effective metric for the phase perturbation around a background state. We show that the metric previously obtained previously by the same authors arises naturally as a particular case of a more general structure, in which the complete functional variation of the quantum potential is retained and external classical potentials can be incorporated. This generalization preserves the dependence of the quantum potential on the density and its spatial derivatives, generating additional terms that introduce dispersive corrections and act as sources in the effective Klein-Gordon equation. To organize these contributions, we introduce differential operators that separate the local sector responsible for the effective geometry from the corrections associated with the complete functional structure of the quantum potential. We identify the conditions under which these additional terms become negligible, recovering homogeneous propagation and the effective geometry for the Gaussian wave packet of a free particle.

papers.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for the Minimal Input/Output Node Cardinality Disturbance Decoupling Problem via Output Feedback
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an algorithm that solves, in polynomial-time, the minimal input/output node cardinality disturbance decoupling problem via output feedback. The optimal solution, intended as a minimal-cardinality pair of sets of control inputs and measurement output nodes needed to achieve the decoupling, is computed by solving a modified min-cut/max-flow problem.

papers.title: A Non-Split Motohashi Formula for Toric Periods over Number Fields
papers.abstract: We establish a non-split Motohashi formula for toric Eisenstein periods over an arbitrary number field $F$. For a quadratic extension $E/F$, we compare toric Fourier inversion for a product of two Eisenstein series with the $\mathrm{GL}_2/F$-spectral expansion of its Rankin--Selberg kernel. The kernel regularizes the product in a cone of absolute convergence. Eisenstein corrections and contour residues give the geometric and residual terms in the meromorphically continued identity. Suitable test data give twisted first- and second-moment formulas for the completed $L$-functions of everywhere unramified toric characters. Over general $F$ these provide an adelic counterpart of the moment formulas of Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec that does not use the geometry of Heegner points. In the CM case, we prove the absolute nonvanishing proportion $4.9\times10^{-4}$ for every totally real base field and all sufficiently large CM discriminants, with the threshold depending on the base field and no restriction on the number of ramified primes. We incorporate inverse Euler factors at small ramified primes into the mollifier. Local unit-group tests control the resulting moments and remove the ramified Euler-factor loss.

papers.title: The Diophantine Problem in Wreath Products of Groups
papers.abstract: We study the Diophantine problem in restricted wreath products of groups. Write $G=B\wr H$, where $B$ is the passive factor and $H$ is the active factor. The main results demonstrate that in a wide class of wreath products $G$, the Diophantine problem is undecidable. First, we show that if both factors are indicable, then $G$ has a retract isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}\wr\mathbb{Z}$ and therefore has undecidable Diophantine problem. Then, we show that for any groups $B$ and $H$, the Diophantine problems in $B$ and $H$ are polynomial time reducible to the Diophantine problem in $G$. Finally, we combine e-definability with retractions in order to prove that the Diophantine problem in $G$ is undecidable whenever $B$ is an infinite finitely generated abelian group and $H$ is a finitely generated group containing an infinite e-definable finitely generated abelian subgroup $A$.

papers.title: Cross-ratios and first order ordinary differential equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the usefulness of the cross-ratio in the study of first order odes of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K,\;n\geqslant1$, where $K$ is a differential field of characteristic zero with algebraically closed field of constants. We discover along the way many differential algebraic identity between solutions to that equation. We also explain why the cross-ratio of any four solutions to such an equation is in general not constant when $n\geq3$ by exhibiting an obstruction which prevents its constancy when $n\geq3$. Finally to any separable polynomial $P_\varphi(z)=z^{n+1}+\varphi_1z^n+\varphi_2z^{n-1}+\ldots+\varphi_{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, over a differential field of meromorphic function on some domain of $\mathbb C$ with the usual derivation we associate a uniquely defined first order ode of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K$ such that every root of $P_\varphi(z)$ is a solution to the said differential equation.

papers.title: On exponential stability of generalized linear functional differential equations
papers.abstract: We develop a general approach to uniform exponential stability for a broad class of linear functional differential equations with Volterra operators. The considered class includes delay differential equations, integro-differential equations, equations with distributed delays, vector equations, and systems of scalar functional differential equations. Standard assumptions on the equation are relaxed to include measurable parameters. Some results remain valid for equations with unbounded delays and oscillatory coefficients and kernels. For all the above mentioned classes of equations, explicit uniform exponential stability tests are obtained.

papers.title: Universal operators: topology and consequences of ISP failure
papers.abstract: Assuming a negative answer to the invariant subspace problem for separable complex Hilbert spaces, we prove that every universal operator has a continuum of minimal infinite-dimensional invariant subspaces with pairwise trivial intersections. These subspaces can be chosen so that the restrictions are invertible and their powers decay at any prescribed geometric rate. For an affine composition operator on the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{D})$, we derive restrictions on the zeros, inner factors and Hardy regularity of generators, and construct minimal models with radial vanishing of any prescribed finite order. Independently of the invariant subspace problem, we identify the norm interior, closure and boundary of the universal operator class. Its interior is the Caradus--Pozzi class, its closure is the complement of the upper semi-Fredholm class, and its boundary consists of the operators that are neither upper nor lower semi-Fredholm.

papers.title: Optimal approximation of smooth functions by ReLU neural networks
papers.abstract: We study uniform approximation of the Hölder ball $\mathcal H_1^s([0,1]^D)$ by fully connected ReLU networks. Except in the one-dimensional Lipschitz case, existing constructions remain separated from the information-theoretic efficiency limit. This article closes the gap for every $s>0$ and $D\ge1$: networks with width $O(N)$, depth $O(L)$, and parameter magnitude $O(1)$ attain uniform approximation error of order $(N^2L^2\log N)^{-s/D}$. No relation between width and depth is required. The construction uses new encoding and decoding mechanisms that exploit higher-order finite-difference bounds for local Taylor coefficients of the target function. As a statistical consequence, empirical risk minimizers over the corresponding clipped network classes attain the minimax regression rate $n^{-2s/(2s+D)}$ without additional logarithmic factors. The paper also gives a detailed exposition of the key approximation techniques, covering both established and new mechanisms.

papers.title: Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations
papers.abstract: Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a promising approach for simulating open quantum systems, yet their expressive power and trainability remain poorly understood. We propose a variational framework for solving Lindblad master equations by minimizing a residual cost function using a compositional ansatz obtained by combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit. The density matrix is represented through a purification on an enlarged Hilbert space, ensuring positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace by construction, while all gradients are evaluated exactly via the parameter-shift rule. Beyond the algorithmic formulation, we derive an upper bound for the covering number of the proposed compositional model and compare it with that of purely quantum neural networks. Our analysis shows that the classical parametrization enlarges the effective hypothesis class while providing finer control over its complexity, thereby establishing a theoretical connection between expressivity, covering numbers, effective dimension, and the barren plateau phenomenon. Numerical experiments validate both the accuracy of the proposed method for representative Lindblad master equations and the theoretical predictions regarding gradient concentration. These results provide a unified variational and theoretical framework for the simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics using compositional quantum machine learning models.

papers.title: Circuit Synthesis for Variational Quantum Algorithms: The Depth of Algebra and Geometry
papers.abstract: The analysis of Hamiltonian Variational Ansätze centers on three fundamental questions: which states are exactly reachable from a given initial state, what native control depth suffices for local and global synthesis, and whether a bounded circuit extension can expose a direction of decreasing cost at a suboptimal output. We address these challenges by leveraging the dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) associated with the circuits and the geometry of the initial state's orbit under the action of the corresponding dynamical Lie group $G$. We show that an initial state has a closed projective orbit whenever it is a nondegenerate eigenstate of a control Hamiltonian. Combined with asymptotic QAOA convergence, this guarantees exact, finite depth ground state preparation for architectures employing diagonal problem Hamiltonians and irreducible stoquastic mixers. We bound the number of native control exponentials required for local unitary synthesis and state preparation using DLA commutator filtration growth alongside reachable orbit dimensions. Complementing these local results, we construct global frameworks on invariant sectors equipped with full unitary or special unitary dynamical Lie algebras. These constructions yield explicit applications to Pauli-generated systems and constrained maximum independent set multi-angle QAOA circuits; specifically, we show that their native control costs are directly determined by commutator filtration depth and independent-set toggle-group geometry, respectively. Finally, if the dynamical Lie group is compact, the observable $H_P$ generates an admissible evolution ($iH_P \in \mathfrak{g}$, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is the DLA), and the projective orbit of the initial state contains a ground state ray of $H_P$, then a bounded depth, identity-initialized circuit extension exhibits either first-order descent or negative curvature at every suboptimal circuit output.

papers.title: Optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems
papers.abstract: We design and test several new optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems. Each method is A-stable, implicit, and second-order accurate. We focus on achieving the smallest possible error constant while also ensuring that stiff modes are damped. We recover some known optimal L-stable three- and four-step methods, and provide new and improved five-step methods. We also develop new methods that are not L-stable but provide a prescribed rate of damping in the infinitely stiff limit. Variable-step-size formulae are also provided for some of the new methods. Numerical tests demonstrate that the improved error constants lead to improved accuracy.

papers.title: Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds
papers.abstract: We fully classify vector bundles of critical rank on normal affine surfaces and threefolds over algebraically closed fields via their Chern classes. We also prove existence of rank $2$ bundles on threefolds with prescribed first and second motivic Chern classes. The main input is the motivic filtration on algebraic $K$-theory: its third piece is generated by smooth closed points and is identified with motivic cohomology by the third Chern class.

papers.title: Generic vanishing for Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We study generic vanishing for the Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules, where the differentials in the Dolbeault complex are modified by a one-form. We prove that, on the Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs line bundles, the cohomology support loci of mixed Hodge modules agree with the images of the cohomology support loci of their underlying $\mathscr{D}$-modules on the de Rham moduli space under the map induced by the nonabelian Hodge correspondence.
