We further apply this result to study Fourier-Mukai transforms of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties. We show that the extended Fourier-Mukai transform for bounded complexes of mixed Hodge modules has cohomology sheaves that are flat over the twistor line of $λ$-connections. This also gives an extension of Fourier transform of mixed Hodge modules to a compactification of the de Rham moduli space.

papers.title: String functions and cyclotomic Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the Kleshchev multipartitions that label simple modules of certain cyclotomic Hecke algebras with parameters $1$ and $-1$. The $2$-residue statistic divides these multipartitions into blocks. We deduce a bivariate generating function for the blocks using representation theory. We also relate the generating functions of multipartitions in a fixed block to string functions associated by Kac and Peterson to irreducible highest weight modules of a type $A_1^{(1)}$ affine Lie algebra. By considering matrices formed by these generating functions, we reprove some results of Kac--Peterson on string functions using the Macdonald identities of Rosengren--Schlosser. As an application, we obtain new infinite product formulas for these generating functions.

papers.title: A Spectral Approach to Fixed Points in Product Spaces
papers.abstract: We study fixed points of mappings on finite products of Banach spaces whose coordinatewise Lipschitz estimates are controlled by a nonnegative matrix $A$. Our main result states that, if every coordinate space has normal structure and $r(A)\leq1$, then every such self-mapping of a nonempty weakly compact convex set has a fixed point. The result is a direct generalization of the Browder--Göhde--Kirk principle. The proof combines classical nonexpansive fixed point theory with Frobenius normal form, passing successively to coordinate projections and invariant fibres. As preparation, the classical reduction of Perov's theorem to the Banach contraction principle through adapted lattice norms is revisited. Applications include a Dirichlet boundary value problem for systems of abstract second order differential equations and a periodic problem for ODE systems satisfying one-sided matrix estimates.

papers.title: Rational decomposition of polyhedra and a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer
papers.abstract: We prove in the affirmative a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer (2003), which relates unambiguous rational sets to a well known result due to Khovanskii and Pukhlikov (1992) and independently to Lawrence (1990) on the valuations of the algebra spanned by the indicator functions of polyhedra.

papers.title: Disc-presheaves and normal invariants
papers.abstract: In this note, we elaborate on a result of Krannich--Kupers--Mehzer on Disc-presheaves. We show that equivalences of $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves of manifolds yields homotopy equivalences with trivial normal invariant. As an application, we show that two closed, simply connected manifolds are homeomorphic if and only if their $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves are equivalent.

papers.title: Spectral stability for strong ideal-gas shock layers
papers.abstract: We give a purely analytical proof of one-dimensional spectral stability of sufficiently strong shock layers for the full ideal-gas Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity and heat conduction. Earlier work reduced this question to a limiting problem and gave numerical evidence of stability, but no proof. We prove stability on an explicit region of gas constants and transport ratios that includes air and monatomic gases. No step of the argument relies on numerical computation, and the arguments, taking the cited results of Humpherys, Lyng, and Zumbrun as hypotheses, have also been verified in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
papers.abstract: Consider the bipartite Erdős--Rényi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $γ= n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Marčenko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $γ$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values. Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.

papers.title: Absolute continuity of invariant measures for random diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We develop criteria showing that invariant measures for random walks generated by diffeomorphisms of manifolds are in the Lebesgue class. Our assumptions are first, that there is a uniform expansion gap in the Lyapunov spectrum of the random walk, and second, that the conditionals of the invariant measure along the appropriate (partial) stable manifolds are in the Lebesgue class.

papers.title: A $\mathbb{C}$-motivic $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{DY} = \mathbb{1}/(η, ν) \in \mathrm{SH}(\mathbb{C})$. We construct a $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1 $w:Σ^{5,3}\mathrm{DY} \to \mathrm{DY}.$ The cofiber is a realization of $DA(1)$, the double of the subalgebra $A(1)$ of the $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Steenrod algebra $A$.

papers.title: Space-filling curves and small-ball probabilities for the Kloosterman process
papers.abstract: We construct explicitly a space-filling curve in the support of the limiting Kloosterman process, using the planar partial-sum curve of the Rudin--Shapiro sequence. The qualitative existence statement was previously attributed to J. Bober by Kowalski. The resulting curve is a closed, $1/2$-Hölder continuous loop whose image contains a specified triangle of area $1/128$. Its Fourier coefficients are purely imaginary and satisfy $|\widehat f(h)|\leq(2π|h|)^{-1}$ for $h\ne 0$. We also prove a uniform lower bound for small balls centred at closed $1/2$-Hölder curves with a fixed coefficient bound, of the form $\exp\{-C\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(2/\varepsilon)\}$. Known functional convergence then gives a quantitative lower bound for the limiting proportion of two-parameter Kloosterman paths approximating the constructed loop.

papers.title: A holomorphic motion with non-subharmonic Hausdorff dimension
papers.abstract: We present an example of a holomorphic motion of a Cantor set $λ\mapsto A_λ$ for which neither the Hausdorff dimension $\dimH(A_λ)$ nor the lower Minkowski dimension $\dimMl(A_λ)$ is a subharmonic function of~$λ$. This answers negatively a question of Fuhrer--Ransford--Younsi, and distinguishes these dimensions from packing and upper Minkowski dimensions, for which subharmonicity holds. All four dimensions are computed explicitly.

papers.title: Universal Threshold Laws for Dipolar Evaporation of Molecular Fermi Gases
papers.abstract: Fermi statistics suppress the elastic collisions that rethermalize a Fermi gas during evaporative cooling, creating a fundamental low-temperature bottleneck for producing quantum degenerate gases. We show that, for shielded single-component ultracold dipolar molecular Fermi gases in the Wigner threshold regime, this bottleneck is governed by universal threshold laws fixed by the effective dimensionality of the gas. In this regime, Fermi suppression of rethermalization scales quadratically with temperature in 3D but only linearly in 2D. Consequently, the thermalization-to-loss ratio is more favorable in 2D than in 3D, and these results suggest that 2D geometries are better suited for reaching deep degeneracy. We also present ab initio close-coupling calculations that agree well with experimental measurements on Fermi degenerate gases of KRb molecules, supporting our conclusions.

papers.title: Hard Instances on Demand
papers.abstract: The conclusions of an experimental study of algorithms are only as good as the instances they are run on. Benchmark libraries for well-studied problems took decades to curate, while evaluations of new problems often fall back on random instances, which are known to be misleading: they may say more about the random generator than about the algorithmic question at hand. We treat instance generation as an optimization problem: parameterize the instance space, take the solver's running time as the objective, and let a black-box optimizer search for hard instances. We develop a widely applicable workflow built on the Nevergrad optimization platform and demonstrate it on four NP-hard problems: satisfiability, traveling salesperson, Hamiltonian cycle, and non-permutation flow-shop scheduling. The search needs only the solver, an instance encoder, and a compute budget. Our evolved instances beat the hardest instance of a budget-matched random draw in all four case studies, by an order of magnitude or more in three. They are often competitive with long-curated benchmark sets: our SAT champion is harder (for a three-solver portfolio) than 78% of the 498 SAT Competition formulas in its size class; our 20-city TSP champions take several times longer than the hardest measured classical TSPLIB instance (229 cities); and our flow-shop champion takes 238.6 seconds of CP Optimizer time to solve to proven optimality (versus 4.5 seconds for the hardest of 100,000 random draws) while denying CP-SAT an optimality proof. The optimizer even recovers known structure from running time alone: it locates a SAT clause/variable ratio near the phase transition and finds structurally different champions for the two scheduling engines.

papers.title: Probabilistic Fourier extension and the Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We give applications of the probabilistic Fourier extension theorem for the paraboloid in d dimensions (see [Saw7] for the sphere, and the proof there holds for a smooth compact piece of the paraboloid) to the global initial value problem for the Schrödinger equation with initial data f, in which we obtain sharp averaged Sobolev regularity results over certain `martingale transforms' of the intial data f. The deterministic analogue in three dimensions has been obtained recently by OpenAI [Ope].

papers.title: Maximizing the spectral gap for free bosonic CFTs
papers.abstract: We study the spectral gap $Δ_1$ of Narain CFTs, the smallest scaling dimension of a nonvacuum $U(1)^c_L\times U(1)^c_R$ primary, as a function on the Narain moduli space. Using the exceptional isomorphisms for $SO^+(2,2)$ and $SO^+(3,3)$, we prove the sharp bounds $Δ_1\le 2/3$ at $c=2$ and $Δ_1\le 3/4$ at $c=3$, with equality exactly at the $SU(3)_1$ and $SU(4)_1$ WZW models up to $O(c)\times O(c)$, and we describe local maxima of $Δ_1$. For $4\le c\le 12$, we compare the Narain moduli space with the densest known Euclidean lattices: an arithmetic obstruction excludes five candidates, a computer-assisted classification shows that $E_8$, $K_{12}$, and $BW_{16}$ each admit a unique Narain structure up to lattice automorphisms, and a conceptual argument excludes the Leech lattice.

papers.title: Transposed Poisson structures in graded and algebroid geometry
papers.abstract: We ask whether the transposed Leibniz rule $2z\cdot[x,y]=[z\cdot x,y]+[x,z\cdot y]$ survives the two passages that turn Poisson algebras into geometry, the shift of degree which produces Gerstenhaber algebras and the passage from algebras to algebroids. We introduce graded transposed Poisson algebras with a bracket of arbitrary degree and show that the parity of the degree decides which shape the answer takes. In even degree, over a unital base, such brackets are in bijection with homogeneous derivations, and on the exterior algebra of a vector bundle in degree zero they are exactly the gauge derivations of the bundle. In odd degree the bracket is forced to be the product with a single element of that degree, so a non-negatively graded algebra carries no non-zero transposed Gerstenhaber bracket. In particular, for a Lie--Rinehart algebra $(A,L)$, the Schouten--Rinehart Gerstenhaber algebra $Λ_A L$ is transposed if and only if the anchor and the bracket of $L$ both vanish. We then introduce transposed $F$-algebroids and classify those with an identity: if the rank is at least two the anchor vanishes and the structure is the datum of a derivation of the multiplication, while if the rank is one the bundle is trivialised by the identity and the structure is, globally, the Jacobi bracket of a single vector field. For the tangent $F$-algebroid of an $F$-manifold $M$ this forces $\dim M=1$.

papers.title: Distributed Optimization over Simplicial Complexes via Topological Dirac Synchronization
papers.abstract: We introduce a distributed optimization framework for systems with higher-order interactions represented by simplicial and cell complexes. Specializing global topological Dirac synchronization to gradient flows of strongly convex local objectives, we show that the synchronized equilibrium coincides with the minimizer of the aggregate cost, without Lagrange multipliers, dual variables, or saddle-point dynamics. Orientation-equivariant convex terms and cell-dependent dimensional targets allow the optimal state to be nonzero, as determined by joint per-dimension optimality conditions. Our algorithm couples signals across dimensions through the Dirac operator: nodes interact with edges, edges with nodes and faces, and faces with edges, enabling information exchange beyond graph-Laplacian methods. In the isotropic case, a Master Stability Function analysis yields a necessary and sufficient condition for local exponential stability: the product of the directional coupling strengths must be below the squared ratio of the strong convexity parameter to the spectral radius of the complex. A weighted Lyapunov argument accounting for non-normal Dirac coupling establishes global exponential convergence at the same rate. Finally, we identify a topological admissibility condition ensuring invariance of the synchronization manifold and coherent convergence of cells to the optimum, with no counterpart in classical graph-based distributed optimization.

papers.title: Double interaction principle for the Lorentz force equation
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the Lorentz force equation using the Poincare action functional. We show that, if the scalar electric potential has good interactions at infinity and around the origin with the vector magnetic potential, then the Lorentz force equation has at least two periodic solutions with a fixed period. For the proof of our main result we introduce a new minimax theorem for the Poincare action functional that does not require the Palais-Smale compactness condition and provides the existence of twin critical points. The interaction at infinity in the electromagnetic potential implies a weak compactness property of the Poincare action functional, while the interaction around the origin gives the separation property of the functional.

papers.title: Axis-parallel square packing with an exact formula for optimal packing of seven squares
papers.abstract: How large a square is needed to hold axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths? We give exact formulas for the optimal side through seven squares, with explicit constructions and geometric lower-bound proofs. For every $n\ge6$, the optimum for $n$ squares is a sum of at most $n-3$ of the prescribed side lengths. This bound is sharp on an open set of side lengths and yields the optimal Euclidean Lipschitz constant $\sqrt{n-3}$ of the optimum as a function of the $n$ side lengths.

papers.title: Complete regular dessins: the nonmetacyclic case
papers.abstract: We classify regular dessins on $K_{2^e,2^f}$ with nonmetacyclic colour-preserving automorphism group, retaining the two specified vertex rotations. We give nonredundant presentations and exact counts in both the abelian and nonabelian Frattini cases. For orientation- and colour-preserving isomorphisms, the number is $2^{2e-2}+16$ when $e=f\ge4$ and $3\cdot2^{2f-3}+16$ when $e>f\ge4$, with explicit counts for all smaller exponents. The construction uses a parity criterion in the abelian case and a uniquely determined odd quadratic root with two lifts in the nonabelian case. A dessin in the classification is reflexible exactly when its Frattini subgroup is abelian. All symmetric classes are circular. We determine every circular subfamily, including its face orders and genera; the circular count is $2^e+8$ on the diagonal and $2^{f-2}(2^{f-1}+1)+8$ off the diagonal for $e\ge f\ge4$.

papers.title: On the two critical exponents for a dispersive equation with weak dissipation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a nonlinear Cauchy problem written in normal form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_{tt} + A u+ Bu_t =D|u|^α, & t\geq 0, x \in \mathbb{R}^n\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\,u_t(0,x)=u_1(x). \end{cases} \end{equation*} Here~ $Af=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(a(ξ)^2\mathscr{F}f)$, with $a(ξ)$ homogeneous of order $k > 0$ under the assumption that the Hessian matrix of $a(ξ)$ is nonsingular, the operator $Bf=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(b(ξ)\mathscr{F}f)$ represents a weak dissipation, in the sense that $b(ξ) \sim 1$ as $|ξ| \to \infty$ and %, in several models, $D=B$ but we also consider the case $Df=ν\ast (-Δ)^δ(I-Δ)^{-δ}$, with $ν$ a bounded measure and $δ\geq k/2$. We derive $L^p-L^q$ estimates of the linear solution operator to the considered model and we prove the transition from a Fujita-type exponent to a Strauss-type exponent for the global-in-time existence of small data solution for the corresponding nonlinear problems.

papers.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
papers.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

papers.title: Proof Perplexity: A Probabilistic Approach to Measuring non-triviality in Machine Generated Proofs
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose a benchmark to quantify the non-triviality and novelty of machine-generated mathematical proofs compared to existing literature. Our core methodology uses a probabilistic measure to evaluate the non-triviality of the underlying mathematical arguments in comparison to the current \texttt{MATHLIB} library. Finally, we apply this benchmark to the recent proof generated by Claude on the complex zeros of the Riemann zeta function to test for non-trivial steps.

papers.title: Volterra-Skorokhod Reflection and Fluid Limits of Loss Queues
papers.abstract: In the $G_t/G/n/n$ loss queue, a customer blocked at time $u$ remains missing from the system for as long as it would have been served. A fraction $K(t-u)$ of the blocking at $u$ therefore still affects the occupancy at time $t$, where $K=1-G$ is the service survival function. We show that, for every arrival process satisfying a functional strong law of large numbers, the fluid limit of this queue is a reflection with kernel $K$ of the fluid limit of the associated infinite-server queue. The reflection is defined by a one-sided reflection problem on $(-\infty,1]$ in which the regulator is convolved with a memory kernel. Given a càdlàg input $ρ$ and a kernel $K$ with $K(0)=1$, we seek a pair $(\hatρ,η)$ such that $\hatρ=ρ-\int_0^\cdot K(\cdot-u)\,dη(u)$ takes values in $(-\infty,1]$, $η$ is nondecreasing, and $η$ increases only when $\hatρ=1$. We refer to this problem as the Volterra-Skorokhod problem. We show existence and uniqueness of the solution and that the solution map is Lipschitz continuous in the uniform norm and nonanticipating. It therefore applies to stochastic inputs path by path. Unlike the classical Skorokhod map, this map is not monotone. For nonincreasing kernels, however, the regulator is the smallest admissible one and monotone in the input. In the queue, this orders the cumulative fluid losses under ordered arrival rates. Furthermore, since arrivals enter the queue through the reflection kernel, the regulator is a thinning of the arrivals.

papers.title: On strongly coherent confidence envelopes for the false discoveries
papers.abstract: Coherence is a long term notion in the literature of multiple testing. From FWER control multiple testing theory to confidence envelopes on the number of false positives, coherence is a desirable property for multiple testing procedures. However, we show in this article that coherence is not a sufficient property to ensure that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via an interpolation mechanism. We introduce a new no- tion, the notion of strong coherence, which is a stronger property than coherence and ensures that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via the interpolation mech- anisms considered in the literature. Finally, we provide a uniform improvement of the confidence envelope from Durand et al. (2020) that is computable in polynomial time and demonstrate the improvement on simulated data.

papers.title: An Unbounded Gap Between Identification and Identifiable Elicitation: Central Moments
papers.abstract: For $n\geq2$, two expectation equations identify the mean together with the $n$th central moment. How many coordinates must a report have if a one-observation loss uniquely elicits it and the report determines that moment? We prove that $n$ coordinates are necessary and sufficient among all identifiable intermediaries. The result holds on every open convex set of positive distributions on any $n+1$ distinct real outcomes. It requires no regularity of the loss, report map, identification function, or link. Thus $\operatorname{elic}_{\mathcal I}(μ_n)=n$ while $\operatorname{iden}(μ_n)\leq2$, giving an unbounded gap between identifiable elicitation and indirect identification. This resolves the central-moment conjecture of Frongillo and Kash on the stated domains. The proof constructs a $C^1$ manifold of supporting coefficients from the affine fibers of a convex negative Bayes risk. Translations along that manifold force an $n$-dimensional tangent space. Standardized moments of order at least three have the same exact complexity. The bound also extends to convex distribution classes with a full-dimensional raw-moment image.

papers.title: Computing Fréchet Means on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fréchet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fréchet means for data supported on an unknown compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M_{1}$ embedded in an ambient metric space $(X,d_{\operatorname{obs}})$. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on $M_{1}$ and the observation metric $d_{\operatorname{obs}}$, without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an $O(1/T)$ expected objective gap guarantee using at most $\widetilde{O}(T^{4d+3})$ sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.

papers.title: The Schubert bialgebra
papers.abstract: We introduce a Schubert bialgebra $\mathcal{A}=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, in which polynomials in different numbers of variables multiply to zero and the coproduct splits the variables into two consecutive blocks, and study its graded dual $\mathcal{D}$, whose product is concatenation of weak compositions. The Schubert polynomials $\mathfrak{S}_u^n$ form a basis of $\mathcal{A}$; we give an explicit formula for the dual Schubert basis $Ξ_u^n$ of $\mathcal{D}$ via a transition formula to an elementary symmetric basis, and show that the Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^w$ are the coefficients of the coproduct of $\mathcal{D}$ in the dual Schubert basis. The product of $\mathcal{D}$ is then lifted to an associative product $\sqcup$ on the free abelian group $\mathcal{BRC}$ of bounded RC graphs, built from a transition map $\mathcal{Z}$ on RC graphs that realizes the Lascoux-Schützenberger transition formula and generalizes Little's bumping algorithm. Quotienting $\mathcal{BRC}$ by ideals coming from Demazure crystal equivalence, Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence, and quasi-Yamanouchi equivalence yields manifestly positive Littlewood-Richardson rules for the dual Schubert, dual key, dual forest, and dual slide bases of $\mathcal{D}$. Read on $\mathcal{A}$, these are branching rules: enumerative formulas for splitting a Schubert, key, forest, or slide polynomial across two blocks of variables, and in the Schubert case they compute the Levi branching coefficients of Ressayre-Richmond for $\mathrm{GL}_p\times\mathrm{GL}_q\hookrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{p+q}$.

papers.title: Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined by Stable Bundles on Curves of Genus 2
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$. This paper also discusses the generalization of these strategies to higher genus and gives a computation when $E$ is not stable and may be written as a direct sum of line bundles.

papers.title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
papers.abstract: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.

papers.title: Embedding theorems for Herz-Type Sobolev spaces on domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we further investigate the properties of Herz-type Sobolev spaces on domains, which unify and generalize the classical Sobolev spaces. In particular, we establish several Sobolev-type embedding theorems for these spaces. Moreover, by means of a suitable example, we show that some of the assumptions imposed on the parameters are optimal.

papers.title: Deterministic Bounds on Accuracy and Stability of Metric-Space Regression and Classification
papers.abstract: Data-driven approaches often face ambiguity in datasets due to sensor or target noise, insufficient information, and noise in the input data. While best-fit machine learning methods can accommodate such noise through uncertainty estimates, they are prone to overfitting and it is challenging to quantify ambiguity of the relation between inputs and targets. We introduce a geometric framework that quantifies this ambiguity through the average kernel size, computed with data-dependent, i.e. model-independent, feasible sets derived from worst-case input and target noise. The framework provides computable, deterministic, non-asymptotic bounds on the best achievable empirical error and accuracy for a finite, constructed dataset, independent of the predictive model class, and applies to regression and classification with pseudo-metric input spaces and metric target spaces. The ambiguity of the input-target relation implies three consequences: an empirical error floor, an accuracy-stability trade-off, and, under standard probabilistic assumptions, a strictly positive distribution-training error gap when training below the accuracy bounds. Under standard Borel assumptions for Euclidean norms, the distributional analogue of the average kernel size is related to Bayes risk as it reduces to the optimal distribution root-mean-squared error times the square root of two. Experiments spanning tabular regression, image regression and classification datasets yield nontrivial bounds on the best achievable empirical error and accuracy on a constructed dataset, alongside descriptive comparisons with model performance on the original datasets. The bounds provide a computable, model-independent reference scale on the constructed dataset and comparisons with model performance on the original dataset are descriptive.

papers.title: Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of all planar graphs
papers.abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours. Fabrici, Lužar, Rindošová and Soták conjectured that three colours always suffice. We disprove this conjecture. We give a simple gadget construction that turns every planar graph of chromatic number four into a planar graph with no such colouring with three colours. This also shows that it is NP-complete to decide whether three colours suffice for a planar graph. We also give a planar graph on $25$ vertices that needs four colours. Further, we give critical planar graphs on $25$ vertices with $52$ and with $51$ edges, an infinite family of plane triangulations that need four colours, and an infinite family of critical examples.

papers.title: Geometric rigidity principles for $\mathscr{A}$-free Young measures
papers.abstract: We study generalized Young measures generated by $\mathscr{A}$-free measures, $\mathscr{A}$ a constant-rank operator, in a compactification of the value space adapted to an energy. Given an $\mathscr{A}$-quasiconvex integrand $G$ of linear growth with coercive recession function $G^\infty$, the unit sphere at infinity is replaced by the indicatrix $\mathbb{S}_G=\{G^\infty=1\}$, which need be neither convex nor symmetric. The two compactifications are equivalent, but in the adapted one the equality cases of the Jensen inequalities characterizing $\mathscr{A}$-free Young measures become statements of convex geometry about $\mathbb{S}_G$. We prove the characterization in this setting, with a new streamlined proof of the inhomogenization step based on a dyadic martingale argument. We then show that if $\mathscr{A}$-free measures $μ_j\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}μ$ and their $G$-energies converge, then at $|μ^s|$-almost every point the concentration-angle measure is supported on the smallest exposed face of $\overline{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbb{S}_G)$ containing the $G$-polar of $μ^s$; in particular, it never charges the set where $G^\infty$ differs from its convex envelope, which, by the automatic convexity of Kirchheim and Kristensen, does not meet the wave cone. The concentration on the singular part of $μ$ is elementary for every such sequence if and only if each point of the wave cone on $\mathbb{S}_G$ is an extreme point of $\overline{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbb{S}_G)$, as for the Euclidean norm underlying Reshetnyak's continuity theorem; on flat faces of $\mathbb{S}_G$, rigidity degrades from a point to a face. Finally, we prove a transfer principle for the convergence of energies of $\mathrm{BV}$ maps under Dirichlet boundary conditions.

papers.title: The transition between order to disorder in the Seppäläinen-Johansson model
papers.abstract: We study the Seppäläinen-Johansson model of first-passage percolation along a region of the plane where it moves from an ordered to a disordered phase, represented by a 2nd order discontinuity in its limit shape function. The fluctuations in this transition region are of order one, and we determine that certain limiting statistics are described by Fredholm determinants and are closely related to the largest eigenvalue of the GUE.

papers.title: Hausdorff Matrices on the BMOA and Bloch spaces
papers.abstract: We determine the spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum of Hausdorff operators $\mathcal{H}_μ$ on BMOA and the Bloch space $\mathscr{B}$, for suitable finite positive Borel measures $μ$ on $(0,1]$.

papers.title: Local Projected Controllability of Nonlocal Continuity Equations
papers.abstract: We formulate and study the problem of local projected controllability (LPC) for characteristic solutions of controlled nonlocal continuity (transport) equations on the space of probability measures over a separable Banach space. The task is motivated in particular by self-interacting models in machine learning, whose action can be represented as controlled dynamics of the probability distribution over input data, while the actual output is given by a finite-dimensional vector of features extracted from the terminal distribution by a possibly nonlinear observation map. Given a fixed finite family of velocity fields which may depend on the transported measure, we ask whether the reachable values of the observable vector fill a neighborhood of its reference value. Our approach is to lift the transport equation in the space of measures to an ordinary differential equation on a Banach space of maps. This representation makes it possible to employ the machinery of Lie brackets developed for Banach manifolds, while the resulting sufficient condition for LPC can be formulated directly on the space of measures.

papers.title: A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.

papers.title: An improved randomized algorithm for finding sinks of Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations of the binary hypercube
papers.abstract: Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations (AUSOs) of the binary hypercube form an elegant abstraction of various optimization problems, ranging from linear programs whose feasibility region is a combinatorial hypercube, to 2-player turn-based stochastic games (2TBSGs) in which one of the players has two actions from each one of its states. The currently fastest known randomized algorithm for finding the sink of such AUSOs is the Random-Facet algorithm of Kalai (STOC 1992), and of Matoušek, Sharir and Welzl (SoCG 1992), adapted to the binary hypercube by Gärtner (RSA 2002). The expected number of vertex queries made by the algorithm is at most $e^{2\sqrt{n}}$, where $n$ is the dimension of the cube. We design an improved randomized sink-finding algorithm that performs an expected number of only $e^{\sqrt{(2+o(1))n}}$ queries. This is the first improved bound for the problem in over two decades. The improved algorithm is obtained by adapting improved versions of the Random-Facet algorithm for solving general linear programs, and LP-type problems, developed by Kalai (STOC 1992), Gärtner (FOCS 1992), and by Hansen and Zwick (STOC 2015). The improved bound is not implied by these much more general algorithms. A key feature of the improved algorithm and its analysis is its simplicity. The structure of binary AUSOs enables a simpler description and a much simpler analysis of the adapted algorithm. In particular, the recurrence relations bounding the complexity of the algorithm depend on only one variable, and not two, and they can be solved using fairly straightforward techniques.

papers.title: Hardy-Sobolev-Maz'ya inequalities for $\boldsymbol{1<p<2}$
papers.abstract: We establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$ for singularities supported on affine subspaces and for arbitrary domains. We first prove a Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality for singularities supported on affine subspaces of arbitrary codimension $1\leq k<N$, showing that the deficit in the sharp Hardy inequality controls a suitable weighted Sobolev norm. Combining the same convexity estimate with the one-dimensional approach of Frank and Loss in [9], we also establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on arbitrary domains with the mean distance to the boundary and thereby solve a problem posed in [9]. These results complete the previously unresolved subquadratic range $1<p<2$ and, together with the known results for $p\geq 2$, provide a unified Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya theory for all $1<p<N$ associated with plane singularities and general domains.

papers.title: Failure of direct finiteness for group algebras in every odd characteristic
papers.abstract: For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finitely presented group $G_p$ and elements $a,b,c\in\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$ such that $ab=1$, $ac=0$, and $c\ne0$. Thus $\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$, and the group algebra over every field of characteristic $p$, fails to be directly finite. The construction combines a single exceptional self-product pair with signed bipartite cancellation. New integer matching data realize the exceptional self-intersection while retaining a strict squared-word decay estimate. We verify the adaptations needed for the earlier bounded-path and planar-localization arguments. A minimal disk picture protects the identity coefficient of $c$, so the proof does not require torsion-freeness.

papers.title: Solvability of complex Hessian equations corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials
papers.abstract: On compact Hermitian manifolds, we establish a framework using radial normalization for the solvability of complex Hessian equation in form type, corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials whose coefficients may not be constant functions. The solvability of a radial normalized equation is characterized by the existence of a C-subsolution at radial slope, which extends the results of Guo-Song to this setting.

papers.title: A new proof of equality cases of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality on manifolds
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of equality cases of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality on manifolds, following the work of Balogh-Krisátly. Our proof extends also to equality cases of the strong Brunn-Minkowski inequality, introduced by Magnabosco-Portinale-Rossi.

papers.title: Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a Jüttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.

papers.title: Asymptotic dimension of graphs excluding an induced or fat minor
papers.abstract: Asymptotic dimension is a large-scale invariant of metric spaces that was introduced by Gromov (1993). A major open problem in coarse graph theory asks whether, for every fixed graph $H$, the class of graphs excluding $H$ as a fat minor has bounded asymptotic dimension. A weaker conjecture asserts the same conclusion for graphs excluding $H$ as an induced minor. We substantially expand the range of graphs $H$ for which these conjectures are known to hold. Specifically, we prove bounded asymptotic dimension for the following classes of graphs: graphs excluding a fixed planar graph as a fat minor; and graphs excluding a fixed string graph as an induced minor. All of our results also hold for the stronger notion of Assouad--Nagata dimension, a refinement of asymptotic dimension. These results have a number of applications, two of which we mention here. First they imply that an induced minor-closed class is $χ$-bounded if and only if it does not contain some Burling graph. Second they imply that, in graph classes excluding a fixed planar graph as an induced minor, treewidth is polynomial in maximum degree.

papers.title: Generating functions of hypermaps and m-constellations with two alternating boundaries
papers.abstract: We study the enumeration of planar hypermaps with several alternating boundaries. We first derive a peeling recursion with an arbitrary number of alternating boundaries and, in the two- boundary case, translate it into a functional equation for the corresponding generating function. Our main result is an explicit solution of this equation for m-constellations. In particular, we obtain a rational expression for the genus-zero two-point function, or cylinder generating function, with two alternating boundaries.

papers.title: Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings
papers.abstract: We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $κ$ for which they are $κ$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.

papers.title: Admissible solutions of the Euler equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the existence of an extensive class of initial data--characterized by intermittency dimension and roughness--for which the d-dimensional Euler equations (d \ge 2) admit a decreasing energy channel with infinitely many admissible solutions arising from the same initial data. This class includes initial data in C^{1-κ}(\mathbb{T}^d) and W^{1,p}(\mathbb{T}^d) for any 0 < κ< 1 and 2 < p < \infty, thereby demonstrating the sharpness of the Lions and Yudovich uniqueness principles. Our proof is based on a new backward convex integration scheme employing approximate Λ-Euler equations to reduce the initial error and on uncovering a quantitative relationship between regularity, energy, and intermittency.

papers.title: Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
papers.abstract: Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.

papers.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
papers.abstract: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.

papers.title: Uniform estimates for elliptic systems with critical Sobolev coefficients
papers.abstract: The $W^{1,p}$ estimate for uniformly elliptic operators of divergence form with VMO coefficients is classical. In particular, this provides $W^{1,p}$ estimates for elliptic operators with coefficients in $W^{1,n}$. However, this theory does not yield constants in the estimates controlled by the $W^{1,n}$ norm of the coefficients, since the total $W^{1,n}$ norm does not control the rate of decay for the mean oscillation. In this work, we establish uniform estimates for divergence-form elliptic systems whose coefficients lie in the critical Sobolev--Lorentz spaces $W^{1,(n,s)}$ with $1\le s<\infty$, have an $L^\infty$-bounded spatially symmetric part, and satisfy an integral ellipticity condition. The constant in the estimate is controlled by the corresponding norms of coefficients and the ellipticity constant.

papers.title: Integral and higher-genus quantum McKay correspondence in type D
papers.abstract: We establish Iritani's integral form of the $\mathbb{C}^\times$-equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture (CTC) for the minimal resolution of the surface singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$, where $\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$ is the binary dihedral group of order $4n$. We then use Givental's quantisation formalism to prove the all-genus full-descendent CTC in that case. As an application, we deduce the Bryan-Cadman-Young degree-zero form of the orbifold Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas correspondence for the Calabi-Yau 3-orbifold $[\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}] \times \mathbb{C}$.

papers.title: The rank problem for metric spaces
papers.abstract: We construct a complete, second countable metric space with uncountable Scott rank. This answers a well-known question posed by Fokina, Friedman, K{ö}rwien and Nies, and shows that the known upper bound $ω_1$ on the rank, proved by Doucha, is sharp. Further, a Baire category based variant of the rank of metric spaces is developed, and this is used to give new proofs of the known rank bounds based only on standard methods of descriptive set theory.

papers.title: On exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients
papers.abstract: Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|\leq1}$ be multiplicative, and suppose that $α$ has a rational approximation $a/q$ with $|α-a/q|\leq 1/(qx)$ and $q\leq x/((\log x)^2(\log\log x)^3)$. We prove that $\left|\sum_{n\leq x}f(n)e(nα)\right|\leq \left(\frac4{\sqrt6}+o(1)\right)\frac{x}{\sqrt q} +O\left(\frac{x}{\log x}\right)$, whereas complete multiplicativity improves $4/\sqrt6$ to $1$. Both constants are optimal. In particular, this confirms a folklore conjecture on exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients motivated by the work of Montgomery and Vaughan (1977). We also obtain logarithmically weighted estimates and give counterexamples to related conjectures.

papers.title: Polynomial Maximal Surfaces in H^{2,2} and Spherical Polygons
papers.abstract: We study the moduli space of complete maximal surfaces in pseudo-hyperbolic space $\mathbf{H}^{2,2}$ with polygonal asymptotic boundary a lightlike $(n+4)$-gon in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, up to the action of $\mathsf{SO}_0(2,3)$. Importantly, this space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ is disconnected for $n\geq 2$. We introduce a \emph{turning invariant} $Θ$ that classifies the components in terms of the geometry of the boundary polygons in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, which is related to \emph{spherical polygons} in $\mathbb{S}^2$. We provide a geometric parametrization of the moduli space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ via holomorphic data, namely a pair of polynomials $α$, $β$. These polynomials appear in relation to certain components of the complexified second fundamental form of the corresponding surface. We then relate the holomorphic data $α,β$ with the turning invariant $Θ$. This leads to characterizations of the \emph{Hitchin component} of polygonal maximal surfaces studied by Tamburelli-Wolf.

papers.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
papers.abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.

papers.title: Differential equations as difference-differential equations
papers.abstract: We analyze the behavior of systems of algebraic differential equations when considered as systems of difference-differential equations, with special emphasis on systems which define minimal sets relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCF}$ of differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ distinguished commuting derivations. We show that if $p$ is a minimal type relative to $\operatorname{DCF}$ defined by a system of algebraic partial differential equations and inequations and the forking geometry on $p$ is trivial (also called ``disintegrated''), then $p$ remains minimal when regarded as a partial type relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCFA}$ of difference-differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ commuting derivations in the sense that every completion has $\operatorname{SU}$-rank one. We illustrate this theorem by describing in detail the possible difference-differential equations consistent with differential equations of the form $y' = y^3 + a_2 y^2 + a_1 y + a_0$ where $a_0$, $a_1$, and $a_2$ are differential constants.

papers.title: $h$-cobordisms between $1$-connected manifolds with boundary
papers.abstract: We classify $h$-cobordisms between compact simply-connected $4$-manifolds with boundary in both the smooth and topological categories. This extends a result of Kreck, which proved the corresponding result for closed manifolds. As an application, we recover the injectivity portion of Orson-Powell's computation of the mapping class group for simply-connected topological $4$-manifolds with boundary.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Parallel $M$-Matrix Scaling
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of computing a positive diagonal scaling of a $d \times d$ symmetric $M$-matrix so that all row and column sums are $1$. We provide a poly-logarithmic iteration algorithm that solves this problem to high accuracy, where the cost of each iteration is dominated by the cost of solving a Laplacian system. This improves upon the recent $\tilde{O}(d^{1/3})$ iteration bound of [Vladu STOC 2025] and yields a randomized algorithm for the problem that runs in near-linear time and poly-logarithmic parallel depth.

papers.title: An Induced Subgraph Paradigm for Strongly Regular Graph Constructions
papers.abstract: How many disjoint copies of some graph $H$ can appear in an induced subgraph of a strongly regular graph? We give upper and lower bounds that depend on the number of vertices in their boundary. This generalizes a result of Lou-Murin which bounds the independence number of a (hitherto still elusive) strongly regular graph with parameters $(99,14,1,2)$. The equality cases suggest alternative structural approaches for potential constructions of such a graph. We show, using computer searches, that one cannot impose certain additional natural conditions for some of the cases.

papers.title: Automorphic Dirac Operators and an Analogue of the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator on $Γ\backslash \mathfrak{H}$
papers.abstract: In the 2010's Bombieri and Garrett showed that the discrete spectrum, if any, of a self-adjoint extension of a restriction of the hyperbolic Laplacian on the upper half plane is $s(s-1)$ where $ζ_{\mathbb{Q}(i)}(s) = 0$. However, they also showed that at most 94% of the zeros of zeta can participate in this spectrum. In an effort to obtain a larger discrete spectrum, Sands in 2020 characterized an automorphic Hamiltonian that is an analogue of the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator for the modular curve. The motivation for this is that the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator is a discretized version of the Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}$. In describing this operator, it is necessary to understand automorphic Dirac operators and the growth of the potential. Here, we explain several noteworthy features of automorphic Dirac operators, prove that Sands' Hamiltonian has a purely discrete spectrum using an explicit presentation of Kronecker's limit formula, and use the operator to give a characterization of an automorphic Schwartz space.

papers.title: Extending Donaldson's HyperKähler Structure via Minimal Surfaces into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$
papers.abstract: We construct a deformation space for minimal immersions into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ with its holomorphic Killing form, and define an explicit, mapping class group invariant, complex hyperKähler structure on such deformation space. Such complex hyperKähler structure restricts to: Donaldson's hyperKähler structure on a totally real copy of almost-Fuchsian space, Mazzoli-Seppi-Tamburelli's para-hyperKähler structure on a totally real copy of maximally globally hyperbolic $\mathbb{A}\mathrm{d}\mathbb{S}^3$ manifolds, and Loustau-Sanders' complex bi-Kähler structure on a holomorphic copy of quasi-Fuchsian space. Moreover, all these loci are totally geodesic. We discuss other geometric aspects of this space, such as the Hamiltonian property of a natural $\mathbb{C}^*$-action, involving the Goldman symplectic form and a complex-valued area functional.

papers.title: Causal Fingerprints Reveal Hidden Mechanisms in Partially-Observed Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: In partially-observed dynamical systems, distinct hidden mechanisms can produce similar observable summary statistics while explaining individual events differently. We introduce causal fingerprints: realization-dependent patterns that track how information about a hidden state is revealed through subsequent evolution. Within a prescribed dynamical model, we compare the filtering posterior, based on observations up to a given time, with the smoothing posterior, obtained after adding an expanding window of future observations. We quantify this retrospective information gain using Kullback-Leibler divergence and track its evolution as the future window of observational data expands. The fingerprint reveals both the strength and temporal reach of hidden influence, which can vary across events and their stages. Because the observed trajectory is held fixed while hidden-state inference depends on the candidate model, fingerprints reveal how competing dynamical mechanisms explain the same observations even when selected statistics agree. In linear Gaussian systems, we derive a characteristic fingerprint timescale for the temporal reach of hidden influence. Calibrated surrogates matching the observable mean, variance, and decorrelation time can still produce distinct fingerprints when feedback memory, hidden-noise memory, or hidden forcing timescales are misrepresented. Nonlinear examples reveal mechanism-dependent signatures for extreme bursts, oscillatory variability, and regime switching, including multiplicative instability versus additive forcing, deterministic nonlinear feedback versus state-dependent multiplicative noise, and intrinsic bistability versus hidden double-well forcing. Causal fingerprints therefore provide a time- and event-resolved diagnostic for asking not only whether a model reproduces observed statistics, but how its hidden dynamics explain individual events.

papers.title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
papers.abstract: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory to include a temperature dimension. This gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. The framework formally unifies information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation (TAO-)DFT as special cases, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set derived from biphenyl. The results help to clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture near hyperbolic metrics
papers.abstract: We give an LLM-assisted construction of counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture, with real analytic metrics arbitrarily close to a hyperbolic metric in dimension three. For acyclic unitary line characters tending to the trivial character, the modulus of the Ruelle zeta function at zero divided by analytic torsion squared tends to zero.

papers.title: Tensor-generating line bundles on toric varieties
papers.abstract: A line bundle is $\otimes$-generating if its powers generate the derived category of perfect complexes. Refining the derived Nakai--Moishezon criterion of Ito--Olander, we characterize $\otimes$-generating line bundles on proper toric varieties by a combinatorial criterion on the fan, leading to the notion of $\otimes$-generating fans characterizing $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Furthermore, we prove an analogue of Kleiman's criterion of ampleness for $\otimes$-generation. As applications, we provide several examples including: (i) smooth proper fourfolds with no $\otimes$-generating line bundle, by showing that products of two or more positive-dimensional proper toric varieties admit a $\otimes$-generating line bundle only when they are projective, (ii) families of smooth non-projective proper threefolds with $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Finally, we study subvarieties obstructing $\otimes$-generation of canonical bundles and implications to autoequivalences of derived categories.

papers.title: Uniform Intersection Numbers and Subgroup-Based Generating Graphs of Groups
papers.abstract: The uniform intersection number of a finite group $G$, denoted by $ui(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that the intersection of any $k$ distinct maximal subgroups of $G$ is equal to its Frattini subgroup. We determine the uniform intersection number of dicyclic, dihedral, and quasi-dihedral groups. We then investigate the uniform intersection number through the subgroup-based generating graph $\mathcal{G}(G)$ of a finite group $G$. We characterize the finite groups $G$ for which both the intersection number and the uniform intersection number are equal to two, and show that this condition is equivalent to $\mathcal{G}(G)$ being complete multipartite. We also classify finite groups in terms of the diameter, girth, and perfectness of $\mathcal{G}(G)$. Finally, we show that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ is Hamiltonian if and only if $n=p_1^{r}p_2^{r}$, where $r\geq 2$ and $p_1$ and $p_2$ are distinct primes.

papers.title: Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a discrete-time pull-based remote estimation system involving an information source and a remote monitor where the information source is a finite-state irreducible discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) process. In this system, the remote monitor sends a pull request towards the source which responds by sampling its process so as to transmit the sampled values towards the monitor through a delay channel, encapsulated in information packets. We consider i) zero delay (ZD) and ii) unit delay (UD) channels, where the packet transmission times are zero and one slot, respectively. For remote estimation, we use the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator, and for quantifying its performance, we use the mean age of incorrect information (MAoII) which is a recently proposed freshness and mismatch metric that penalizes an incorrect estimation along with its duration. Our goal is to obtain pull policies so as to minimize MAoII under a long-run sampling rate constraint. For the ZD model, we propose a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) formulation of the problem, which allows us to find the optimum observation-dependent pull policy. On the other hand, the UD channel prevents the monitor from possessing perfect information on the actual AoII process at any given time, and the SMDP formulation of the ZD channel cannot readily be used for the UD model. For the system with the UD channel, we first provide a numerical algorithm to calculate the MAoII and the average sampling rate for a given observation-dependent pull policy. For the optimization of the underlying remote estimation system, we use the joint distribution of the age and source processes to be obtained from the history of all observations, termed as belief. Subsequently, we propose a belief-dependent policy obtained via the belief-MDP formulation and a constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) algorithm.

papers.title: Real-Arithmetic Sketched Eigensolvers for Symmetric Matrices
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop sketched variants of subspace iteration and TraceMIN, called sSI and sTraceMIN, for real symmetric eigenvalue problems by combining basis whitening with the sketched Rayleigh-Ritz (sRR) procedure. The nonsymmetric projected matrix in sRR may have nonreal eigenpairs, leading to complex arithmetic and additional computational costs. We overcome this difficulty using a real Schur formulation of sRR that keeps the iterations in real arithmetic. We further develop procedures for characteristic subspace selection and convergence monitoring within this formulation. On the theoretical side, we discuss suitable subspace embedding assumptions for sketched eigensolvers that use a fixed sketching matrix throughout the iterations. Under a mild embedding assumption, we establish local convergence results for sSI and sTraceMIN. Numerical experiments demonstrate runtime savings of up to 39% for sSI and 21% for sTraceMIN relative to their standard counterparts on the test problems.

papers.title: Global well-posedness of the periodic Majda-Biello systems in the resonant case
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the following Majda-Biello system in the resonant case $α\in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$ on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}$. \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} u_{t} + u_{xxx} & = & - v v_x, v_{t} + αv_{xxx} & = & - (uv)_{x}, (u,v)|_{t=0} & = & (u_0,v_0), \end{array} \right. \quad x \in \mathbb{T}, \, t \in \mathbb{R}. \] Here, the initial data $u_0$ and $v_0$ live in the Sobolev space $H^{s}(\mathbb{T})$ and $u_0$ has zero mean over $\mathbb{T}$. We establish the optimal global well-posedness for the above system when $s\geq \min\{1, s_α+\}$, where $s_α$ is a constant depending only on $α$, and $s_α= \frac12$ for almost every $α\in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$. These indices match the sharp ones in the local theory obtained by Oh (Int. Math. Res. Not., 18:3516-3556, 2009). The main novelty of our proof is to introduce a third modified energy in the I-method by performing a partial correction to the second modified energy around the resonant region. This partial correction avoids the singularity in the full correction, and therefore makes it possible to pointwise bound the quintilinear multipliers arising in the time derivative of the third modified energy. Another feature in our proof is the combination of the Diophantine approximation theory with the sparsity of nearly resonant frequency pairs on the periodic lattice to obtain the key quadrilinear and quintilinear estimates, leading to an almost conservation law sufficient for the global iteration.

papers.title: The ReLU Matrix Decomposition: NP-Hardness, Ill-Posedness, and ReLU-Rank
papers.abstract: The ReLU Matrix Decomposition (RMD) approximates a sparse, nonnegative m-by-n matrix X by max(0, WH), where W is an m-by-r matrix, H is an r-by-n matrix, and r is the rank of the decomposition. The most common formulation, referred to as Fro-RMD, minimizes the Frobenius norm of X - max(0, WH) over W and H. We prove that Fro-RMD is NP-hard, even for binary matrices and r = 1; to the best of our knowledge, this is the first complexity result for RMD. We also show that Fro-RMD is ill-posed, in the sense that its infimum may not be attained. We then turn to exact RMD, that is, X = max(0, WH), and define the ReLU-rank of X as the smallest r for which such a decomposition exists. We interpret exact RMDs geometrically as configurations of points and hyperplanes in an r-dimensional space, associated with the rows of W and the columns of H, respectively. Building on this interpretation, we derive upper bounds on the ReLU-rank of diagonal, block-diagonal, and block-sparse matrices and, under an additional structural assumption, improve the best known bound for block-diagonal matrices. Finally, we propose two formulations of exact RMD as feasibility problems: a nonconvex quadratically constrained program, which can be tackled by global solvers such as Gurobi, and a formulation based on the latent model of Saul, (``A nonlinear matrix decomposition for mining the zeros of sparse data', SIMODS, 2022), which we tackle using alternating projections for which we establish local convergence together with asymptotic convergence rates. We compare these two approaches on some numerical examples.

papers.title: Deterministic Determination of Axial Constants, Sectional Regularities and Annihilator Numbers
papers.abstract: Axial constants and sectional regularities are recently introduced invariants of homogeneous polynomial ideals that, like the already earlier introduced annihilator numbers, depend on generic choices of coordinates. We provide effective characterisations of the genericity underlying these invariants in terms of $β$-maximal position and strong stability. In particular, we show that $β$-maximal position suffices for determining generic annihilator numbers and sectional regularities, while its combination with strong stability yields corresponding results for axial constants. We also develop deterministic linear algebra procedures for detecting the required generic positions and for computing these invariants.

papers.title: Evolution algebras: a survey of results and a list of open problems
papers.abstract: Evolution algebras, introduced by J. P. Tian as an algebraic model of non- Mendelian inheritance, are commutative algebras with a basis whose distinct elements multiply to zero. The first part of the paper surveys the theory: low-dimensional classifica- tions, structure theory, nilpotency, automorphisms and derivations, directed graphs and random walks, infinite-dimensional and dynamical aspects, and embedding theorems. The second part is a unified list of fifty open questions and eleven new conjectures, each accompanied by the available evidence; two of the conjectures and one of the questions are settled here. We also prove several new observations, most of them formally verified in the proof assistant Lean (see Section 2.1.11): every finite group is the automorphism group of a simple evolution algebra over every field, and | Aut(A)|/ dim A takes every positive ratio- nal value on simple evolution algebras over every field; infinitude of the automorphism group of nilpotent algebras, the possible numbers of idempotents of real perfect evolution algebras, a Galois-theoretic criterion for the existence of idempotents in dimension two, the average number of idempotents over finite fields, and a perfect evolution algebra whose automorphism group is a non-split extension.

papers.title: An infinite completely normal basis theorem
papers.abstract: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem; the case of finite base fields was previously established in an equivalent form by Hachenberger.

papers.title: Geometric Graph Representations via Compact SAT Encodings
papers.abstract: We present compact SAT encodings and certifying exact solvers for boxicity and cubicity. The boxicity of a graph is the minimum dimension in which it is the intersection graph of axis-aligned boxes; cubicity is defined analogously using unit cubes. Grid-based formulations face a geometric discretization bottleneck, growing rapidly with the target dimension. We avoid this bottleneck by encoding the total order of interval endpoints in each coordinate. For an $n$-vertex graph and target dimension $d$, our boxicity encoding uses $O(n^2d)$ variables and $O(n^3d)$ clauses, both linear in $d$. Requiring the left- and right-endpoint orders to agree yields a cubicity encoding of the same asymptotic size. Satisfying models are decoded into independently checked geometric representations, while unsatisfiable instances used as lower-bound evidence carry mechanically verified DRAT certificates. In a controlled evaluation with 186 trials per encoding on standard and structured graph families, the order encoding solves 96.8% of trials, compared with 71.0% for the known grid formulation, and reduces mean PAR-2 time from 178.21 to 21.70 seconds. The pipeline also certifies exact values for several named graphs. We turn one such value into a reusable obstruction by proving that every Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ with $k\ge3$ and $n\ge2k+1$ contains an induced Desargues graph. The resulting lower bound, together with an explicit three-dimensional representation of $K(7,3)$, establishes $\operatorname{boxicity}(K(7,3))=3$. This disproves the conjecture of Caoduro and Sebo that $\operatorname{boxicity}(K(n,k))=n-k$ for all $k\ge3$ and $n\ge2k+1$.

papers.title: Transient Heat Conduction on Quantum Hardware: Replicated Temperature-Field Reconstruction and Shot-Count Sensitivity with a Variational Quantum Linear Solver
papers.abstract: Implicit discretizations of transient heat conduction repeatedly generate sparse linear systems, making diffusion problems a natural test bed for quantum linear solvers. This study evaluates how accurately a variational quantum linear solver (VQLS) recovers the temperature field produced by one backward-Euler step of one-dimensional conduction on IBM quantum hardware. A pre-specified confirmatory experiment compares N=4 interior temperatures encoded on two qubits with N=8 temperatures encoded on three qubits using ten paired hardware blocks; a separately defined N=16, four-qubit extension is evaluated in five independently scheduled exploratory blocks. Local VQLS optimization reduces relative temperature-field error to approximately 10^{-8} for all three cases, establishing an essentially exact ideal reference at this scale. On hardware, mean relative L2 temperature-field error is 8.07% for N=4 and 20.14% for N=8, a paired increase of 12.06 percentage points (95% CI, 10.71-13.42; exact paired sign-flip p=0.001953). The exploratory N=16 mean is 24.75+/-1.84%. A pre-specified N=16 shot-count follow-up then evaluates the same locked circuit at 2,048, 8,192, and 32,768 shots in six independently scheduled blocks. Mean field error remains 23.64%, 24.57%, and 24.37%, respectively; the 32,768-minus-2,048-shot contrast is +0.74 percentage points (95% CI, -0.65 to 2.12; p=0.281). In contrast, ideal multinomial sampling predicts a reduction from 2.68% to 0.75%. Higher shot counts reduce block-to-block variability but do not recover the mean cold-side temperature field. The results show that full-field readout of a strongly nonuniform thermal state is limited by more than ordinary finite-shot sampling under the tested hardware conditions, motivating observable-focused quantum formulations for heat flux, stored energy, and selected temperatures.

papers.title: Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) accelerate generation by unmasking multiple tokens in parallel, but sampling these tokens independently ignores their correlations and biases the output. Anari et al. (2026) corrected this bias with rejection sampling, decomposing the log acceptance probability into a sum of token-level terms, but the evaluation requires one score query per unmasked token. We propose the Single-Increment Rejection Sampler (SIRS), which provides an estimate of the log acceptance probability from a single randomly sampled increment at the cost of one query. SIRS then converts a Poisson number of clipped estimates into accept/reject decisions through a Bernoulli factory adapted from Chen et al. (2026). Since each query returns the conditionals of all remaining tokens in the block, we further Rao-Blackwellize each increment by averaging over these tokens at no extra cost, thereby reducing clipping.
